## Algorithms

### Stable Z sort

Renderables are sorted by a composite key:

```csharp
public static readonly Func<IRenderable, int> RenderableZPositionComparisonKey =
    r => r.Pos.Y + r.Pos.Z + r.ZOffset;
```

The Y coordinate, Z height, and explicit Z offset are combined so that sprites lower on the screen are drawn later. Because the sort key can be identical for many renderables (for example, units standing on the same cell), the original index `i` is packed into the low 32 bits of the sort key. This makes the sort stable, which is critical: an unstable sort would cause sprites with equal Z to swap order every frame, producing visible flicker. The sort uses `CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan` and `keys.Sort` to sort both the keys and the renderables in place without extra allocations.

### On-screen actor culling

`World.ScreenMap` partitions actors spatially. `RenderableActorsInBox` returns only actors whose bounds intersect the viewport. This is much faster than iterating over every actor in the world. The culling is conservative: an actor whose bounding box touches the viewport is rendered even if its actual sprite is not visible, so render traits must still clip their own output if necessary.

### Overlay grouping

Overlay renderables are grouped by type to maintain historical draw behavior:

```csharp
var groupedOverlayRenderables = preparedOverlayRenderables.GroupBy(prs => prs.GetType());
foreach (var g in groupedOverlayRenderables)
    foreach (var r in g)
        r.Render(this);
```

Grouping by `GetType()` means all health bars of one type are drawn together, then all selection brackets of another type, and so on. This preserves the original draw order from before the overlay renderables were batched and prepared. Without grouping, interleaving different overlay types could cause one type to draw on top of another in an inconsistent order depending on the spatial sort of the underlying actors.

### Palette refresh

Each frame, palette modifiers are applied:

```csharp
public void RefreshPalette()
{
    palette.ApplyModifiers(World.WorldActor.TraitsImplementing<IPaletteModifier>());
    Game.Renderer.SetPalette(palette);
}
```

This allows effects such as flashing, color cycling, or faction tinting to update the GPU palette without changing sprite data. `ApplyModifiers` modifies the `MutablePalette` copies, uploads the result, and then resets the mutable palettes back to their originals so that each frame starts from a known baseline.

### Renderable collection

`GenerateRenderables` pulls renderables from five sources:

1. On-screen actors (`actor.Render(this)`).
2. The world actor (`World.WorldActor.Render(this)`), which holds world-level render traits.
3. The render player's player actor, if any.
4. The current order generator (`World.OrderGenerator.Render(this, World)`), used for cursors, target lines, and preview sprites.
5. Effects, both unpartitioned and partitioned.

`GenerateOverlayRenderables` and `GenerateAnnotationRenderables` use `World.ApplyToActorsWithTrait<T>` to iterate all actors with the relevant interface, then additionally process selected actors (for the `WhenSelected` variants) and effects that implement the matching effect interface. This three-stage collection keeps the main actor layer sorted by Z while letting overlays and annotations bypass the Z-sort.

### Depth buffer usage
![Extension points diagram](images/Part_04_Chapter_02_WorldRenderer-extension-hook-diagram-showing-the-interface-s-to-implement-b4a27b.svg)


When `MapGrid.EnableDepthBuffer` is true, the depth buffer is enabled during the terrain and actor phases. The depth value for each sprite is derived from its world position and any per-pixel depth offset provided by a secondary `SpriteWithSecondaryData`. The depth buffer is cleared twice during `Draw`: once after the actor layer (so above-world effects do not depth-fight with actors) and once after the above-world layer (so the shroud and overlays are not depth-tested). It is disabled before overlays are drawn because UI indicators should always be visible regardless of world depth.

## Extension Points

### Add a custom renderable trait

Implement `IRenderable` on an actor trait. The `Render` method returns one or more `IRenderable` objects. Implement `PrepareRender` to convert them to `IFinalizedRenderable` for the GPU. Most traits do not implement `IRenderable` directly; instead they return one of the built-in renderable types such as `SpriteRenderable`.

### Draw above shroud

Implement `IRenderAboveShroud` to draw after the shroud layer. This is useful for selection indicators, range circles, and target lines. Use `IRenderAboveShroudWhenSelected` if the overlay should only appear when the actor is selected.

### Draw annotations

Implement `IRenderAnnotations` to draw text or debug graphics. Annotations are drawn with anti-aliasing enabled. Use `IRenderAnnotationsWhenSelected` for selection-only annotations.

### Add a post-processing pass

Implement `IRenderPostProcessPass` and add it as a world trait. The pass can render a full-screen effect using the framebuffer. Choose the `PostProcessPassType` carefully: `AfterWorld` is the most common for full-screen tinting, while `AfterAnnotations` is useful for effects that must include the UI overlays.

### Custom terrain renderer
![Common pitfalls  guardrails diagram](images/Part_04_Chapter_02_WorldRenderer-checklist-infographic-style-diagram-summarizing-the-top-pitf-fb069e.svg)


Implement `IRenderTerrain` on a world trait to replace the default tile rendering. The default implementation uses `TerrainSpriteLayer` and `TerrainRenderer`.

### Custom sprite sequence loader

If a mod needs tileset-specific artwork, derive from `DefaultSpriteSequenceLoader` and a `ClassicSpriteSequence` subclass, as `CameoSpriteSequence` does. Register the loader in `mod.yaml` with `SpriteSequenceFormat: <YourLoaderName>`, and implement `ReserveSprites`/`ResolveSprites` to load the correct sprites per tileset.

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **Render thread only:** all rendering code must run on the main thread. Do not create renderables from background threads.
- **Disposal:** `WorldRenderer` is disposable. It must be cleaned up when the world is destroyed; it also disposes the `World` it owns.
- **Palette invalidation:** if you add palettes after initialization, raise `PaletteInvalidated` so that sequences can re-resolve their palette references.
- **Renderable lifetime:** `IRenderable` objects are created each frame. Do not cache them between frames unless they are independent of world state.
- **Sorting cost:** very large numbers of renderables increase sort cost. Use spatial partitioning to keep the count low.
- **Depth buffer:** enabling the depth buffer changes the draw order semantics. Isometric mods need it; top-down mods typically do not. Do not rely on depth sorting for overlays, because the depth buffer is cleared before the overlay layer.
- **Overlay grouping:** if you add a new overlay type, be aware that `GroupBy(prs => prs.GetType())` will draw all instances of your type together. If your overlay depends on being drawn relative to another type, you may need to coordinate the order or choose a different render interface.
- **PrepareRender before Draw:** `Draw` expects `PrepareRenderables` to have been called first. Calling `Draw` without preparation will result in empty render lists.
- **Scissor and annotations:** annotations are drawn outside `WorldRenderer.Draw`, after the scissor has been disabled. If your annotation needs world clipping, compute the clip rectangle yourself from `Viewport.GetScissorBounds`.
- **World vs UI rendering:** `Widget` subclasses such as `CommanderTreeWidget` and `IngamePromotionCounterWidget` are not part of the `WorldRenderer` pipeline. If your feature needs to obey world depth, fog, or Z sort, do not implement it as a widget.
- **Fog synchronization:** `TintedCellsLayer` keeps separate `tiles` and `renderedTiles` dictionaries. The render-visible copy must only be updated in `ITickRender`, not in `ITick.Tick`, to avoid leaking simulation state through fog.
- **Tileset overrides:** when adding `TilesetFilenames` or `TilesetFilenamesPattern`, ensure the override sequence still has the same number of frames as the base sequence, or the `ResolveSprites` indexing will be off.

This chapter explains how `WorldRenderer` turns the simulation world into a rendered frame, and how the Cameo mod extends that pipeline.

After reading this chapter, you should be able to:

- Trace the layered render pipeline from terrain through actors/effects, above-world, post-processing, shroud, overlays, annotations, and final post-processing.
- Choose the correct renderable interface (`IRenderable`, `IRenderAboveShroud`, `IRenderAnnotations`, etc.) for a trait.
- Explain why `PrepareRenderables` is split from `Draw` and why stable Z-sort matters.
- Configure depth buffer and post-processing passes in YAML.
- Implement a custom renderable trait using `IRenderAnnotationsWhenSelected` or a similar interface.
- Identify Cameo-specific additions such as `TintedCellsLayer`, `CameoSpriteSequence`, the promotion/quota UI widgets, and the custom annotation traits in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` and `OpenRA.Mods.CA`.

If any of the concepts above feel unclear, review the relevant section before continuing. For source files and further reading, see the References section.

# Chapter 4.3 — Widgets and Chrome (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_04_Chapter_03_Widgets}

## Purpose
![Mental model diagram](images/Part_04_Chapter_03_Widgets-learning-objectives-summary-diagram-or-concept-map-showing-h-fe332a.svg)


OpenRA's user interface is built on a custom [widget](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) system. Menus, HUDs, tooltips, and editors are all declared in YAML "[chrome](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)" files and driven by C# logic classes. This chapter explains the widget hierarchy, the `WidgetLoader`, the base widget lifecycle, event propagation, and how chrome interacts with the game world, with a focus on the Cameo mod's custom UI widgets and logic.

The Cameo mod adds several custom widgets and logic classes for its unique mechanics: custom formations command bar, commander/promotion tree, production quota palette, auto control groups, and Cameo-specific HUD overlays. These all live in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/` and are registered through the same YAML chrome system as upstream widgets.

## Mental Model

Think of the widget tree as a set of nested picture frames on a glass table.

- **The window** is the outermost frame (`Ui.Root`). Inside it are the menu frames (`MenuRootWidget`) and the in-game frames (`WorldRootWidget`).
- **Every widget** is a smaller frame placed inside its parent. It has its own painting (`Draw`), heartbeat (`Tick`), and touch sensor (`HandleInput`).
- **Layout expressions** (`X`, `Y`, `Width`, `Height`) are the ruler and compass the engine uses to place each frame at load time.
- **Events** are like drops of water falling from above. The topmost frame under the drop gets the first chance to catch them; if it catches the drop, the water stops. If it lets the drop pass, the water drips through to the next frame below.
- **Focus** is the same as holding a frame steady so it continues to catch drops even when the mouse moves away. `MouseFocusWidget` keeps drag events on a widget, and `KeyboardFocusWidget` keeps typed text on a text field.
- **Logic classes** (`ChromeLogic`) are the backstage crew. They are attached to a frame and update its state, but they are not the frame itself.

This mental model explains why events stop at the first widget that handles them (a button on top of a scroll panel prevents the panel from scrolling), why hidden frames do not tick or draw (they are removed from the table), and why `OpenWindow`/`CloseWindow` use a stack (opening a new picture covers the old one without throwing it away). The YAML syntax is parsed by the engine described in [Part 2.1 — MiniYaml Parser](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_01_MiniYaml) and the data-driven rules in [Part 2.4 — Rulesets, Actors, and Weapons](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_04_Rules_Weapons); for a complete UI walkthrough see [Part 10.3 — Porting, Modding, and Developer Workflows](#file-chapters-Part_10_Chapter_03_Port_And_Modding).

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the OpenRA widget hierarchy and the roles of `Ui.Root`, `MenuRootWidget`, and `WorldRootWidget`.
- Describe how YAML chrome files define widget layouts and logic classes.
- Trace the widget lifecycle from loading through `Tick`, `Draw`, and input handling.
- Use `ChromeMetrics` to share UI constants across widgets.
- Implement a custom widget type and a `ChromeLogic` logic class.
- Explain focus management and the window stack behavior.
- Describe how mouse and keyboard events propagate through the widget tree.
- Author a new chrome layout from YAML to a working screen.
- Recognize Cameo-specific widgets and logic classes and how they integrate with the command bar, promotion tree, and production palette.

| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/Logic/ProductionTooltipCameoLogic.cs` | Cameo production tooltip logic. |

## Architecture

### Widget tree
![Widget tree](images/Part_04_Chapter_03_Widgets-Widget_tree.svg)


All UI widgets are nodes in a single tree rooted at `Ui.Root`. The engine maintains two main subtrees: the menu chrome (`MenuRootWidget`) and the in-game chrome (`WorldRootWidget`). Windows can be pushed onto a stack so that closing one restores the previous window. Every widget has a `Parent`, a list of `Children`, and `Bounds` expressed in screen coordinates.

### YAML-driven layout

A widget is defined in YAML like this:

```yaml
MainMenu:
    Container:
        X: (WINDOW_WIDTH - WIDTH)/2
        Y: (WINDOW_HEIGHT - HEIGHT)/2
        Width: 400
        Height: 300
        Children:
            Label@TITLE:
                X: 0
                Y: 0
                Width: 400
                Height: 40
                Text: OpenRA
            Button@START:
                X: 50
                Y: 80
                Width: 300
                Height: 40
                Text: Start Game
                Font: Bold
```

The widget type is the node key (e.g., `Container`, `Label`, `Button`). The `@NAME` suffix sets the widget's `Id`. The type name `Foo` in YAML maps to a C# class named `FooWidget` by naming convention. `FieldLoader` maps the remaining YAML keys to public fields or properties on the widget class.

### Logic classes

Widgets can have one or more `Logic` classes declared in YAML:

```yaml
MainMenu:
    Container:
        Logic: MainMenuLogic
        ...
```

The logic class must inherit `ChromeLogic` and is instantiated when the widget is loaded. It receives the widget and any `WidgetArgs` passed during loading. Logic classes handle events, update widget state, and implement screen behavior. The `Logic` field can be a single string or a comma-separated list; multiple logic objects are created in order and each receives `Tick`, `BecameHidden`, and `BecameVisible`.

### Metrics

`ChromeMetrics` is a global dictionary of UI values shared across widgets:

```yaml
Metrics:
    TextfieldColorHighlight: 3A8C3A
    ButtonTextColor: FFFFFF
    ButtonTextColorDisabled: 808080
```

Widgets reference these keys in code via `ChromeMetrics.Get<T>("key")`. They are loaded from the files listed in the manifest's `ChromeMetrics` section. Metrics are commonly used for colors, default cursors, button sizes, and spacing constants.

### Widget lifecycle

The complete lifecycle of a widget is:

```
WidgetLoader.LoadWidget
  -> NewWidget (ObjectCreator creates FooWidget by naming convention)
  -> AddChild to parent
  -> Load Id from "Type@Id"
  -> FieldLoader loads fields from YAML (except Children)
  -> Initialize(args)        // evaluates layout expressions, sets Bounds
  -> recursively LoadWidget for each child
  -> PostInit(args)          // creates ChromeLogic objects
  -> TickOuter() each frame  // calls Tick(), then children, then Logic.Tick()
  -> DrawOuter() each frame  // calls Draw(), then children
  -> HandleMouseInputOuter() / HandleKeyPressOuter() / HandleTextInputOuter()
  -> Hidden() / Removed()    // logic objects receive BecameHidden / Dispose
```

Important lifecycle details:

- `Initialize` is called after the widget object is created and its fields are loaded, but before children are created. This is where `Bounds` is evaluated from the `X`, `Y`, `Width`, `Height` expressions.
- `PostInit` is called after all children are created. It instantiates the `ChromeLogic` classes listed in the `Logic` field, adds them to `LogicObjects`, and subscribes them to the `Ui` mediator.
- `TickOuter` visits children in order and then ticks each logic object. Only visible widgets tick; hidden widgets are skipped entirely.
- `DrawOuter` visits children in order. Only visible widgets draw.
- `Hidden()` is called when a widget is removed from its parent by `HideChild` (for example, when a new window is opened and the old one is hidden). It forces the widget to yield mouse and keyboard focus and propagates `Hidden()` to children. The logic objects receive `BecameHidden` from `Ui.OpenWindow`/`CloseWindow`.
- `Removed()` is called when a widget is permanently removed. It yields focus and disposes logic objects.

### Cameo-specific widgets

Cameo adds custom widgets and logic classes in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/`:

- **`CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic`** — Replaces the standard command bar logic for the custom formation system. It binds the `ATTACK_MOVE`, `FORCE_MOVE`, `FORCE_ATTACK`, `GUARD`, `SCATTER`, `DEPLOY`, `STOP`, and `QUEUE_ORDERS` buttons to the custom order generators (`CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator`, `ForceModifiersOrderGenerator`, `GuardOrderGenerator`, etc.). It also highlights the attack-move button when the active `OrderGenerator` is a `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator`.
- **`CommanderTreeWidget`** — A custom production/research tree widget that renders the promotion tree. It displays nodes, edges, and group boxes, handles mouse hover and click, and integrates with the production queue and tooltip system.
- **`CommanderTreeDismissWidget`** and **`CommanderTreeWindowLogic`** — Supporting widget and logic for opening/dismissing the commander tree window.
- **`IngamePromotionCounterWidget`** — Draws the player's current rank, points, and progress on the in-game HUD using `PlayerPromotions`.
- **`ObserverPromotionsIconsWidget`** and **`PlayerUpgradesIconsWidget`** — Display promotion/upgrade icons in observer and player UIs.
- **`AutoControlGroupsWidget`** — Captures hotkeys to register selected unit types to a control group via `AutoControlGroupsManager`.
- **`QuotaProductionPaletteWidget`** — Extends the production palette to show unit quotas (`alive/quota`) and allows left/right click to adjust quotas through `QuotaProductionManager`.
- **`DragHandleWidget`, `RoundedImageWidget`, `ScaledImageWidget`** — Low-level custom widgets for drag handles and image rendering.
- **`CameoGameplaySettingsLogic`, `CameoObserverStatsLogic`, `IngameActorStatsLogicCameo`, `ArmyTooltipCameoLogic`, `ActorIconTooltipCameoLogic`, `ProductionTooltipCameoLogic`** — Logic classes that drive Cameo-specific settings, observer stats, actor stats, and tooltips.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Loading a chrome screen

1. `WidgetLoader.LoadWidget` is called with the YAML root node and a parent widget.
2. `NewWidget` uses `ObjectCreator` to instantiate the C# widget class (`TypeName + "Widget"`).
3. `FieldLoader` populates public fields from YAML keys (`X`, `Y`, `Width`, `Height`, `Text`, etc.).
4. `Initialize` evaluates layout expressions and sets `Bounds`.
5. Children are loaded recursively.
6. `PostInit` creates `ChromeLogic` objects listed in the `Logic` field.
7. Every frame, `TickOuter` and `DrawOuter` visit the widget tree in order.

### Input propagation

1. A mouse or keyboard event is delivered to `Ui.HandleInput`.
2. The engine walks the widget tree from front to back, calling `HandleMouseInputOuter`/`HandleKeyPressOuter`.
3. The first widget whose bounds contain the event and that returns `true` consumes the event.
4. If no widget consumes it, the event may be passed to the world (e.g., clicking on the map to issue an order).
5. `MouseFocusWidget` and `KeyboardFocusWidget` override the normal hit-test so drag and text events stay on the focused widget.

### Cameo command bar example

1. The player selects units and clicks the `ATTACK_MOVE` button in the command bar.
2. `CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic` sets `world.OrderGenerator = new CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator(selectedActors, button)`.
3. The custom order generator takes over input handling, renders command-line markers, and produces `AttackMove`/`AssaultMove` orders on mouse release.
4. The orders are issued through `World.IssueOrder` and processed by the lockstep simulation.

## Configuration (YAML)

### Chrome manifest entry

```yaml
Chrome:
    mods/common/chrome/mainmenu.yaml
    mods/cameo/chrome/ingame.yaml
```

### Declaring a custom widget

```yaml
CameoPromotionCounter:
    IngamePromotionCounterWidget:
        X: 10
        Y: 10
        Width: 200
        Height: 60
        Font: Bold
        Align: Right
```

The key `IngamePromotionCounterWidget` maps to the C# class `IngamePromotionCounterWidget` in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/IngamePromotionCounterWidget.cs`.

### Attaching logic

```yaml
COMMAND_BAR:
    Container:
        Logic: CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic
        Children:
            ...
```

### Chrome metrics

```yaml
Metrics:
    ClickSound: click.wav
    ClickDisabledSound: clickdisabled.wav
```

Cameo-specific widgets also use `ChromeMetrics` keys such as `TextContrastColorDark` and `TextContrastColorLight` for text rendering.

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **Widget type name mismatch.** A YAML key `Foo` must map to a C# class `FooWidget`. If the class is missing, `WidgetLoader.NewWidget` throws.
- **Logic class not found.** The `Logic` string must map to a class inheriting `ChromeLogic`. If it is missing, `PostInit` throws.
- **Missing `ChromeMetrics` key.** Calling `ChromeMetrics.Get<T>` for a key that is not defined throws at runtime.
- **Event capture.** A widget that returns `true` from `HandleMouseInput` stops propagation. Make sure invisible/disabled widgets do not accidentally capture events.
- **World access in widgets.** Widgets can access `World`, but they must not mutate simulation state directly. Always issue `Order` objects through `World.IssueOrder` for synced changes.
- **Cameo custom widgets require the assembly.** Custom widget classes must be in an assembly listed in `mod.yaml` `Assemblies:` so `ObjectCreator` can find them.
- **Promotion/tooltip widgets need `PlayerPromotions` or production queues.** If the trait is missing, the widget may fail to initialize or show no data.

## Summary

Cameo uses the same widget/chrome system as upstream OpenRA but adds a significant number of custom widgets and logic classes in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/`. The most important additions are the command bar logic for custom formations, the commander/promotion tree, the quota production palette, and the various HUD/statistics widgets. All of them follow the same lifecycle: YAML declares the widget layout and logic classes, `WidgetLoader` instantiates the C# classes, `FieldLoader` populates fields, and the widget tree ticks and draws every frame.

# Chapter 4.4 — Viewport and Input (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_04_Chapter_04_Viewport_Input}

## Purpose
![Mental model diagram](images/Part_04_Chapter_04_Viewport_Input-learning-objectives-summary-diagram-or-concept-map-showing-h-fe332a.svg)


The [viewport](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) maps the simulation world to the screen, while the input pipeline turns mouse and keyboard events into [orders](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) that cross into the deterministic simulation. OpenRA provides the engine-level `Viewport`, `WorldInteractionControllerWidget`, and the order-generator framework. Cameo reuses the engine viewport and coordinate spaces unchanged, but replaces the default unit order generator and command-bar wiring with a custom formations system that supports drag-line waypoints, assault-move variants, and richer on-world annotation rendering. This chapter explains the shared viewport and input architecture and the Cameo-specific order generators that sit on top of it.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain how the `Viewport` maps world coordinates (`WPos`, `CPos`) to screen pixels and back.
- Describe the input dispatch pipeline from the platform window to the active `IOrderGenerator`.
- Implement or extend a custom order generator for a new command mode.
- Configure viewport sizes, cursors, and command-bar widgets in YAML.
- Trace how a mouse click in the world becomes a `World.IssueOrder` call.
- Compare the engine's `UnitOrderGenerator` with Cameo's `CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator`.
- Identify common pitfalls in viewport coordinate transforms and order-generator lifecycle.

## Practical Example: Custom Formations Attack-Move Mode

Suppose the player selects a group of tanks and clicks the **Attack Move** button. In vanilla OpenRA the command bar would install `AttackMoveOrderGenerator` from `OpenRA.Mods.Common`. In Cameo the command bar installs `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator`, which captures a drag line instead of a single click and emits `AttackMove` or `AssaultMove` orders depending on whether the player is holding `Ctrl`.

### UI wiring

`CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic` creates the generator when the button is clicked:

```csharp
attackMoveButton.IsHighlighted = () => world.OrderGenerator is CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator;

void Toggle(bool allowCancel)
{
    if (attackMoveButton.IsHighlighted())
    {
        if (allowCancel)
            world.CancelInputMode();
    }
    else
        world.OrderGenerator = new CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator(
            selectedActors,
            Game.Settings.Game.ResolveActionButton(MouseActionType.ConfirmOrder));
}

attackMoveButton.OnClick = () => Toggle(true);
attackMoveButton.OnKeyPress = _ => Toggle(false);
```

`world.OrderGenerator` is the engine's active order generator property. Once assigned, the engine's `WorldInteractionControllerWidget` routes subsequent mouse events to the generator's `OnLMBDown`, `OnMouseMove`, and `OnLMBUp` callbacks, exactly as it does for the upstream order generators.

### Order generator

`CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator` derives from `CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase`, which in turn implements `IOrderGenerator`. The generator tracks the mouse drag as a command line and emits one order per waypoint along the line:

```csharp
public class CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator : CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase
{
    readonly TraitPair<AttackMove>[] subjects;
    protected override MouseActionType ActionType => MouseActionType.ConfirmOrder;
    readonly MouseButton expectedButton;

    public CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator(IEnumerable<Actor> subjects, MouseButton button)
    {
        expectedButton = button;
        this.subjects = subjects.Where(a => !a.IsDead)
            .SelectMany(a => a.TraitsImplementing<AttackMove>()
                .Select(am => new TraitPair<AttackMove>(a, am)))
            .ToArray();
    }

    public override string GetCursor(World world, CPos cell, int2 worldPixel, MouseInput mi)
    {
        var isAssaultMove = mi.Modifiers.HasModifier(Modifiers.Ctrl);
        // ... choose between assault / blocked / normal cursor
        return isAssaultMove ? info.AssaultMoveCursor : info.AttackMoveCursor;
    }

    protected override IEnumerable<Order> OnLMBUp(CPos inCell, int2 inWorldPixel, MouseInput inMouseInput)
    {
        string orderName = inMouseInput.Modifiers.HasModifier(Modifiers.Ctrl) ? "AssaultMove" : "AttackMove";
        if (IsTap)
        {
            foreach (var o in TapOrder(inCell, inWorldPixel, inMouseInput, orderName))
                yield return o;
        }
        else
        {
            foreach (var o in EndCommandLine(inCell, inWorldPixel, inMouseInput, orderName))
                yield return o;
        }

        if (expectedButton != MouseButton.Left)
            OwningWorld.CancelInputMode();
    }
}
```

The generator does not issue the orders directly to the network; it yields `Order` objects that the engine collects and routes through `World.IssueOrder`. Because the orders follow the same path as human orders, they are replay-safe and synchronized across clients.

## Architecture

### Viewport coordinate spaces

The engine uses several coordinate spaces that every order generator must understand:

- **World position** (`WPos`) — 3D world coordinates in world pixels. The `Z` component is height above the ground plane.
- **Cell position** (`CPos`) — tile coordinates on the map grid.
- **Map position** (`MPos`) / **Projected position** (`PPos`) — internal grid coordinates for rectangular and isometric maps.
- **View position** (`int2`) — screen pixels relative to the viewport origin.
- **UI position** (`int2`) — screen pixels relative to the window.

The `Viewport` provides the conversions:

- `WorldToViewPx` — converts a `WPos` or `int2` world pixel to screen pixels, accounting for zoom, UI scale, and the viewport center.
- `ViewToWorldPx` — the inverse of `WorldToViewPx`.
- `ViewToWorld` — converts screen pixels to a `CPos`, handling isometric cells and falling back to the nearest candidate cell.
- `ProjectedPosition` — unprojects a screen pixel to the ground plane (`Z = 0`), resolving the ambiguity caused by the `screenY = worldY - worldZ` projection.

Cameo uses these same transforms. The custom generators operate in cell coordinates and world pixels (`int2`) when deciding waypoints, and call `wr.Viewport.WorldToViewPx(...)` only inside `RenderAboveShroud` to produce on-screen annotations. Keeping simulation decisions in world/cell space is important: if the generator used screen-space math for order targets, zoom or UI scale could change game behavior.

### Input dispatch pipeline

The input pipeline is unchanged by Cameo:

1. **SDL2 / platform layer** (`Sdl2Input`) reads mouse and keyboard events and wraps them in `MouseInput` / `KeyInput`.
2. **Widget root** (`Game.cs`) routes the event through the UI widget tree. If a widget handles it, the event stops.
3. **World interaction controller** (`WorldInteractionControllerWidget`) receives unhandled events that fall through to the world viewport. It converts the screen pixel to a cell and calls the active order generator.
4. **Active order generator** (`World.OrderGenerator`) interprets the event. It may change the cursor, render a preview, or yield `Order` objects.
5. **World issue order** (`World.IssueOrder`) takes the yielded orders and pushes them into the lockstep order queue.

Cameo participates only at step 4 by installing custom generators. The upstream engine still owns viewport panning, zoom, culling, and lockstep order routing.

### Order generator lifecycle

The `IOrderGenerator` interface is defined in the engine and has the following lifecycle hooks:

| Method | Called when | Typical use |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `Tick(World)` | Every game tick. | Animate cursors, update internal state. |
| `GetCursor(World, CPos, int2, MouseInput)` | Every frame while the mouse is over the world. | Choose a cursor based on the target cell and modifiers. |
| `RenderAboveShroud(WorldRenderer, World)` | Every frame. | Draw drag boxes, command lines, waypoints, etc. |
| `RenderAnnotations(WorldRenderer, World)` | Every frame. | Draw annotations above the shroud. |
| `InputOverridesSelection(World, int2, MouseInput)` | When deciding whether a click selects a unit. | Cameo uses this to override selection behavior during drag-line mode. |
| `OnMouseInput` / `OnLMBDown` / `OnLMBUp` / `OnRMBDown` / `OnRMBUp` | Mouse events. | Begin or end command-line, drag-box, or cancel mode. |
| `Deactivated()` | When the generator is replaced. | Clean up rollover selection. |

Cameo's `CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase` implements the common logic: drag boxes, command lines, multi-tap selection, circle commands, and marker rendering. Derived classes (`CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator`, `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator`) override how clicks are translated into orders.

## Data Flow

### Click-to-order path for a Cameo attack-move line

1. The player clicks **Attack Move** in the command bar. `CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic` sets `world.OrderGenerator = new CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator(selectedActors, button)`.
2. `WorldInteractionControllerWidget` receives `OnMouseDown` on the world. It calls `orderGenerator.OnLMBDown(cell, worldPixel, mi)`.
3. `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator.OnLMBDown` calls `StartCommandLine(cell)` and records the first waypoint in the base class's `CurrentMarkedCells` list.
4. As the player drags, `OnMouseMove` extends the command line and adds additional cells.
5. On release, `OnLMBUp` calls `EndCommandLine(..., "AttackMove")` or `"AssaultMove"` depending on `Ctrl`. The base class converts the line into one order per cell and yields them.
6. `WorldInteractionControllerWidget` collects the yielded orders and calls `World.IssueOrder(order)` for each one.
7. The order enters the lockstep queue, is processed by `UnitOrders` or `AttackMove` traits, and becomes actor behavior on the next tick.

### Selection path in the default Cameo generator

`CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator` can be configured as the default order generator in `mod.yaml` by setting `DefaultOrderGenerator: CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator`. When active, it starts a drag-box selection on left mouse down and calls `SelectionUtils.SelectActorsInBoxWithDeadzone` on release, using the deadzone from `Game.Settings.Game.SelectionDeadzone`. A double-click expands the selection to all matching selection classes on screen, exactly like the upstream `UnitOrderGenerator`. The current Cameo mod keeps the upstream `UnitOrderGenerator` as the default and uses `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator` only for attack-move / assault-move drag-line commands from the command bar.

## Configuration

### mod.yaml

The default order generator is the entry point for the whole input pipeline. Cameo points it to the custom unit generator:

```yaml
Mod:
    # Default upstream order generator used by the current Cameo mod:
    DefaultOrderGenerator: UnitOrderGenerator
    # Optional: switch to the custom formations generator for full drag-line behavior:
    # DefaultOrderGenerator: CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator
```

### cursors.yaml

Cameo reuses the upstream cursor names (`move`, `attackmove`, `assaultmove`, `force-move`, `force-attack`, `guard`, etc.) but can also add custom cursors for the new line-order modes. The generators resolve cursor names through `ChromeMetrics` and `IOrderTargeter` results.

### chrome.yaml / ingame.yaml

The command bar widget is wired to `CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic` instead of the upstream `CommandBarLogic`. The widget names (`ATTACK_MOVE`, `FORCE_MOVE`, `FORCE_ATTACK`, `GUARD`, `SCATTER`, `DEPLOY`, `STOP`, `QUEUE_ORDERS`) and hotkeys are the same as upstream so that existing modders can find them quickly, but the logic behind them creates Cameo generators where appropriate.

### CustomFormationsModOptions

`CustomFormationsModOptions` is a player-actor trait loaded with mod-level YAML keys such as `MoveOrderMarkerImage`, `MoveOrderMarkerPalette`, `AttackMoveOrderTileMarkerSequence`, etc. The order generator base reads these in `OnInitialize` and uses them to create the `SpriteRenderable` and `Animation` instances that draw command-line markers. This keeps the visual look of the command line data-driven rather than hard-coded.

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_04_Chapter_04_Viewport_Input-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


| Component | Connects to | Why |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator` | `WorldInteractionControllerWidget`, `World.Selection` | Optional replacement for the default selection and contextual order behavior. |
| `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator` | `AttackMove` trait, `CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic` | Provides drag-line attack-move / assault-move commands. |
| `CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase` | `Viewport`, `UILineAnnotationRenderable`, `SelectionUtils` | Draws drag boxes, command lines, and rollover selection using engine rendering helpers. |
| `CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic` | `World.OrderGenerator`, `ButtonWidget` | Installs custom generators and forwards hotkeys. |
| `CustomFormationsModOptions` | `Map.Sequences`, `WorldRenderer.Palette` | Supplies marker image and palette names so the command line looks data-driven. |
| `World.IssueOrder` | `OrderManager`, `UnitOrders` | Converts yielded orders into synchronized simulation state. |

## Algorithms

### Command-line waypoint generation

`CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase` builds the command line incrementally as the mouse moves. When the mouse enters a new map cell, the cell is appended to `CurrentMarkedCells` and its center (`world.Map.CenterOfCell(cell)`) is added to `CurrentOrderMarkers`. The render pass turns these markers into `SpriteRenderable` instances, either static or animated, depending on the mod options. On release, the line is converted into one `Order` per cell, preserving the sequence the player drew. This is the core mechanic that distinguishes Cameo from the vanilla single-click order generators.

### Drag-box selection with modifiers

The base class draws the drag box using `UIRectangleAnnotationRenderable`, whose corners are `wr.Viewport.WorldToViewPx(DragStartMousePosition)` and `wr.Viewport.WorldToViewPx(CurrentMousePosition)`. The color changes based on modifier keys (`Alt`, `Ctrl`) to preview selection modes (add, remove, or same-type). The selection itself is delegated to `SelectionUtils.SelectActorsInBoxWithDeadzone`, which respects the configured deadzone.

### Cursor selection

The default generator's `GetCursor` re-implements the upstream `UnitOrderGenerator` logic: it checks `MouseControlStyle`, overrides selection when appropriate, and picks the highest-priority `IOrderTargeter` result from the selected actors. This keeps the cursor behavior familiar while adding the custom line-mode cursor transitions when the player is in `CommandLine` mode.

## Common Pitfalls

- **Screen-space vs. world-space logic.** `RenderAboveShroud` must use `Viewport.WorldToViewPx`, but order targets must be computed in `CPos` or `WPos`. Mixing them up causes the waypoint behavior to change with zoom level.
- **Order generator lifetime.** The generator holds references to `World`, `WorldRenderer`, `Animation`, and renderable lists. If it is not cleaned up when `world.OrderGenerator` is reassigned, stale state can leak. Always use `world.CancelInputMode()` to reset the generator to the default.
- **Replay and sync safety.** Order generators run on the local client only. They must never mutate the world directly (for example, by moving actors). All changes must travel through yielded `Order` objects so that replays remain deterministic.
- **Cursor name mismatches.** If `GetCursor` returns a name that does not exist in `cursors.yaml`, the cursor will fall back to the default or disappear silently.
- **Multi-tap and deadzone handling.** The base class uses `Game.Settings.Game.SelectionDeadzone` for both tap detection and drag-box validation. A deadzone that is too large makes precise single-click orders hard, while one that is too small makes drag-box selection trigger unintentionally.
- **Mod options not loaded.** If `CustomFormationsModOptions` is missing from the player actor rules, `OnInitialize` will fail and the generator will return early, leaving the world without a valid order generator.

## Summary

- The `Viewport` and `WorldInteractionControllerWidget` are engine components that Cameo reuses unchanged.
- Cameo specializes the **order-generator layer** by adding `CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator` (an optional replacement for the default `UnitOrderGenerator`) and `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator` for drag-line attack-move / assault-move commands.
- The current Cameo mod keeps the upstream `UnitOrderGenerator` as the default and installs `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator` from `CustomFormationsCommandBarLogic`. A mod can switch to `CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator` in `mod.yaml` if desired.
- All world-changing input still flows through `World.OrderGenerator` → `World.IssueOrder` → `OrderManager`, so Cameo input remains deterministic, replay-safe, and compatible with the lockstep engine.
- The base class handles the shared mechanics: drag boxes, command lines, circle commands, marker rendering, and rollover selection. Derived classes only decide which orders to issue.

| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/WorldInteractionControllerWidget.cs` | `OnMouseDown`, `OnMouseUp`, `OnMouseMove` | How the engine feeds events to the order generator. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Orders/IOrderGenerator.cs` | Interface declaration | Lifecycle hooks every order generator must implement. |
| `OpenRA.Game/World.cs` | `OrderGenerator` property, `IssueOrder` | Entry point for order generation and lockstep submission. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Orders/CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase.cs` | `OnLMBDown`, `OnLMBUp`, `RenderAboveShroud`, `StartCommandLine`, `EndCommandLine` | Shared drag-line, drag-box, and rendering logic. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Orders/CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator.cs` | `GetCursor`, `OnLMBDown`, `OnLMBUp` | Default selection and contextual order behavior in Cameo. |

# Chapter 5.1 — Audio Architecture (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_05_Chapter_01_Audio_Architecture}

## Purpose

OpenRA's audio system bridges game events (unit voices, UI feedback, music, weapon reports) to a low-level sound engine. The architecture is deliberately layered: the engine defines a small, backend-agnostic interface (`ISoundEngine`), the `Sound` class manages samples, voices, notifications, and music, and a platform-specific implementation (OpenAL) handles device management, source pooling, and 3D spatialization. This chapter explains the layers, the data flow, and the configuration that ties them together, with a focus on the Cameo mod's audio file loaders and sound-specific traits.

The Cameo mod inherits the upstream audio architecture. It adds an `AudioBagLoader` for legacy `.bag`/`.idx` audio archives and a handful of sound-related traits (`SoundAnnouncement`, `AmbientSoundCA`, `AnnounceOnCreation`, `AttackSoundsCA`) that extend or replace upstream sound triggers.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the layered audio architecture from game code through [ISoundEngine](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) to the OpenAL backend.
- Describe the roles of `ISoundEngine`, [ISoundSource](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary), [ISound](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary), and the `Sound` class.
- Trace how a sound file is loaded, cached, and played through the audio pipeline.
- Configure audio loaders and sound [manifests](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) in `mod.yaml`.
- Explain the difference between UI sounds and world sounds, including player filtering.
- Describe source pooling and per-frame capping in `OpenAlSoundEngine`.
- Recognize Cameo-specific audio extensions: `AudioBagLoader`, `SoundAnnouncement`, `AmbientSoundCA`, `AnnounceOnCreation`, and `AttackSoundsCA`.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_01_Audio_Architecture-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Game/Sound/SoundDevice.cs` | `ISoundEngine`, `ISound`, `ISoundSource`, and `SoundDevice` records. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Sound/Sound.cs` | Main API: sample caching, playback, music, video audio, and listener position. |
| `OpenRA.Game/GameRules/SoundInfo.cs` | Ruleset sound configuration (variants, prefixes, voice pools, notification pools). |
| `OpenRA.Game/GameRules/MusicInfo.cs` | Music track metadata (filename, title, hidden, volume modifier, length). |
| `OpenRA.Platforms.Default/OpenAlSoundEngine.cs` | OpenAL backend implementation: device enumeration, source pool, spatial attenuation. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/FileFormats/ImaAdpcmReader.cs` | IMA ADPCM format reader. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/AudioLoaders/WavLoader.cs` | WAV format loader. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/AudioLoaders/OggLoader.cs` | Ogg Vorbis loader. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/AudioLoaders/Mp3Loader.cs` | MP3 loader. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/AudioLoaders/VocLoader.cs` | Westwood VOC format loader. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/VideoLoaders/VqaLoader.cs` | VQA video loader (also produces audio). |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/MusicPlaylist.cs` | World trait that drives the music playlist, victory/defeat music, and background music. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Settings.cs` | `SoundSettings` for volume, device, mute, shuffle, etc. |
| `OpenRA.Game/ModData.cs` | Holds `SoundLoaders` and exposes them to `Sound.Initialize`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/FileSystem/BagFile.cs` | `AudioBagLoader` for legacy `.bag`/`.idx` audio archives. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/SoundAnnouncement.cs` | Plays a sound when the trait is enabled. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AmbientSoundCA.cs` | Extended ambient sound trait with initial/final sounds and fog control. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AnnounceOnCreation.cs` | Plays a notification when an actor is created. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AttackSoundsCA.cs` | Extended attack sound trait with armament filtering and fog control. |

## Architecture

### Layered audio stack

```
[Game / Traits] -> [Sound] -> [ISoundEngine] -> [OpenAlSoundEngine] -> [OpenAL device]
```

The `Sound` class is the single point of contact for the rest of the game. It never talks to OpenAL directly. Instead it calls methods on the `ISoundEngine` interface, which is provided by `IPlatform.CreateSound(...)`. The only shipped implementation is `OpenAlSoundEngine` in `OpenRA.Platforms.Default`.

### Key abstractions

- `ISoundEngine` — backend contract: create sources, play sounds, pause/stop, set listener position, manage volume.
- `ISoundSource` — a loaded audio buffer (e.g., an OpenAL buffer). Created once and reused for many plays.
- `ISound` — an active playing instance (e.g., an OpenAL source). Tracks completion and position.
- `Sound` — high-level cache and playback API exposed as `Game.Sound`.

### Sound object lifetime
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_01_Audio_Architecture-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


At startup, `Sound` receives a `SoundSettings` object and asks the platform to create an engine. It then loads audio files on demand through a `Cache<string, ISoundSource>` keyed by filename. When a game mod is loaded, `Sound.Initialize` is called with the mod's `SoundLoaders` and `IReadOnlyFileSystem`. This stops all current sounds, disposes cached sources, and rebuilds the cache for the new mod.

### Cameo audio additions

Cameo does not change the core `Sound`/`ISoundEngine` architecture. It adds:

1. **`AudioBagLoader`** — a package loader (not a sound loader) that lets the VFS mount legacy `.bag`/`.idx` audio archives. When a sound file is requested from a mounted bag, the package returns a synthetic WAV stream, which is then parsed by the upstream `WavLoader` or `AudLoader`. See [Part 6.3 — Virtual File System](#file-chapters-Part_06_Chapter_03_VFS) and [Part 6.5 — Asset Loaders](#file-chapters-Part_06_Chapter_05_Asset_Loaders) for the full VFS/loader details.
2. **Sound trigger traits** — `SoundAnnouncement`, `AmbientSoundCA`, `AnnounceOnCreation`, and `AttackSoundsCA` live in the Cameo assemblies and extend the upstream sound trigger family with extra YAML fields and behaviors.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Engine creation and initialization

```csharp
soundEngine = platform.CreateSound(soundSettings.Device);
```

`IPlatform.CreateSound` is implemented by `OpenRA.Platforms.Default` and returns an `OpenAlSoundEngine` (or a dummy engine if sound is disabled). The device string comes from the `SoundSettings.Device` field. If `soundSettings.Mute` is true, `Sound.MuteAudio()` is called immediately.

### Loading a sample

```csharp
ISoundSource LoadIntoMemory(ISoundFormat soundFormat) => soundEngine.AddSoundSourceFromMemory(
    soundFormat.GetPCMInputStream().ReadAllBytes(), soundFormat.Channels, soundFormat.SampleBits, soundFormat.SampleRate);

sounds = new Cache<string, ISoundSource>(filename => LoadSound(filename, LoadIntoMemory));
```

When `Sound.Play` is called with a filename, the cache resolves the filename, opens the file via the mod file system, tries each `ISoundLoader` until one parses the format, and then asks the engine to create a source from the decoded PCM.

For files inside a `.bag` archive, the VFS returns a `MergedStream` containing a synthetic WAV header followed by the raw audio data. The upstream sound loaders then parse that stream as a normal WAV or IMA ADPCM file.

### Playing a sound

The central `Play` method is:

```csharp
ISound Play(SoundType type, Player player, string name, bool headRelative, WPos pos, float volumeModifier = 1f, bool loop = false)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(name) || DisableAllSounds || (DisableWorldSounds && type == SoundType.World))
        return null;

    if (player != null && player != player.World.LocalPlayer)
        return null;

    return soundEngine.Play2D(sounds[name],
        loop, headRelative, pos,
        InternalSoundVolume * volumeModifier, true);
}
```

`SoundType` is either `UI` or `World`. UI sounds are always head-relative and unattenuated. World sounds are placed at a `WPos` and are attenuated by distance and the listener position.

### Player filtering

`PlayToPlayer` plays a sound only for a specific player. If `player` is not the local player, the call returns null immediately. This is used for per-player notifications such as "Building complete" or "Unit ready".

### Listener position

The camera/controller sets the listener position:

```csharp
public void SetListenerPosition(WPos position)
{
    soundEngine.SetListenerPosition(position);
}
```

World sounds are attenuated relative to this listener. UI sounds are relative to the listener (head-relative) so they are not attenuated.

### Source pooling

`OpenAlSoundEngine` pre-creates a pool of 256 OpenAL sources. When a sound is played, the engine allocates an idle source, or reclaims one whose sound has completed. If the pool is exhausted and no completed sounds are reclaimable, the play request returns null.

The engine also implements per-frame capping: if more than `MaxInstancesPerFrame` (3) instances of the same sound source start within 5 frames and within `GroupDistance` (2730 world units) of each other, additional plays are dropped to prevent audio spam.

### Music and video audio
![Configuration (yaml) diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_01_Audio_Architecture-annotated-yaml-snippet-diagram-showing-the-key-fields-and-ho-6a1b98.svg)


Music is loaded via `Sound.PlayMusic(MusicInfo, bool looped)` and streamed through `ISoundEngine.Play2DStream`. The `Sound.Tick` method monitors the music `ISound.Complete` flag and invokes the `onMusicComplete` callback to advance the playlist.

Video audio is decoded by the video loader and passed directly as raw PCM to `soundEngine.AddSoundSourceFromMemory` and `soundEngine.Play2D`.

### Cameo sound trigger data flow

- **`SoundAnnouncement`** — when its parent trait becomes enabled, it picks a random sound from `SoundFiles` and plays it as a world sound. It respects `AudibleThroughFog` and `OneShot`.
- **`AmbientSoundCA`** — on creation it picks a random delay from `Delay`, then plays the `InitialSound` (if configured), then loops the main `SoundFiles` or plays them at `Interval`. It supports an optional `FinalSound` when the trait is disabled or the actor is removed.
- **`AnnounceOnCreation`** — when the actor is created, it plays a `Speech` notification for the owner (or all players if `NotifyAll` is true).
- **`AttackSoundsCA`** — implements `INotifyAttack` and `ITick`. It plays a sound when an attack or preparation event occurs on a matching armament, with optional delay and fog control.

## Configuration (YAML)

### Sound manifest

The mod manifest lists the audio file loaders:

```yaml
Loaders:
    Sound:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.WavLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.OggLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.Mp3Loader
```

The order matters: `Sound.LoadSound` tries each loader in order until one succeeds.

Cameo also registers the bag package loader:

```yaml
Loaders:
    Package:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Cnc.FileSystem.MixLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.FileSystem.InstallShieldLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Cameo.FileSystem.AudioBagLoader
```

### Voices and notifications

`SoundInfo` is loaded from the manifest's `Voices` and `Notifications` files. It defines:

- `Variants` — per-actor sound file extensions (e.g., `.aud`, `.ogg`).
- `Prefixes` — per-actor path prefixes.
- `Voices` — named voice sets mapped to arrays of sound files.
- `Notifications` — named notification sets mapped to sound pools with volume modifiers and interrupt types.

Example:

```yaml
Sounds:
    Voices:
        e1:
            Select: e1sel1, e1sel2, e1sel3
            Move: e1mov1, e1mov2, e1mov3
            Attack: e1atk1, e1atk2
```

### Cameo audio trait YAML

```yaml
SOME_UNIT:
    AttackSoundsCA:
        Sounds: attack1, attack2
        Delay: 5
        DelayRelativeTo: Preparation
        AudibleThroughFog: false
        Armaments: primary
    AmbientSoundCA:
        SoundFiles: ambient_loop
        InitialSound: startup
        FinalSound: shutdown
        AudibleThroughFog: true
        VolumeMultiplier: 0.8
    AnnounceOnCreation:
        Notification: UnitReady
        NotifyAll: false
```

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **Sound loader order.** The first loader that recognizes the file wins. Make sure specialized loaders (e.g., `VocLoader`) are listed before generic ones if they are needed.
- **Bag files need matching `.idx` files.** `AudioBagLoader` opens the `.idx` file with the same base name as the `.bag`. Missing or corrupt indices cause the package to fail loading.
- **Audio bag entries are wrapped as WAV.** `BagFile.GetStream` synthesizes a WAV header. The actual codec is determined by the entry flags (PCM or IMA ADPCM). The upstream sound loader parses the wrapped stream.
- **Source pool exhaustion.** With 256 sources, heavy combat can exhaust the pool. Per-frame capping helps, but many overlapping sounds can still be dropped.
- **Player filtering on notifications.** `PlayNotification` silently drops sounds for non-local players. This is correct for per-player feedback but can be confusing when debugging.
- **Fog control in Cameo traits.** `SoundAnnouncement`, `AmbientSoundCA`, and `AttackSoundsCA` all respect `AudibleThroughFog`. If false, the sound is not played (or played at zero volume) when the actor is under shroud or fog.
- **Armament filtering in `AttackSoundsCA`.** Only armaments whose names are in `Armaments` trigger the sound. The default is `primary`, `secondary`.

## Summary

Cameo inherits the upstream OpenRA audio architecture (`Sound` → `ISoundEngine` → `OpenAlSoundEngine`). Its additions are at the edges: the `AudioBagLoader` package loader lets the VFS mount legacy audio archives, and the `SoundAnnouncement`, `AmbientSoundCA`, `AnnounceOnCreation`, and `AttackSoundsCA` traits provide extra sound trigger behaviors with fog control, armament filtering, and initial/final sounds.

# Chapter 5.2 — Spatial Sound Attenuation (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_05_Chapter_02_Spatial_Attenuation}

## Purpose

[Spatial attenuation](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) makes world sounds feel as if they originate from places on the battlefield. A tank firing near the camera is loud; a distant explosion is quiet. OpenRA delegates this to OpenAL, feeding it source positions and a listener position that tracks the camera. The Cameo mod uses the upstream spatial attenuation unchanged; it does not add a custom sound engine or alter OpenAL's distance model. This chapter explains how positions flow from the simulation to OpenAL, the OpenAL attenuation model, the tuning constants OpenRA uses, and how Cameo's sound-specific traits interact with that pipeline.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain how spatial attenuation makes world sounds feel positioned in the battlefield.
- Describe how the listener position follows the camera and how source positions are set.
- Trace the data flow from a `WPos` to an OpenAL source position.
- Interpret OpenRA's OpenAL constants (reference distance, max distance, listener Z offset).
- Explain the inverse-distance attenuation model used by OpenAL.
- Implement moving sounds and per-sound volume modifiers correctly.
- Recognize Cameo-specific sound traits that pass world positions into the audio system.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_02_Spatial_Attenuation-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Game/Game.cs` | Calls `Sound.SetListenerPosition(worldRenderer.Viewport.CenterPosition)` once per render frame. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Sound/Sound.cs` | `SetListenerPosition`, `Play(..., WPos pos)`, `SetPosition(ISound, WPos)`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Sound/SoundDevice.cs` | `ISoundEngine` interface methods for listener position and source position. |
| `OpenRA.Platforms.Default/OpenAlSoundEngine.cs` | OpenAL implementation: `SetListenerPosition`, `OpenAlSound` constructor, `SetSoundPosition`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/WorldRenderer.cs` | Provides `Viewport.CenterPosition` for the listener. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AmbientSoundCA.cs` | Cameo ambient-loop trait that positions and moves sounds with an actor. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AttackSoundsCA.cs` | Cameo attack-sound trait that fires world-positioned sounds by armament. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/SoundAnnouncement.cs` | Cameo trait that plays a sound when enabled, optionally positioned at the actor. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AnnounceOnCreation.cs` | Cameo trait that plays a player notification on actor creation (non-positional). |

The engine paths above are relative to the OpenRA engine checkout used by the Cameo mod; the Cameo mod does not modify these files.

## Architecture

### Listener follows the camera

```
[Game loop] -> [WorldRenderer.Viewport.CenterPosition] -> [Sound.SetListenerPosition] -> [OpenAL listener]
```

Once per frame, the main loop in `OpenRA.Game/Game.cs` sets the listener to the center of the [viewport](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary):

```csharp
Sound.SetListenerPosition(worldRenderer.Viewport.CenterPosition);
```

World sounds that are played with a `WPos` argument are automatically placed at their source position. OpenAL then computes the gain based on the distance between the source and the listener.

### UI sounds vs world sounds

UI sounds are played with `headRelative: true`. OpenAL treats them as attached to the listener, so they are not attenuated by distance. World sounds use `headRelative: false` and are positioned in the world. The `SoundType` enum (`UI` or `World`) is used by `Sound.Play` to suppress world sounds when the user disables them, but it does not affect attenuation directly.

### Moving sounds
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_02_Spatial_Attenuation-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


A sound that has already started can be moved by calling `Sound.SetPosition(ISound, WPos)`. This updates the source's OpenAL `AL_POSITION` while the sound is playing. This is used for continuous sounds attached to moving actors, such as sirens or long-running ambient loops.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Playing a positioned sound

```csharp
public ISound Play(SoundType type, string name, WPos pos) { return Play(type, null, name, false, pos, 1f); }
```

The public overload passes `headRelative: false` and the world position to the internal `Play` method, which calls `soundEngine.Play2D(sounds[name], loop, headRelative, pos, volume, attenuateVolume: true)`.

### Inside OpenAL

`OpenAlSoundEngine.Play2D` obtains a source from the pool, fills a `PoolSlot` with position and metadata, and constructs an `OpenAlSound`:

```csharp
slot.Sound = new OpenAlSound(source, loop, relative, pos, volume * atten, alSoundSource.SampleRate, alSoundSource.Buffer);
```

The `OpenAlSound` constructor sets the OpenAL source parameters:

```csharp
AL10.alSourcef(source, AL10.AL_PITCH, 1f);
AL10.alSource3f(source, AL10.AL_POSITION, pos.X, pos.Y, pos.Z);
AL10.alSource3f(source, AL10.AL_VELOCITY, 0f, 0f, 0f);
AL10.alSourcei(source, AL10.AL_LOOPING, looping ? 1 : 0);
AL10.alSourcei(source, AL10.AL_SOURCE_RELATIVE, relative ? 1 : 0);
AL10.alSourcef(source, AL10.AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE, 6826);
AL10.alSourcef(source, AL10.AL_MAX_DISTANCE, 136533);
```

After the source is configured, `AL10.alSourcePlay(source)` starts playback.

### Listener setup
![Configuration (yaml) diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_02_Spatial_Attenuation-annotated-yaml-snippet-diagram-showing-the-key-fields-and-ho-6a1b98.svg)


`OpenAlSoundEngine.SetListenerPosition` moves the listener slightly above the ground plane and sets the world-to-meter scale:

```csharp
public void SetListenerPosition(WPos position)
{
    AL10.alListener3f(AL10.AL_POSITION, position.X, position.Y, position.Z + 2133);

    var orientation = new[] { 0f, 0f, 1f, 0f, -1f, 0f };
    AL10.alListenerfv(AL10.AL_ORIENTATION, orientation);
    AL10.alListenerf(EFX.AL_METERS_PER_UNIT, .01f);
}
```

The `+2133` on the Z axis pulls the listener out of the isometric plane so that sounds directly under the camera center are not panned too sharply. The orientation vector is a fixed "look down, Y up" orientation. The scale `0.01` means one world unit is treated as one centimeter by OpenAL's distance model.

## Configuration (YAML)

Spatial attenuation is driven entirely by C# constants and OpenAL defaults; there are no mod-facing YAML knobs for the reference distance or max distance. However, the effective loudness of a sound is controlled by two YAML-level values:

- `VolumeModifier` on a `MusicInfo` or `SoundPool` entry.
- The `volumeModifier` argument passed by traits when they call `Game.Sound.Play`.

For example:

```yaml
Notifications:
    Explosion:
        VolumeModifier: 0.7
        Notifications: expl1, expl2
```

A trait can then call `Game.Sound.Play(SoundType.World, "Explosion", self.CenterPosition, volumeModifier)` to further scale the sound.

Cameo also exposes `SoundVolume` on weapon definitions to scale the report sound independently of the spatial attenuation:

```yaml
ConscriptAK47:
    SoundVolume: 0.5
    Report: conscriptak.wav
```

And `VolumeMultiplier` on `AmbientSoundCA` instances in actor rules:

```yaml
SomeAmbientActor:
    AmbientSoundCA:
        SoundFiles: ambience1.wav
        VolumeMultiplier: 2
```

Music tracks in `mods/cameo/music.yaml` use the upstream `VolumeModifier` field:

```yaml
Music:
    SomeTrack:
        Filename: some_track.ogg
        VolumeModifier: 0.9
```

## Cameo-specific sound spatialization

Cameo does not change the upstream spatial attenuation implementation. It uses the same `OpenAL` inverse-distance model, the same reference distance, max distance, and listener Z offset, and the same source-pool throttling. The spatial differences are all in the trait layer: some Cameo sound traits pass world positions to `Game.Sound.Play`, while others remain head-relative.

### Custom sound traits that reference world position

- **`AmbientSoundCA`** (`OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AmbientSoundCA.cs`) — plays a looping or interval sound at the actor position. When the actor occupies space, it calls `Game.Sound.Play(SoundType.World, sound, self.CenterPosition, Info.VolumeMultiplier)` or `Game.Sound.PlayLooped(SoundType.World, sound, cachedPosition)`. Every tick it compares the current `self.CenterPosition` to a cached position and calls `ISound.SetPosition(pos)` to keep the sound moving with the actor.
- **`AttackSoundsCA`** (`OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AttackSoundsCA.cs`) — plays a sound during attack preparation or the attack itself. It calls `Game.Sound.Play(SoundType.World, info.Sounds, self.World, self.CenterPosition)`, so the sound is positioned at the attacker and attenuated by distance from the camera.
- **`SoundAnnouncement`** (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/SoundAnnouncement.cs`) — plays a sound when the trait is enabled. If the actor occupies space, it calls the positioned overload `Game.Sound.Play(SoundType.World, sound, self.CenterPosition, volume)`; otherwise it falls back to the non-positioned overload `Game.Sound.Play(SoundType.World, sound, volume)`, which is head-relative and therefore not spatially attenuated.

### Traits that are not spatially positioned

- **`AnnounceOnCreation`** (`OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AnnounceOnCreation.cs`) — plays a notification through `Game.Sound.PlayNotification(...)`. Notifications are head-relative UI-style speech, so they are not affected by spatial attenuation.

### Additional Cameo YAML fields

- **`AudibleThroughFog`** — present on `AmbientSoundCA`, `AttackSoundsCA`, and `SoundAnnouncement`. This is a visibility filter, not an attenuation control; it decides whether the sound may start while the actor is under shroud or fog. Once the sound is started, normal OpenAL distance attenuation still applies.
- **`SoundVolume`** — weapon-level field used in `mods/cameo/weapons/*.yaml` to scale the weapon's `Report` sound.
- **`VolumeMultiplier`** — field on `AmbientSoundCA` rule entries in `mods/cameo/rules/*.yaml` to scale ambient sound volume.
- **`VolumeModifier`** — standard field on music tracks in `mods/cameo/music.yaml`.

Because there is no significant divergence in the core spatialization engine, the Cameo mod relies entirely on the upstream behavior described in the rest of this chapter. For a deeper look at the audio architecture, see [Part 5.1 — Audio Architecture](#file-chapters-Part_05_Chapter_01_Audio_Architecture).

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_02_Spatial_Attenuation-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:** [Part 5.1 — Audio Architecture](#file-chapters-Part_05_Chapter_01_Audio_Architecture), [Part 4.2 — WorldRenderer](#file-chapters-Part_04_Chapter_02_WorldRenderer), [Part 1.4 — Math, Coordinates, and Determinism](#file-chapters-Part_01_Chapter_04_Math).
- **Used by:** [Part 5.4 — Sound Triggers](#file-chapters-Part_05_Chapter_04_Sound_Triggers), Part 8 (bot notifications), and any trait that plays a world sound.

## Algorithms

### OpenAL inverse-distance attenuation

With the default OpenAL distance model (inverse distance clamped), source gain is:

```
distance = max(distance, AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE)
gain = AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE / (AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE + AL_ROLLOFF_FACTOR * (distance - AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE))
gain = clamp(gain, 0.0, 1.0)
```

OpenRA does not set `AL_ROLLOFF_FACTOR`, so it defaults to `1.0`, producing standard inverse-distance rolloff. The gain is clamped so that sounds beyond `AL_MAX_DISTANCE` become silent and sounds at or within `AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE` are at full volume.

### OpenRA constants in world units

Because `AL_METERS_PER_UNIT = 0.01`, the OpenAL constants translate to world units as follows:

- `AL_REFERENCE_DISTANCE = 6826` world units (~68.3 meters).
- `AL_MAX_DISTANCE = 136533` world units (~1365 meters).
- Listener Z offset = 2133 world units (~21 meters above the ground plane).
- `GroupDistance = 2730` world units used for the instance-throttling heuristic.

These values were chosen so that the isometric camera (typically looking down at an angle) hears nearby combat clearly and distant combat fades naturally.

### Instance throttling and volume

Before the source is allocated, `OpenAlSoundEngine.Play2D` computes an additional attenuation factor based on how many sources are currently active:

```csharp
atten = 0.66f * ((PoolSize - activeCount * 0.5f) / PoolSize);
```

This is multiplied by the requested volume. As the pool fills, all new sounds become slightly quieter to reduce the overall perceived volume and prevent clipping. This is independent of spatial distance attenuation.

### Per-frame capping

The same sound source starting too many times within 5 frames and within `GroupDistanceSqr` (2730 world units) is dropped entirely:

```csharp
if (++instances == MaxInstancesPerFrame)
    return null;
```

This prevents rapid-fire sounds (e.g., many machine guns from a cluster of infantry) from overwhelming the audio pipeline.

### Moving a playing sound
![Extension points diagram](images/Part_05_Chapter_02_Spatial_Attenuation-extension-hook-diagram-showing-the-interface-s-to-implement-b4a27b.svg)


`OpenAlSound.SetPosition` updates `AL_POSITION` directly:

```csharp
public void SetPosition(WPos pos)
{
    if (done)
        return;

    AL10.alSource3f(Source, AL10.AL_POSITION, pos.X, pos.Y, pos.Z);
}
```

This is the only way to keep a long sound spatially accurate as its source actor moves.

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **Listener Z offset:** the `+2133` offset means sounds very far above or below the listener plane can behave unexpectedly. Always pass a grounded `WPos` (e.g., `self.CenterPosition` or `self.World.Map.CenterOfCell(cell)`) for world sounds.
- **Source-relative flag:** `headRelative: true` disables spatialization entirely. Do not accidentally pass `false` for UI sounds.
- **Max distance:** sounds beyond 136533 world units will be silent. This is rarely hit on typical maps, but very large custom maps should keep this in mind.
- **Pool exhaustion:** if the source pool is exhausted, the sound is simply dropped. There is no queue; the gameplay is unaffected.
- **Determinism:** attenuation is client-side. The simulation does not know whether a sound was played or how loud it was. Never use audio state for gameplay logic.
- **Volume hierarchy:** the final gain is the product of the source volume, the `volumeModifier`, the OpenAL distance gain, and the global `AL_GAIN` listener gain. Changing any one changes the final loudness.
- **Cameo trait visibility:** `AudibleThroughFog` controls whether a sound may start under the fog, not how loud it is. Do not confuse it with a volume or attenuation setting.

## Summary

This chapter explains how OpenRA positions world sounds in 3D space through OpenAL spatial attenuation, from source and listener positions to the inverse-distance model and tuning constants. The Cameo mod inherits this behavior unchanged; its only spatial additions are a few custom traits that pass actor positions into the existing `Game.Sound` API and YAML fields that scale per-sound or per-music volume.

## References

- `OpenRA.Game/Game.cs` — listener position update in the main loop.
- `OpenRA.Game/Sound/Sound.cs` — `SetListenerPosition`, `Play` with position, `SetPosition`.
- `OpenRA.Game/Sound/SoundDevice.cs` — `ISoundEngine` interface.
- `OpenRA.Platforms.Default/OpenAlSoundEngine.cs` — `SetListenerPosition`, `Play2D`, `OpenAlSound`, source pool.
- `OpenRA.Platforms.Default/DummySoundEngine.cs` — no-op backend for headless/muted mode.
- `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/WorldRenderer.cs` — viewport and camera position.
- `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AmbientSoundCA.cs` — Cameo ambient sound trait with position updates.
- `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AttackSoundsCA.cs` — Cameo attack sound trait positioned at the attacker.
- `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/SoundAnnouncement.cs` — Cameo sound announcement trait with optional world positioning.
- `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/Sound/AnnounceOnCreation.cs` — Cameo creation notification trait (non-positional).
- `mods/cameo/weapons/*.yaml` — `SoundVolume` examples for weapon reports.
- `mods/cameo/music.yaml` — `VolumeModifier` examples for music tracks.
