## Algorithms

### Package format detection

`OpenPackage` resolves a path and tries to parse it as a package:

```csharp
public IReadOnlyPackage OpenPackage(string filename)
{
    var resolvedPath = Platform.ResolvePath(filename);
    if (!resolvedPath.Contains('|') && Directory.Exists(resolvedPath))
        return new Folder(resolvedPath);

    if (TryGetPackageContaining(filename, out var parent, out var subPath))
        return parent.OpenPackage(subPath, this);

    var stream = Open(filename);
    if (TryParsePackage(stream, filename, out var package))
        return package;

    stream.Dispose();
    return null;
}
```

Directories are opened as `Folder` packages. Files are opened as streams and passed to each package loader.

### Loader chain

```csharp
public bool TryParsePackage(Stream stream, string filename, out IReadOnlyPackage package)
{
    package = null;
    foreach (var packageLoader in packageLoaders)
        if (packageLoader.TryParsePackage(stream, filename, this, out package))
            return true;

    return false;
}
```

A loader that recognizes the stream takes ownership of it. If no loader recognizes the stream, the caller must dispose it.

### File index priority

When a package is mounted, its contents are added to the file index. Re-mounting the same package moves it to the end of the list for each file, increasing its priority. The `GetFromCache` method uses `LastOrDefault` to select the highest-priority package.

### Case insensitivity
![Extension points diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_03_VFS-extension-hook-diagram-showing-the-interface-s-to-implement-b4a27b.svg)


`ResolveCaseInsensitivePath` normalizes paths to support case-insensitive lookups. This is important because many legacy game archives store filenames in uppercase while mod YAML uses lowercase.

## Extension Points

### Add a new package format

Implement `IPackageLoader` and a matching `IReadOnlyPackage` class. Register the format name in the mod manifest under `PackageFormats`. The loader must:

- Recognize the stream format.
- Take ownership of the stream on success.
- Reset the stream position on failure.

### Add custom mount logic

Mods can call `FileSystem.Mount(package, name)` at runtime to add explicit mounts. This is used by maps and dynamic asset loading.

### Implement a writable package
![Common pitfalls  guardrails diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_03_VFS-checklist-infographic-style-diagram-summarizing-the-top-pitf-fb069e.svg)


Implement `IReadWritePackage` to support modifying package contents. This is used by the map editor when saving maps.

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **Stream ownership:** a package loader must dispose the stream when it takes ownership, or reset the stream position when it does not. Leaked streams can cause file locks or memory leaks.
- **Mount order:** because later mounts override earlier ones, the manifest order matters. Put optional or mod-specific packages after the base packages.
- **Optional packages:** use the `~` prefix for packages that may not exist. The VFS will ignore the mount if the package is missing.
- **Mod references:** mod packages referenced with `$` are owned by the mod manager and are not disposed by the VFS.
- **Explicit mounts:** the `|` syntax is powerful but can fail silently if the explicit mount name is misspelled.
- **Case sensitivity:** Windows and Linux handle case differently. Use the VFS `Exists` and `TryOpen` methods rather than direct file system checks.
- **Map package lifecycle:** map packages are mounted when the map loads and unmounted when the world is disposed. Do not hold streams from map packages after the map is unloaded.
- **Bag index pairing:** a `.bag` file must be accompanied by its `.idx` sibling with the same base name. If the index is missing or misnamed, `AudioBagLoader` will reject the archive and the file will not be readable.
- **Bag audio format flags:** the `BagFile` entry `Flags` value determines whether the loader emits a PCM or IMA ADPCM WAV header. If the flags are unrecognized, the returned stream may be invalid for the sound loader.

If any of the concepts above feel unclear, review the relevant section before continuing. For source files and further reading, see the References section.

# Chapter 6.4 — Crypto and Security (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto}

## Purpose

Cameo, as an OpenRA-based mod, inherits the upstream OpenRA cryptographic utilities for player authentication, server verification, and replay/game-save integrity. The operations are deliberately simple: RSA public-key signing, SHA1 hashing, and PEM key encoding. This chapter covers the `CryptoUtil` class and how the player profile system uses these primitives, with notes on where Cameo diverges (or does not diverge) from upstream.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the cryptographic primitives used by OpenRA (RSA, SHA1, PEM).
- Describe how player identity is derived from a public key fingerprint.
- Trace the authentication flow from handshake to signature verification.
- Encode and decode PEM public keys and compute SHA1 fingerprints.
- Configure PlayerDatabase and ServerSettings authentication options.
- Recognize the security limitations of SHA1 and the appropriate use cases for crypto in OpenRA.
- Identify Cameo-specific file-loading behavior and its integrity guarantees.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Game/CryptoUtil.cs` | RSA key encoding/decoding, signing, verification, SHA1 hashing, PEM helpers. |
| `OpenRA.Game/PlayerProfile.cs` | Player profile data including fingerprint, public key, and badges. |
| `OpenRA.Game/PlayerDatabase.cs` | Loads player badges and profile data from the forum server. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Network/Handshake.cs` | Server handshake that exchanges public keys and signatures. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Network/Session.cs` | Lobby session containing client public keys and fingerprints. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Server/Server.cs` | Server-side validation of signed client data. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Network/GameServer.cs` | Game server listing with optional fingerprint/signature fields. |
| `OpenRA.Test/OpenRA.Game/Sha1Tests.cs` | Unit tests for SHA1 hashing. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/FileSystem/BagFile.cs` | Cameo-specific `.bag`/`.idx` audio package loader. |
| `mods/cameo/mod.yaml` | Cameo manifest that mounts `ContentPacks` and registers `AudioBag`. |
| `mods/cameo/ContentPacks/TiberianDawn/GDI/content.yaml` | Example optional content pack manifest. |
| `mods/cameo-content/installer/soviet95.yaml` | Example installer manifest with SHA1 `IDFiles` hashes. |

## Architecture

### Crypto primitives

`CryptoUtil` is a static helper class with three categories of functions:

1. **Key encoding** — `EncodePEMPublicKey`, `DecodePEMPublicKey`, `PublicKeyFingerprint`.
2. **Signing/verification** — `Sign`, `VerifySignature` using RSA with SHA1.
3. **Hashing** — `SHA1Hash` for streams, byte arrays, and strings.

All cryptographic operations use .NET's `RSACryptoServiceProvider` with SHA1.

### Player identity

Player identity is based on an RSA public key. The **fingerprint** of a key is the SHA1 hash of the key's modulus and exponent bytes:

```csharp
public static string PublicKeyFingerprint(RSAParameters parameters)
{
    return SHA1Hash(parameters.Modulus.Append(parameters.Exponent).ToArray());
}
```

This fingerprint is used to identify players consistently across sessions and to verify that a player's public key has not changed.

### Authentication flow
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


1. A player generates or loads an RSA key pair.
2. The client sends the public key to the server during the handshake.
3. The server sends a challenge or a session token.
4. The client signs the challenge with its private key and sends the signature back.
5. The server verifies the signature against the public key and fingerprint.
6. The server can then look up the player's profile in the forum database using the fingerprint.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### RSA key encoding

Public keys are exchanged in PEM format. `EncodePEMPublicKey` builds an ASN.1 DER structure and base64-encodes it with PEM header/footer:

```csharp
public static string EncodePEMPublicKey(RSAParameters parameters)
{
    var data = Convert.ToBase64String(EncodePublicKey(parameters));
    var output = new StringBuilder();
    output.AppendLine("-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----");
    for (var i = 0; i < data.Length; i += 64)
        output.AppendLine(data.Substring(i, Math.Min(64, data.Length - i)));
    output.Append("-----END PUBLIC KEY-----");

    return output.ToString();
}
```

`DecodePEMPublicKey` parses the ASN.1 structure to extract the modulus and exponent.

### Signing data

```csharp
public static string Sign(RSAParameters parameters, byte[] data)
{
    using (var rsa = new RSACryptoServiceProvider())
    {
        rsa.ImportParameters(parameters);
        return Convert.ToBase64String(rsa.SignHash(SHA1.HashData(data), CryptoConfig.MapNameToOID("SHA1")));
    }
}
```

The data is first SHA1-hashed, then signed with RSA PKCS#1 v1.5.

### Verifying a signature

```csharp
public static bool VerifySignature(RSAParameters parameters, byte[] data, string signature)
{
    using (var rsa = new RSACryptoServiceProvider())
    {
        rsa.ImportParameters(parameters);
        return rsa.VerifyHash(SHA1.HashData(data), CryptoConfig.MapNameToOID("SHA1"), Convert.FromBase64String(signature));
    }
}
```

### SHA1 hashing

```csharp
public static string SHA1Hash(byte[] data)
{
    return ToHex(SHA1.HashData(data), true);
}
```

Hashes are returned as lowercase hex strings.

### Player profile lookup
![Configuration (yaml) diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto-annotated-yaml-snippet-diagram-showing-the-key-fields-and-ho-6a1b98.svg)


`PlayerProfile` stores the fingerprint and public key for an authenticated player. `PlayerDatabase` loads additional profile data (name, rank, badges) from the OpenRA forum server. Badges are loaded asynchronously and cached in a sprite sheet.

## Configuration (YAML)

### Player database endpoint

The `PlayerDatabase` URL is configured in the mod's global mod data:

```yaml
PlayerDatabase:
    Profile: https://forum.openra.net/openra/info/
    IconSize: 24
```

### Server authentication

Server settings in `ServerSettings` control whether authentication is required:

```yaml
ServerSettings:
    RequireAuthentication: false
    EnableGeoIP: true
    ...
```

### Cameo manifest

The Cameo `mod.yaml` registers the package formats and mounts the optional `ContentPacks` package:

```yaml
PackageFormats: Mix, AudioBag, D2kSoundResources
...
FileSystem: DefaultFileSystem
    Packages:
        ...
        cameo|ContentPacks: ContentPacks
        ...
        ~cameo|bits/ra2/audio.bag
```

The `AudioBag` loader is provided by `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/FileSystem/BagFile.cs`. The `ContentPacks` directory is exposed as a mod package so optional sub-factions can be loaded as part of the normal file system.

## Cameo Security Considerations

This section documents how Cameo extends (or does not extend) the upstream crypto and security model.

### No custom crypto code in the mod

A search of `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` and `OpenRA.Mods.CA` for `CryptoUtil`, `RSACryptoServiceProvider`, `SHA1`, `VerifySignature`, `PublicKey`, `Fingerprint`, `PlayerDatabase`, `PlayerProfile`, and `Authentication` found no custom crypto, signing, or player-authentication implementations. Cameo therefore relies entirely on the upstream OpenRA engine for the cryptographic operations described in the sections above.

### `.bag` / `.idx` loading

The only Cameo-specific file-loading code with security relevance is `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/FileSystem/BagFile.cs`. The `AudioBagLoader` accepts a file only if its name ends with `.bag`:

```csharp
bool IPackageLoader.TryParsePackage(Stream s, string filename, FS context, out IReadOnlyPackage package)
{
    if (!filename.EndsWith(".bag", StringComparison.InvariantCultureIgnoreCase))
    {
        package = null;
        return false;
    }

    // A bag file is always accompanied with an .idx counterpart
    var indexFilename = Path.ChangeExtension(filename, ".idx");
    List<IdxEntry> entries = null;

    try
    {
        using (var indexStream = context.Open(indexFilename))
            entries = new IdxReader(indexStream).Entries;
    }
    catch
    {
        package = null;
        return false;
    }

    package = new BagFile(s, entries, filename);
    return true;
}
```

The loader then opens the sibling `.idx` file, parses the index entries, and returns a `BagFile` that streams raw audio data prefixed with a synthesized WAV header. There is **no checksum, signature, or length validation** beyond the index entries themselves. The loader trusts the `.idx` file to describe the correct offsets and lengths. A mismatched or corrupt `.idx` will cause wrong audio data to be served or may crash the stream consumer.

### `ContentPacks`

The optional `ContentPacks` directory is mounted in `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`:

```yaml
cameo|ContentPacks: ContentPacks
```

The example `mods/cameo/ContentPacks/TiberianDawn/GDI/content.yaml` references additional rules and translation files:

```yaml
Rules:
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/faction.yaml
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/buildings.yaml
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/infantry.yaml
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/vehicles.yaml
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/aircraft.yaml
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/naval.yaml
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/yaml/upgrades.yaml

FluentMessages:
    ContentPacks|TiberianDawn/GDI/translations/en.ftl
```

This file is loaded as a normal mod package through the engine's file system. The content packs are **not signed or hash-verified** at runtime; the engine treats them the same as any other mod package.

### Integrity verification for original assets

The only hash verification present in the Cameo source is in the content installer manifests under `mods/cameo-content/installer/*.yaml`. For example, `mods/cameo-content/installer/soviet95.yaml` lists `IDFiles` with SHA1 digests:

```yaml
soviet: Red Alert 95 (Soviet Disc, English)
    IDFiles:
        MAIN.MIX: 9d108f18560716b684ab8b1da42cc7f3d1b52519
            Length: 4096
        INSTALL/REDALERT.MIX: 0e58f4b54f44f6cd29fecf8cf379d33cf2d4caef
```

The upstream engine validates these with `CryptoUtil.SHA1Hash` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Installer/InstallerUtils.cs` before extracting assets. This only protects the *source* installation files; it does not verify the extracted files at runtime.

### Network and authentication differences

Neither `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` nor `OpenRA.Mods.CA` implement custom handshakes, server connection logic, order encryption, or additional authentication. Custom order generators (e.g., `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Orders/CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase.cs`) and custom UI widgets use the standard engine order and session APIs. Server settings, player fingerprints, and authentication flow are handled by the upstream engine classes (`OpenRA.Game/Network/Handshake.cs`, `OpenRA.Game/Network/Session.cs`, `OpenRA.Game/Server/Server.cs`).

### Conclusion

Cameo has **no significant divergence** from upstream OpenRA cryptographic or security behavior. For the engine-side security model, see the upstream OpenRA Manual Chapter 6.4 and [Part 9.2 — Server and Connection Layer](#file-chapters-Part_09_Chapter_02_Server_Connection).

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:** [Part 2.1 — MiniYaml Parser](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_01_MiniYaml), [Part 3.1 — Mod SDK and Project Structure](#file-chapters-Part_03_Chapter_01_Mod_SDK), [Part 6.3 — Virtual File System](#file-chapters-Part_06_Chapter_03_VFS), [Part 4.3 — Widgets and Chrome](#file-chapters-Part_04_Chapter_03_Widgets).
- **Used by:** [Part 9.2 — Server and Connection Layer](#file-chapters-Part_09_Chapter_02_Server_Connection), [Part 10.2 — Online Services and References](#file-chapters-Part_10_Chapter_02_Online_References).

## Algorithms

### ASN.1 DER encoding

`EncodePublicKey` manually constructs a DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo structure:

1. Outer `SEQUENCE`.
2. Algorithm identifier `SEQUENCE` with the RSA OID header.
3. `BIT STRING` containing the inner `SEQUENCE`.
4. Inner `SEQUENCE` with two `INTEGER`s: modulus and exponent.

The modulus and exponent are padded with a leading zero byte to prevent them from being interpreted as negative numbers in ASN.1 INTEGER encoding.

### TLV length encoding

```csharp
static void WriteTLVLength(BinaryWriter writer, int length)
{
    if (length < 0x80)
        writer.Write((byte)length);
    else
    {
        var lengthBytes = BitConverter.GetBytes(length).Reverse().SkipWhile(b => b == 0).ToArray();
        writer.Write((byte)(0x80 | lengthBytes.Length));
        writer.Write(lengthBytes);
    }
}
```

This implements ASN.1 length encoding for DER.

### Fingerprint computation
![Extension points diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto-extension-hook-diagram-showing-the-interface-s-to-implement-b4a27b.svg)


The public key fingerprint is simply the SHA1 of the concatenated modulus and exponent bytes:

```csharp
return SHA1Hash(parameters.Modulus.Append(parameters.Exponent).ToArray());
```

This is deterministic and stable, so the same key always produces the same fingerprint.

## Extension Points

### Add a new hash algorithm

Add a new helper method to `CryptoUtil`. If the hash is used for sync or file identity, ensure it is deterministic and consistent across platforms.

### Custom authentication providers

`PlayerDatabase` is a global mod data object. A custom mod could replace it with a subclass that loads profiles from a different service.

### Server-side verification
![Common pitfalls  guardrails diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_04_Crypto-checklist-infographic-style-diagram-summarizing-the-top-pitf-fb069e.svg)


Server traits can use `CryptoUtil.VerifySignature` to validate signed orders or admin commands. This is how vote-kick and authentication commands are verified.

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **SHA1 is not collision-resistant:** while OpenRA uses SHA1 for fingerprints and signatures, it is not suitable for new security-critical use cases. The existing use is acceptable because the data is not high-value.
- **RSA key size:** `RSACryptoServiceProvider` defaults to a 1024-bit key on older .NET versions. Ensure keys are large enough for your security needs.
- **Private key storage:** private keys are stored on the client machine. They must be protected from unauthorized access by the operating system.
- **Signature verification:** always verify signatures before trusting data from the network. The server does this during authentication.
- **Badges async loading:** badges are loaded asynchronously from the network. UI code must handle the case where a badge is not yet available.
- **Do not use crypto for gameplay:** cryptographic operations are not deterministic enough for the simulation. Never include signature verification or hash results in sync state.
- **Cameo `.idx` trust:** the `AudioBagLoader` trusts the contents of the paired `.idx` file. Do not treat `.bag`/`.idx` pairs as tamper-proof; they are not signed or hashed at runtime.
- **ContentPacks are not authenticated:** optional content packs are loaded through the normal VFS and are not validated beyond standard package loading.

## What to read next

- [Part 6.3 — Virtual File System](#file-chapters-Part_06_Chapter_03_VFS) for how badge textures, `ContentPacks`, and `.bag` files are mounted and loaded.
- [Part 9.2 — Server and Connection Layer](#file-chapters-Part_09_Chapter_02_Server_Connection) for the handshake that uses the crypto primitives covered here.
- [Part 10.2 — Online Services and References](#file-chapters-Part_10_Chapter_02_Online_References) for the online-services ecosystem that player authentication plugs into.

## Summary

This chapter explains the cryptographic utilities OpenRA uses for player authentication, server verification, and replay/game-save integrity, and how Cameo reuses them without modification.

After reading this chapter, you should be able to:

- **Key encoding** — `EncodePEMPublicKey`, `DecodePEMPublicKey`, `PublicKeyFingerprint`.
- **Signing/verification** — `Sign`, `VerifySignature` using RSA with SHA1.
- **Hashing** — `SHA1Hash` for streams, byte arrays, and strings.
- **Cameo-specific loading** — `AudioBagLoader` and `.bag`/`.idx` behavior; `ContentPacks` are not authenticated; installer hashes are only for source assets.

If any of the concepts above feel unclear, review the relevant section before continuing. For source files and further reading, see the References section.

# Chapter 6.5 — Asset Loaders (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_06_Chapter_05_Asset_Loaders}

## Purpose

OpenRA assets come in many formats: legacy Westwood [sprites](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) (SHP/TMP), audio (AUD/VOC/WAV/OGG/MP3), video (VQA), and modern formats (PNG). The engine uses a plugin-style loader system so each format can be parsed independently. This chapter covers the loader interfaces for sprites, [sequences](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary), audio, and video, and how they are registered and invoked, with a focus on the Cameo mod's custom asset loaders.

The Cameo mod adds two major custom asset loaders:

- **`CameoSpriteSequence`** / **`CameoSpriteSequenceLoader`** — extends the upstream `ClassicSpriteSequence` with tileset-specific filename overrides, remap colors, and fog/shadow conversion for R8 sprites.
- **`AudioBagLoader`** / **`BagFile`** — implements `IPackageLoader` for legacy audio BAG archives (used by some Command & Conquer titles), allowing the VFS to mount `.bag`/`.idx` pairs and stream WAV/ADPCM data on demand.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the loader chain architecture for sprites, sequences, audio, and video.
- Describe the interfaces `ISpriteLoader`, `ISpriteSequenceLoader`, `ISoundLoader`, and `IVideoLoader`.
- Trace the sprite pipeline from raw file to GPU sheet.
- Configure asset loaders in the mod manifest.
- Implement a new loader for a custom asset format.
- Explain how sprite sequences and sheet packing work.
- Recognize Cameo-specific loaders (`CameoSpriteSequenceLoader`, `AudioBagLoader`) and how they are registered in `mod.yaml`.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_05_Asset_Loaders-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteLoader.cs` | `ISpriteLoader`, `ISpriteFrame`, `FrameCache`, `FrameLoader`, `SpriteFrameType`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SequenceSet.cs` | `ISpriteSequence`, `ISpriteSequenceLoader`, `SequenceSet`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteCache.cs` | Caches sprite frames and packs them into GPU sheets. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Sound/Sound.cs` | `ISoundLoader`, `ISoundFormat`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/VideoLoader.cs` | `IVideoLoader`, `IVideo`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/ModData.cs` | Holds `SpriteLoaders`, `SpriteSequenceLoader`, `SoundLoaders`, `VideoLoaders`, and `PackageLoaders`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/SpriteLoaders/*.cs` | Common sprite loaders (Png, Shp, ShpTS, Tmp, etc.). |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/AudioLoaders/*.cs` | Common audio loaders (Wav, Ogg, Mp3). |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/AudioLoaders/VocLoader.cs` | Westwood VOC loader. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/VideoLoaders/VqaLoader.cs` | Westwood VQA video loader. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/Sprite.cs` | In-memory sprite reference. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Graphics/Sheet.cs` | GPU texture sheet. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Graphics/CameoSpriteSequence.cs` | Cameo custom sprite sequence with tileset-specific variants, remap, and fog conversion. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/FileSystem/BagFile.cs` | `AudioBagLoader` and `BagFile` package loader for legacy `.bag`/`.idx` audio archives. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/FileFormats/IdxReader.cs` | Index reader used by `AudioBagLoader` to parse `.idx` files. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.D2k/SpriteLoaders/R8Loader.cs` | R8 sprite loader; provides `RemappableFrame` used by `CameoSpriteSequence`. |

## Architecture

### Loader chains

Each asset category has a loader chain:

```
[File request] -> [FrameLoader/SoundLoader/VideoLoader] -> tries each ISpriteLoader/ISoundLoader/IVideoLoader -> returns parsed asset
```

`ModData` stores the arrays of loaders discovered from the mod manifest. When an asset is requested, the engine tries each loader in order until one succeeds.

### Sprite pipeline

```
[Sprite file] -> [ISpriteLoader] -> [ISpriteFrame[]] -> [SpriteCache] -> [Sheet] -> [Sprite]
```

A sprite loader reads the raw file and produces one or more `ISpriteFrame` objects. The `SpriteCache` reserves space on GPU sheets and, when `LoadSprites` is called, uploads the frames and creates `Sprite` objects.

### Sequence pipeline

```
[sequences/*.yaml] -> [ISpriteSequenceLoader] -> [ISpriteSequence dictionary] -> [SpriteCache] -> resolved sprites
```

Sequences are YAML definitions that describe how a sprite file is sliced into frames, facings, and animations. The `ISpriteSequenceLoader` parses the YAML and creates `ISpriteSequence` objects. Sequences are resolved lazily through the `SpriteCache`.

### Audio pipeline

```
[audio file] -> [ISoundLoader] -> [ISoundFormat] -> [ISoundEngine] -> [ISoundSource]
```

Audio loaders parse the file and expose a PCM stream. The sound engine then creates a source from the PCM data.

### Video pipeline
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_05_Asset_Loaders-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


```
[video file] -> [IVideoLoader] -> [IVideo] -> [renderer] + [sound engine]
```

Video loaders decode frames and audio. The renderer displays frames, and the sound engine plays the audio track.

### Cameo-specific sprite sequence loader

`CameoSpriteSequenceLoader` extends `DefaultSpriteSequenceLoader` and creates `CameoSpriteSequence` instances instead of `ClassicSpriteSequence` instances. The mod manifest selects this loader via:

```yaml
SpriteSequenceFormat: CameoSpriteSequence
```

`CameoSpriteSequence` adds the following fields on top of the upstream `ClassicSpriteSequence` fields:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `Remap` | `Color` | Sets the player remap reference colour for `R8Loader.RemappableFrame`. |
| `UseShadow` | `bool` | Remaps embedded palette index 1 to shadow (default `true`). |
| `ConvertShroudToFog` | `bool` | Indicates that this is a fog sprite definition (default `false`). |
| `TilesetFilenames` | `Dictionary<string, string>` | Per-tileset filename override for `Filename`. |
| `TilesetFilenamesPattern` | `Dictionary<string, string>` | Per-tileset filename pattern override for `FilenamePattern`. |

The `ReserveSprites` method builds an `AdjustFrame` delegate that calls `R8Loader.RemappableFrame.WithSequenceFlags(useShadow, convertShroudToFog, remapColor)` when any of those flags is set. The `ParseFilenames` and `ParseCombineFilenames` overrides first check for a tileset-specific filename before falling back to the standard `Filename`/`FilenamePattern` logic.

### Cameo audio bag loader

`AudioBagLoader` implements `IPackageLoader` and is registered in the `Package` loaders list. It recognizes files ending in `.bag` and opens a matching `.idx` file via the VFS. The `IdxReader` parses the index into `IdxEntry` records, and the `BagFile` package serves each entry as a WAV stream.

`BagFile.GetStream` builds a WAV header on the fly:

- If the entry flags indicate PCM, it writes a standard PCM WAV header.
- If the flags indicate IMA ADPCM, it writes an IMA ADPCM WAV header with `fact` chunk information.

The body of the audio data is read from the original `.bag` stream through a `SegmentStream`, and the header and body are combined into a `MergedStream` so the sound loader sees a valid WAV file.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Loading sprite frames

```csharp
public static ISpriteFrame[] GetFrames(Stream stream, ISpriteLoader[] loaders, string filename, out TypeDictionary metadata)
{
    metadata = null;
    foreach (var loader in loaders)
        if (loader.TryParseSprite(stream, filename, out var frames, out metadata))
            return frames;

    return null;
}
```

The first loader that recognizes the file wins. `metadata` can contain format-specific data (e.g., embedded palettes).

### Sprite cache

`SpriteCache` reserves sprite slots on GPU sheets. It is created during `SequenceSet` construction and loaded after the world is ready:

```csharp
public void LoadSprites()
{
    SpriteCache.LoadReservations(modData);
    foreach (var sequences in images.Values)
        foreach (var sequence in sequences)
            sequence.Value.ResolveSprites(SpriteCache);
}
```

### Loading sequences

```csharp
IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ISpriteSequence>> Load(...)
{
    var nodes = MiniYaml.Load(fileSystem, modData.Manifest.Sequences, additionalSequences);
    var images = new Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ISpriteSequence>>();
    foreach (var node in nodes)
    {
        if (node.Key.StartsWith(ActorInfo.AbstractActorPrefix))
            continue;

        images[node.Key] = modData.SpriteSequenceLoader.ParseSequences(modData, TileSet, SpriteCache, node);
    }

    return images;
}
```

Each top-level YAML node is an "image" (e.g., `e1`, `tank`) that contains multiple named sequences (e.g., `idle`, `run`, `die`). With `CameoSpriteSequenceLoader`, `ParseSequences` creates `CameoSpriteSequence` instances that may use `TilesetFilenames` or `TilesetFilenamesPattern` to select a per-tileset sprite file.

### Loading audio

```csharp
T LoadSound<T>(string filename, Func<ISoundFormat, T> loadFormat)
{
    using (var stream = fileSystem.Open(filename))
    {
        foreach (var loader in loaders)
        {
            stream.Position = 0;
            if (loader.TryParseSound(stream, out var soundFormat))
            {
                var source = loadFormat(soundFormat);
                soundFormat.Dispose();
                return source;
            }
        }
    }

    throw new InvalidDataException(filename + " is not a valid sound file!");
}
```

For files inside a `.bag` archive, the VFS returns a `MergedStream` containing a synthetic WAV header followed by the raw audio data, so the upstream `WavLoader` or `AudLoader` can parse it normally.

### Loading video
![Configuration (yaml) diagram](images/Part_06_Chapter_05_Asset_Loaders-annotated-yaml-snippet-diagram-showing-the-key-fields-and-ho-6a1b98.svg)


```csharp
public static IVideo GetVideo(Stream stream, bool useFramePadding, IVideoLoader[] loaders)
{
    foreach (var loader in loaders)
        if (loader.TryParseVideo(stream, useFramePadding, out var video))
            return video;

    return null;
}
```

## Configuration (YAML)

### Loader registration

The mod manifest declares loaders for each asset type:

```yaml
Loaders:
    Sprite:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.SpriteLoaders.PngLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.SpriteLoaders.ShpLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.SpriteLoaders.ShpTSLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.SpriteLoaders.TmpLoader
    SpriteSequence:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.SpriteLoaders.DefaultSpriteSequenceLoader
    Sound:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.AudLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.WavLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.OggLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.AudioLoaders.Mp3Loader
    Video:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Cnc.VideoLoaders.VqaLoader
    Package:
        - OpenRA.Mods.Cnc.FileSystem.MixLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Common.FileSystem.InstallShieldLoader
        - OpenRA.Mods.Cameo.FileSystem.AudioBagLoader
```

Cameo's `mod.yaml` adds `AudioBagLoader` to the package loaders and sets `SpriteSequenceFormat: CameoSpriteSequence` to select the custom sequence loader. It also declares `SoundFormats: Aud, Wav, Mp3, Ogg` and `PackageFormats: Mix, AudioBag, D2kSoundResources`.

### Cameo sequence example

```yaml
mtnk:
    Defaults:
        Filename: gtnk.shp
    idle:
        Facings: 32
    icon:
        Filename: gtnkicon.shp
```

With `TilesetFilenames`:

```yaml
someunit:
    idle:
        TilesetFilenames:
            TEMPERATE: someunit-tem.shp
            SNOW: someunit-sno.shp
        Facings: 32
```

With `Remap` (for R8 sprites):

```yaml
someunit:
    idle:
        Filename: someunit.r8
        Remap: FF0000
        UseShadow: true
        ConvertShroudToFog: false
        Facings: 32
```

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **Loader order matters.** The engine tries loaders in the order listed in `mod.yaml`. If a generic loader is listed before a specific one, it may incorrectly claim a file.
- **Sprite sequences must match the loader format.** If `SpriteSequenceFormat` is `CameoSpriteSequence`, sequences can use `TilesetFilenames` and `Remap`. If it is `DefaultSpriteSequenceLoader`, those keys will not be recognized.
- **Bag files require the matching `.idx` file.** `AudioBagLoader` opens the `.idx` file with the same base name as the `.bag`. If the index is missing or corrupted, the package fails to load.
- **Audio bag entries are streamed, not pre-decoded.** `BagFile.GetStream` builds a WAV header and combines it with a segment of the `.bag` stream. The upstream sound loader then parses the resulting WAV/ADPCM stream.
- **R8 remap only works with `R8Loader.RemappableFrame`.** If the sprite file is not an R8 file, the `RemapFrame` delegate returns the frame unchanged.
- **Tileset-specific filenames override the default.** If `TilesetFilenames` is present for the active tileset, `Filename` is ignored. If neither is present, the sequence fails to load.
- **Cache keys must be stable.** `CameoSpriteSequence.ReserveSprites` uses a value-typed tuple `(useShadow, convertShroudToFog, remapColor)` as the `adjustFrameCacheKey` so the `SpriteCache` can recognize equivalent reservations across map loads. The delegate itself cannot be used as a cache key because it captures fresh values each parse.

## Summary

Cameo extends the upstream OpenRA asset loader system with a custom sprite sequence loader (`CameoSpriteSequenceLoader` / `CameoSpriteSequence`) that supports tileset-specific filenames, remap colors, and fog/shadow conversion for R8 sprites, and a custom package loader (`AudioBagLoader` / `BagFile`) that mounts legacy audio `.bag`/`.idx` archives. Both loaders are registered in `mod.yaml` and integrate with the existing `SpriteCache`, VFS, and sound loader chains.

# Chapter 7.1 — Map Generation Pipeline Overview (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_01_Pipeline}

## Purpose

This chapter describes how Cameo turns a seed and a set of UI options into a playable `.oramap`. The underlying pipeline is provided by the OpenRA engine's Random Map Generator (RMG) system; Cameo's primary contribution is YAML-level configuration that adapts the upstream generators to Cameo's multi-franchise tilesets and resource types.

After reading this chapter, you should understand:

- How the map chooser and editor invoke `IMapGeneratorInfo.Generate`.
- What `MapGenerationArgs` carries and how `MapGeneratorSettings` compiles widget state into it.
- Which generator implementations Cameo registers and for which tilesets.
- How Cameo links those registrations into `World`, `EditorWorld`, the mod manifest, and Fluent localization.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the RMG pipeline from UI click to saved map.
- Describe the `IMapGeneratorInfo` / `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` contracts.
- Identify the three generators Cameo exposes and the tilesets each supports.
- Read and edit `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` to change default options or add a new preset.
- Register a generator in YAML and wire it into the map chooser or editor.

## RMG at a glance

Cameo's RMG pipeline follows the standard OpenRA flow:

```
Seed + Settings
    |
    v
[7.1 Pipeline]           MapGenerationArgs, UI entry points
    |
    v
[7.2 Data Structures]    CellLayer, Matrix, MapGrid, Map
    |
    v
[7.3 Algorithms]         Noise, Symmetry, MatrixUtils
    |
    v
[7.4 Terraformer]        Terrain, elevation, roads
    |
    v
[7.5 MultiBrush]         Tile/actor brush stamps
    |
    v
[7.6 Mod Generators]     Per-mod generator classes
    |
    v
[7.7 Resources/Actors]   Spawns, resources, actor placement
    |
    v
[7.8 Extension Points]   Custom generators, brushes, options
    |
    v
[7.9 File Index]         Source reference
    |
    v
.oramap
```

Cameo does not add custom generator classes; it configures the upstream `ClassicMapGenerator`, `D2kMapGenerator`, and `ClearMapGenerator` through `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_01_Pipeline-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/MapGeneratorLogic.cs` | Chrome logic for the map chooser's random-map generation panel. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/Editor/MapGeneratorToolLogic.cs` | Chrome logic for the editor's map generator tool panel. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MapGeneratorSettings.cs` | Parses generator settings YAML and compiles widget state into `MapGenerationArgs`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | Defines `IMapGeneratorInfo`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | Defines `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` and `IMapGeneratorSettings`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/MapGenerationArgs.cs` | Serializable carrier for generator parameters. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClassicMapGenerator.cs` | Standard Red Alert / Tiberian Dawn style generator. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.D2k/Traits/World/D2kMapGenerator.cs` | Dune 2000 generator implementation. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClearMapGenerator.cs` | Minimal "clear everything to one tile" generator. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo's registration and settings for all three generators. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` | Inherits `^MapGenerators` for both `World` and `EditorWorld`. |
| `mods/cameo/mod.yaml` | Loads `cameo\|rules/map-generators.yaml`. |
| `mods/cameo/fluent/en.ftl` | Fluent labels for generator names, options, and choices. |
| `mods/common/chrome/map-chooser.yaml` | Common map chooser generation panel chrome. |
| `mods/common/chrome/editor.yaml` | Common editor generator tool panel chrome. |

## Architecture
![Architecture](images/Part_07_Chapter_01_Pipeline-Architecture.svg)


### The generator contract

The base interface is `IMapGeneratorInfo` in `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IMapGeneratorInfo : ITraitInfoInterface
{
    string Type { get; }
    string Name { get; }
    string MapTitle { get; }

    Map Generate(ModData modData, MapGenerationArgs args);
    bool TryGenerateMetadata(ModData modData, MapGenerationArgs args, out MapPlayers players, out Dictionary<string, MiniYaml> rules);
}
```

- `Type` is the internal identifier looked up by the UI.
- `Name` is the Fluent key for the human-readable label.
- `MapTitle` is the default title applied to generated maps.
- `Generate` builds a full `Map` object.
- `TryGenerateMetadata` produces only the player count and ruleset needed for previews and server selection.

Editor-visible generators implement `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IEditorMapGeneratorInfo : IMapGeneratorInfo
{
    ImmutableArray<string> Tilesets { get; }
    IMapGeneratorSettings GetSettings();
}
```

### The settings bridge

`IMapGeneratorSettings` is the contract that lets the UI logics talk to a generator without knowing its internals. The concrete implementation is `MapGeneratorSettings` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MapGeneratorSettings.cs`. It parses the `Settings` MiniYaml from a generator trait and builds a list of `MapGeneratorOption` objects.

The option types are:

| Option class | YAML key | UI widget | What it produces |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `MapGeneratorBooleanOption` | `BooleanOption@<id>` | checkbox | a single `<Parameter>: True/False` setting |
| `MapGeneratorIntegerOption` | `IntegerOption@<id>` | text field | a single `<Parameter>: <int>` setting |
| `MapGeneratorMultiIntegerChoiceOption` | `MultiIntegerChoiceOption@<id>` | dropdown | a single `<Parameter>: <int>` setting chosen from a fixed list |
| `MapGeneratorMultiChoiceOption` | `MultiChoiceOption@<id>` | dropdown | a block of settings selected by a named choice (can be tileset/player-count filtered) |

All options expose `Id`, `Label`, and `Priority`. Lower `Priority` values are applied first, and later values can override them.

### The generation carrier
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_01_Pipeline-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


`MapGenerationArgs` in `OpenRA.Game/Map/MapGenerationArgs.cs` carries:

| Field | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| `Generator` | The generator `Type`. |
| `Tileset` | The target tileset ID. |
| `Size` | The requested map size in cells. |
| `Seed` | The deterministic RNG seed. |
| `Settings` | A `MiniYaml` node of generator-specific parameters. |
| `Title` / `Author` | Map metadata. |

Cameo's generator YAML populates these fields implicitly: the user picks a tileset, size, seed, and option choices, and `MapGeneratorSettings.Compile` produces the args.

### Cameo generator registration

Cameo registers three generators in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` under the `^MapGenerators` template:

```yaml
^MapGenerators:
    ClassicMapGenerator@classic:
        Type: classic
        Name: map-generator-classic
        Tilesets: RA_TEMPERAT, RA_SNOW, RA_DESERT
        Settings:
            ...
    D2kMapGenerator@d2k:
        Type: d2k
        Name: map-generator-d2k
        Tilesets: ARRAKIS
        Settings:
            ...
    ClearMapGenerator@clear:
        Type: clear
        Name: map-generator-clear
        Tilesets: RA_TEMPERAT, RA_SNOW, RA_DESERT, RA_INTERIOR, ARRAKIS, TEMPERAT, DESERT
        Settings:
            ...
```

- `ClassicMapGenerator@classic` is the default random-map generator, configured for the three Red Alert-derived tilesets.
- `D2kMapGenerator@d2k` is exposed only for the `ARRAKIS` tileset and uses Dune 2000 terrain rules.
- `ClearMapGenerator@clear` is a minimal utility generator that fills the map with a single selectable tile. It supports every tileset that Cameo exposes to the editor.

`mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` inherits this template for both runtime and editor worlds:

```yaml
World:
    Inherits: ^BaseWorld
    Inherits@MapGenerators: ^MapGenerators
    ...

EditorWorld:
    Inherits: ^BaseWorld
    Inherits@MapGenerators: ^MapGenerators
    ...
```

The manifest in `mods/cameo/mod.yaml` ensures the file is loaded:

```yaml
Rules:
    cameo|rules/misc.yaml
    cameo|rules/player.yaml
    cameo|rules/world.yaml
    cameo|rules/map-generators.yaml
    ...
```

### Cameo option presets

`mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` overrides upstream defaults to match Cameo's multi-franchise resource and terrain setup. Notable customizations include:

- `ResourceSpawnSeeds` mapping custom resource actors (`split2`, `splitblue`, `splitred`, `splitgold`) to resource types (`Ore`, `Gems`, `Tiberium`, `BlueTiberium`, `RedTiberium`, `GoldTiberium`).
- `DefaultResource: Ore` for the classic generator, with weights adjusted per resource preset.
- `TerrainType` choices renamed to Cameo's localization keys (e.g., `label-ra-map-generator-choice-terrain-type-plots`).
- `ClearMapGenerator` tile choices covering every supported tileset, mapping each to a specific tile index.

### UI entry points

The map chooser panel is defined in `mods/common/chrome/map-chooser.yaml` (`MAPCHOOSER_GENERATE_PANEL`). Its logic class is `MapGeneratorLogic` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/MapGeneratorLogic.cs`. The editor generator tool is defined in `mods/common/chrome/editor.yaml` (`MAP_GENERATOR_TOOL_PANEL`) and driven by `MapGeneratorToolLogic` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/Editor/MapGeneratorToolLogic.cs`.

Cameo does not override either chrome file or logic class; it relies on the common implementations and supplies its own generator YAML and Fluent strings.

### Saving and preview

Generated maps are saved as `.oramap` packages. `MapChooserLogic` stores the generated package and promotes it into the `MapCache`. `MapPreview` can request a metadata-only path (`TryGenerateMetadata`) for lightweight previews, or a full `Generate` path when the map is actually loaded.

## Data Flow / Code Path

A typical user flow through the Cameo RMG pipeline:

1. The player opens **Multiplayer → Create Game** or the map editor and selects the generator tool.
2. The UI enumerates generators whose `Tilesets` include the current or selected tileset.
3. `MapGeneratorLogic` / `MapGeneratorToolLogic` builds a settings widget from `IMapGeneratorSettings.Options`.
4. The user changes seed, terrain type, symmetry, resource density, etc.
5. The logic calls `MapGeneratorSettings.Compile` to produce `MapGenerationArgs`.
6. For previews, `TryGenerateMetadata` is called to produce player/rules metadata.
7. For final generation, `IMapGeneratorInfo.Generate` builds a full `Map`.
8. The map is saved to disk and either loaded into a game or blitted into the editor as an undoable action.

## Configuration (YAML)

The following tables map generator concepts to the Cameo files that configure them.

| Concept | Cameo file | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Generator registration | `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Defines `classic`, `d2k`, and `clear` entries under `^MapGenerators`. |
| Tileset lists | `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Each generator's `Tilesets` field filters the UI. |
| Option labels | `mods/cameo/fluent/en.ftl` | Fluent keys such as `map-generator-classic` and `label-ra-map-generator-option-seed`. |
| World wiring | `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` | `Inherits@MapGenerators: ^MapGenerators` for `World` and `EditorWorld`. |
| Manifest loading | `mods/cameo/mod.yaml` | `cameo\|rules/map-generators.yaml` listed under `Rules`. |

### Common `ClassicMapGenerator` settings customized by Cameo

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `TerrainFeatureSize` | 20480 | Wavelength of terrain noise. |
| `ForestFeatureSize` | 20480 | Wavelength of forest noise. |
| `ResourceFeatureSize` | 20480 | Wavelength of resource patches. |
| `Water` | 200 | Base water probability. |
| `Mountains` | 100 | Base mountain probability. |
| `Forests` | 25 | Base forest probability. |
| `CivilianBuildings` | 125 | Civilian building density. |
| `ResourcesPerPlayer` | 50000 | Resources placed near each spawn. |
| `DefaultResource` | Ore | Resource type used for default spawns. |
| `SpawnResourceSpawns` | 3 | Number of resource fields per spawn. |

These defaults are overridden by the `TerrainType`, `Resources`, `Buildings`, `Density`, and `CivilianDensity` choice options.

## Interconnectivity

- **Depends on:**
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Matrix.cs`, `OpenRA.Game/Map/CellLayer.cs`, and `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/CellLayerUtils.cs` for data storage.
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/NoiseUtils.cs`, `Symmetry.cs`, and `MatrixUtils.cs` for algorithmic primitives (see Part 7.3).
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/TilingPath.cs`, `RampTiler.cs`, and `MapGenerator.cs` for higher-level terrain/actor placement (see Parts 7.4–7.7).
  - `OpenRA.Support/MersenneTwister.cs` for deterministic RNG.

- **Used by:**
  - The map chooser (`MapGeneratorLogic`) and editor generator tool (`MapGeneratorToolLogic`).
  - Server map selection and map previews via `TryGenerateMetadata`.

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo reuses the upstream RMG pipeline with minimal code changes. The divergence is almost entirely in YAML configuration and localization:

- No custom generator classes exist in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` or `OpenRA.Mods.CA`. All generation is performed by upstream `ClassicMapGenerator`, `D2kMapGenerator`, and `ClearMapGenerator`.
- Cameo adds a `D2kMapGenerator` registration for the `ARRAKIS` tileset, which is not enabled in the base Red Alert mod.
- `ClearMapGenerator` is configured for every tileset Cameo exposes to the editor, including `RA_INTERIOR`, `TEMPERAT`, and `DESERT`.
- Resource and terrain presets are tuned for Cameo's combined resource types (Ore, Gems, Tiberium variants, SCMinerals, Veins, etc.).
- Fluent keys are prefixed with `label-ra-map-generator-*`, `label-d2k-map-generator-*`, and `label-clear-map-generator-*` to match Cameo's naming convention.

## Practical notes

- Adding a new generator to Cameo requires a class implementing `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` in the engine or a Cameo C# mod project, plus a YAML entry under `^MapGenerators`.
- Adding a new tileset to an existing generator is usually just a matter of extending the `Tilesets` field and adding any tileset-specific overrides.
- The `ResourceSpawnSeeds` table is the primary place where Cameo links custom resource actor templates to the generator's economy model.

# Chapter 7.2 — Map Generation Data Structures (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_02_Data_Structures}

## Purpose

This chapter covers the data structures that OpenRA uses to represent, transform, and store generated maps, and the Cameo-specific YAML structures that feed the random map generator (RMG). The engine-level containers (`CellLayer<T>`, `Matrix<T>`, `MapGrid`, and `Map`) are unchanged in Cameo; Cameo's contribution is the high-level configuration data that tells the generators which tilesets, terrain types, resources, and actor templates to use.

After reading this chapter, you should understand:

- How `CellLayer<T>` and `Matrix<T>` differ and when each is used.
- How `MapGrid` and `Map` define the geometry and contents of a generated map.
- Which Cameo YAML files describe tilesets, resources, and generator settings.
- How `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` acts as a structured database of generator parameters.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the difference between `CellLayer<T>` and `Matrix<T>`.
- Convert between `CPos`, `MPos`, `PPos`, and `WPos` using `MapGrid` rules.
- Describe how `Map` assembles tile, resource, height, ramp, and actor layers.
- Identify the tileset and resource definitions that the Cameo RMG consumes.
- Read and extend `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` settings blocks.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_02_Data_Structures-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


### Engine data structures

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/CellLayerBase.cs` | Abstract base for a flat array of values whose dimensions match a `MapGrid`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/CellLayer.cs` | Generic `CellLayer<T>` with `CPos`/`MPos` indexers and a `CellEntryChanged` event. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Matrix.cs` | Generic 2D array indexed by `int2` used by generator algorithms. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/CellLayerUtils.cs` | Bridge helpers between `CellLayer<T>` and `Matrix<T>`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/MapGrid.cs` | Grid type, sub-cells, ramps, and `TilesByDistance`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/Map.cs` | Top-level map container: tile/resource/height/ramp layers, bounds, projection, actors. |
| `OpenRA.Game/CPos.cs` | Packed cell coordinate (X, Y, Layer). |
| `OpenRA.Game/MPos.cs` | Raw map coordinate (U, V) plus the `PPos` projected coordinate struct. |
| `OpenRA.Game/WPos.cs` | World-space 3D position (X, Y, Z). |
| `OpenRA.Game/CVec.cs` | 2D cell-space offset vector. |

### Cameo configuration data

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo's generator registrations and option/override databases. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml` | Red Alert temperate tileset (`RA_TEMPERAT`). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml` | Red Alert snow tileset (`RA_SNOW`). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml` | Red Alert desert tileset (`RA_DESERT`). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_interior.yaml` | Red Alert interior tileset (`RA_INTERIOR`). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` | Dune 2000 Arrakis tileset (`ARRAKIS`). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/temperat.yaml` | Tiberian Dawn temperate tileset (`TEMPERAT`). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/desert.yaml` | Tiberian Dawn desert tileset (`DESERT`). |
| `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` | Resource type definitions and `EditorResourceLayer` configuration. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/misc.yaml` | Resource actor templates referenced by `ResourceSpawnSeeds`. |

## Architecture

### Engine layers

A `CellLayer<T>` is a dense array of `T` values sized to the map and tagged with the grid type (`Rectangular` or `RectangularIsometric`). The base class handles memory, while the sealed subclass adds coordinate-aware indexers and change notification. `Matrix<T>` is a generator workbench: a simple 2D array with no grid awareness, used for noise, distance transforms, and morphological operations.

`CellLayerUtils` bridges the two representations with `ToMatrix` and `FromMatrix`, copying data between `CellLayer<T>` and `Matrix<T>` while respecting grid geometry.

`MapGrid` defines the shape of the world: rectangular vs. rectangular-isometric, sub-cells, ramp rules, and the `TilesByDistance` lookup. `Map` combines all layers into one serializable object and exposes bounds, projection, and actor data.

### Cameo tilesets used by the RMG

Cameo exposes many tilesets, but only a subset is wired into the RMG:

| Tileset file | Tileset ID | Generator support | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml` | `RA_TEMPERAT` | `ClassicMapGenerator`, `ClearMapGenerator` | RA-style temperate. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml` | `RA_SNOW` | `ClassicMapGenerator`, `ClearMapGenerator` | RA-style snow. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml` | `RA_DESERT` | `ClassicMapGenerator`, `ClearMapGenerator` | RA-style desert. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_interior.yaml` | `RA_INTERIOR` | `ClearMapGenerator` only | Interior floors/walls. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` | `ARRAKIS` | `D2kMapGenerator`, `ClearMapGenerator` | Dune 2000 sand/rock. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/temperat.yaml` | `TEMPERAT` | `ClearMapGenerator` only | TD temperate. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/desert.yaml` | `DESERT` | `ClearMapGenerator` only | TD desert. |

Other Cameo tilesets (`CAMEO`, `TIBFIELDS`, `WC2SUMMER`, `WC2SUNSET`, `WC2SWAMP`, `OUTPOST2`, `BARREN`, `CARIBIC`, `JUNGLE`, `WINTER`, `RA2_TEMPERAT`, etc.) are available in the editor but are not registered for random map generation, usually because their terrain templates do not fit the assumptions of the upstream generators.

### Tileset YAML structure

Each tileset YAML contains:

```yaml
General:
    Name: ra_Temperate
    Id: RA_TEMPERAT
    TileSize: 48,48
    SheetSize: 2048
    EditorTemplateOrder: Terrain, Debris, Road, Cliffs, Water Cliffs, Beach, River, Bridge
    HeightDebugColors: AA0000

Terrain:
    TerrainType@Beach:
        Type: Beach
        TargetTypes: Ground
        Color: B09C78
    ...

Templates:
    ...
```

The `Id` value is what the generator's `Tilesets` field matches. The `Terrain` block maps logical terrain types (`Clear`, `Water`, `Cliff`, `Road`, etc.) to colors and passability flags, which the generator uses when deciding where to place actors and resources.

### Cameo generator settings database

`mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` is a structured data file rather than an algorithm. Each generator entry contains:

- `Type`, `Name`, and `Tilesets` metadata.
- A `Settings` block of `MapGeneratorOption` definitions.
- `MultiChoiceOption` presets that override defaults based on tileset, player count, or user choice.

For example, the classic generator's `hidden_tileset_overrides` choice applies tileset-specific tile indices:

```yaml
MultiChoiceOption@hidden_tileset_overrides:
    Choice@ra_desert:
        Tileset: RA_DESERT
        Settings:
            MinimumBeachLength: 15
            MinimumCoastStraight: 3
            LandTile: 255
            WaterTile: 256
    Choice@ra_temperat:
        Tileset: RA_TEMPERAT
        Settings:
            LandTile: 255
            WaterTile: 1
```

This is pure data: no custom C# code is required to add a new override.

### Resource mappings

Cameo's classic generator uses the `ResourceSpawnSeeds` table to map actor template names to resource types:

```yaml
ResourceSpawnSeeds:
    mine: Ore
    gmine: Gems
    split2: Tiberium
    splitblue: BlueTiberium
    splitred: RedTiberium
    splitgold: GoldTiberium
```

The actual actors (`mine`, `gmine`, and the `split*` trees) are defined in `mods/cameo/rules/misc.yaml`. The generator places these actors on valid clear terrain, and the actors' `SeedsResource` or `ResourceLayer` traits handle runtime resource creation.

## Configuration (YAML)

The following Cameo YAML fields are the main data inputs to the RMG:

| Field | Typical file | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `Id` | `mods/cameo/tilesets/*.yaml` | Tileset identifier used in generator `Tilesets` lists. |
| `TerrainType@*` | `mods/cameo/tilesets/*.yaml` | Logical terrain types and their colors/target types. |
| `ResourceSpawnSeeds` | `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Maps actor template names to resource types. |
| `DefaultResource` | `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Resource type used for default spawn fields. |
| `PlayableTerrain` / `DominantTerrain` / `ZoneableTerrain` | `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Terrain categories that guide generator placement. |
| `ClearSegmentTypes` / `BeachSegmentTypes` / `CliffSegmentTypes` / `RoadSegmentTypes` | `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Template segment categories used by the `Terraformer` and `MultiBrush`. |

## Interconnectivity
![Interconnectivity](images/Part_07_Chapter_02_Data_Structures-Interconnectivity.svg)
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_02_Data_Structures-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:**
  - `OpenRA.Game/Map/CellLayer.cs` and `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Matrix.cs` for storage.
  - `OpenRA.Game/Map/MapGrid.cs` and `OpenRA.Game/Map/Map.cs` for geometry and serialization.
  - `mods/cameo/tilesets/*.yaml` for tile and terrain type definitions.
  - `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` and `mods/cameo/rules/misc.yaml` for resource types and resource actors.

- **Used by:**
  - `ClassicMapGenerator`, `D2kMapGenerator`, and `ClearMapGenerator` in the upstream engine.
  - `MapGeneratorSettings` to compile `MapGenerationArgs`.
  - The map editor, which loads the same tileset data for both manual and generated maps.

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo does not introduce new engine data structures for map generation. The divergence is in the *content* of the YAML databases:

- Cameo maintains more tileset files than the base mods, but only registers a subset for RMG use.
- `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` adds resource actor mappings for Tiberium variants (`split2`, `splitblue`, `splitred`, `splitgold`) that do not exist in the base Red Alert mod.
- `ClearMapGenerator` choices cover Cameo's extended tileset set, including `RA_INTERIOR`, `TEMPERAT`, and `DESERT`.
- The `World`/`EditorWorld` rules in `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` define additional resource types (`BlueTiberium`, `RedTiberium`, `GoldTiberium`, `SCMinerals`, `Veins`, etc.) that are available to the editor and to custom generators, even though the upstream `ClassicMapGenerator` only uses a subset.

## Practical notes

- To make a tileset available to the RMG, add its `Id` to the generator's `Tilesets` field and ensure the tileset contains the terrain types the generator expects (`Clear`, `Water`, `Cliff`, `Road`, `Beach`, etc.).
- To add a new resource to the classic generator, add a `ResourceSpawnSeeds` entry pointing to an actor template, and ensure that actor's rules place it on terrain the generator treats as playable.
- Tileset-specific tile indices (such as `LandTile` and `WaterTile`) are usually the only values that need to change when extending a generator to a new tileset.

# Chapter 7.3 — Map Generation Algorithms (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_03_Algorithms}

## Purpose

This chapter documents the algorithmic primitives that OpenRA's random map generator uses to synthesize terrain, roads, resources, and spawn sites. Cameo does not modify these primitives; it only supplies different YAML parameter sets to the upstream generators. The focus here is on how the algorithms work and which Cameo configuration knobs affect them.

After reading this chapter, you should understand:

- How Perlin/fractal noise is synthesized and constrained by symmetry.
- How boolean masks are smoothed, thinned, and converted into paths.
- Which Cameo YAML parameters drive each algorithmic stage.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain how `NoiseUtils` produces candidate height fields.
- Describe how `Symmetry` enforces mirror and rotational fairness.
- Use `MatrixUtils` to threshold, smooth, and extract contours from masks.
- Trace the typical generator path from noise to mask to path to final placement.
- Tune Cameo YAML parameters (`TerrainFeatureSize`, `Water`, `Mountains`, `TerrainSmoothing`, etc.) to change map character.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_03_Algorithms-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/NoiseUtils.cs` | Perlin noise, octave summation, symmetric fractal noise, and amplitude presets. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MatrixUtils.cs` | Boolean morphology, smoothing, contour/path extraction, flood fills, distance transforms. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Symmetry.cs` | Mirror and rotational-symmetry primitives. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Direction.cs` | Direction enum, masks, and adjacency helpers. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo's parameter sets that feed the algorithms above. |

## Architecture
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_03_Algorithms-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


The algorithm layer is a set of static helper classes that operate on `Matrix<T>` and, where necessary, `CellLayer<T>`:

```
NoiseUtils
    PerlinNoise          => Matrix<int>
    FractalNoise         => Matrix<int>
    SymmetricFractalNoise=> Matrix<int>
    SymmetricFractalNoiseIntoCellLayer => CellLayer<int>

Symmetry
    Mirror enum
    WMirror struct
    MirrorPointAround
    RotateAndMirrorPointAround
    RotateAndMirrorWPosAround / CPos

MatrixUtils
    IntegerInterpolate
    BooleanBlur / BooleanBlotch
    RetainThickRegions / DilateThinRegions
    BordersToPoints
    DirectionMapToPaths / DirectionMapToPathsWithPruning
    RemoveStubsFromDirectionMapInPlace
    MaskPathPoints
    DeflateSpace / ChebyshevRoom / WalkingDistances
    FloodFill / KernelFilter / BinomialBlur
```

These classes are functional: each method transforms one matrix into another and often returns a change count so the caller can decide when to stop iterating.

## Data Flow / Code Path
![Configuration (yaml) diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_03_Algorithms-annotated-yaml-snippet-diagram-showing-the-key-fields-and-ho-6a1b98.svg)


A typical high-level generator path looks like this:

1. **YAML parameters are read** by `ClassicMapGenerator` or `D2kMapGenerator`. Values such as `featureSize`, `rotations`, `mirror`, `terrainSmoothing`, `threshold`, and `minimumThickness` are passed as arguments.
2. **Noise is synthesized** by `SymmetricFractalNoise`, which calls `FractalNoise`, which calls `PerlinNoise` for each octave.
3. **Noise is converted to a boolean mask** by `CalibratedBooleanThreshold` or a custom threshold.
4. **The mask is cleaned up** by `BooleanBlotch` (`BooleanBlur`, `RetainThickRegions`, `DilateThinRegions`).
5. **Contours are extracted** from the mask with `BordersToPoints`.
6. **Paths are optimized** with `DirectionMapToPathsWithPruning`, `MaskPathPoints`, and stub/junction removal.
7. **The final path or region data is consumed** by tile placement, cliff/river/road rendering, resource spawning, and actor placement logic.

## Configuration (YAML)

Cameo's `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` maps user-visible choices to the algorithm parameters above. The following table shows the most important mappings for the `ClassicMapGenerator`.

| Parameter | Typical YAML key | Cameo example | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `featureSize` | `TerrainFeatureSize`, `ForestFeatureSize`, `ResourceFeatureSize` | 20480 / 10240 / 51200 | Largest wavelength of the noise field, in 1024ths of a cell. |
| `ampFunc` | `Amplitude`, `Clumpiness` | `ForestClumpiness: 1` | Preset controlling octave contribution. |
| `rotations` | `Rotations` | 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 | Rotational symmetry count from the `Symmetry` choice. |
| `mirror` | `Mirror` | `None`, `LeftMatchesRight`, `TopMatchesBottom` | Mirror mode from the `Symmetry` choice. |
| `terrainSmoothing` / `smoothingThreshold` | `TerrainSmoothing`, `SmoothingThreshold` | 4, 833 | Cellular-automata smoothing radius and vote threshold. |
| `minimumThickness` | `MinimumLandSeaThickness`, `MinimumMountainThickness` | 5 | Minimum Chebyshev thickness of land/water/mountain regions. |
| `bias` | `ExternalCircularBias` | 0, 1, -1 | Tie-breaker used by the `Shape` choice (Square, CircleMountain, CircleWater). |
| `Water` | `Water` | 0–800 | Probability/frequency of water in the noise mask. |
| `Mountains` | `Mountains` | 0–900 | Probability/frequency of mountain obstacles. |
| `Forests` | `Forests` | 0–500 | Probability/frequency of forest patches. |
| `CivilianBuildings` | `CivilianBuildings` | 0–1000 | Density of civilian buildings. |

### How Cameo presets change the algorithm output

The `TerrainType` choice in Cameo's `ClassicMapGenerator` is the clearest example of algorithm steering through YAML alone:

- `Lakes` / `Puddles` / `Wetlands` increase `Water`.
- `Plains` / `Parks` / `Woodlands` set `Water: 0` and increase forests.
- `Rocky` / `Mountains` / `MountainLakes` increase `Mountains` and `Roughness`.
- `Oceanic`, `LargeIslands`, and `Continents` push `Water` and `TerrainFeatureSize` to larger scales.

These are not separate algorithms; they are different parameter sets applied to the same upstream `ClassicMapGenerator`.

### D2k generator parameters

Cameo's `D2kMapGenerator@d2k` uses the same algorithmic primitives but with Dune 2000-specific YAML keys:

- `SandDetailFeatureSize`, `DuneFeatureSize`, `TerrainFeatureSize` control noise scales.
- `Rock`, `SandCliffs`, `Dunes` control terrain-type probabilities.
- `MinimumRockSandThickness`, `MinimumSandCliffThickness`, `MinimumDuneThickness` enforce region thickness.
- `SandDetail`, `SandDetailClumpiness`, `SandDetailCutout` add fine sand detail.

Again, no algorithm code is changed; the YAML supplies different parameter values and terrain category mappings.

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_03_Algorithms-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:**
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Matrix.cs` and `OpenRA.Game/Map/CellLayer.cs` for grid containers.
  - `OpenRA.Support/MersenneTwister.cs` for deterministic RNG.
  - `OpenRA.Game/Primitives/int2.cs`, `WPos.cs`, `WAngle.cs`, `WDist.cs` for coordinate and fixed-point math.
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Direction.cs` for adjacency and direction masks.
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/CellLayerUtils.cs` for coordinate conversions.

- **Used by:**
  - `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClassicMapGenerator.cs` and `OpenRA.Mods.D2k/Traits/World/D2kMapGenerator.cs`.
  - Higher-level generator classes such as `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/TilingPath.cs`, `RampTiler.cs`, and `MapGenerator.cs`.

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo has **no code-level divergence** in the RMG algorithm layer. All differences are expressed as YAML parameter overrides:

- The noise, symmetry, and matrix utilities are taken verbatim from the upstream engine.
- `ClassicMapGenerator` and `D2kMapGenerator` run the same algorithm code as in the base mods.
- Cameo adds more user-visible presets (`TerrainType`, `Resources`, `Buildings`, `Density`, `CivilianDensity`) and populates them with values tuned for Cameo's combined economy.
- Resource/terrain weights and actor mappings are customized, but the underlying placement algorithms (`SpawnSites`, `ResourceSpawns`, `ActorGenerator`, etc.) are unchanged.

## Practical notes

- To change map character without touching C#, edit the numeric parameters under `MultiChoiceOption@TerrainType` or add a new choice in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`.
- `TerrainFeatureSize` is the single most powerful knob for map scale; larger values produce broader continents/lakes, smaller values produce noisy, detailed terrain.
- `EnforceSymmetry` and the `Symmetry` mirror/rotation choices directly feed `Symmetry.RotateAndMirrorPointAround`, so multiplayer fairness is deterministic from the seed.
