# Chapter 7.4 — Terraformer (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_04_Terraformer}

## Purpose

`[Terraformer](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)` is the high-level orchestration class for OpenRA procedural map generation. While the algorithmic primitives live in `NoiseUtils`, `MatrixUtils`, and `Symmetry`, and the brush engine lives in `[MultiBrush](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)`, the `Terraformer` is where a generator author calls those pieces together to create a playable, balanced, and visually coherent map. It provides a single mutable workspace that holds the `Map` being generated, a list of `[ActorPlan](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)`s, symmetry settings, and convenience wrappers for terrain selection, space analysis, path tiling, resource placement, and actor placement.

Cameo does not modify `Terraformer` itself; it drives the upstream class through the YAML parameters in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the role of `Terraformer` as the high-level map generation orchestrator.
- Describe the workspace (`Map`, `ActorPlans`, symmetry settings) and its lifecycle.
- Trace `InitMap` and `BakeMap` and explain what they finalize.
- Identify which Cameo YAML parameters feed each `Terraformer` phase.
- Implement a custom generator phase using the `Terraformer` toolbox.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_04_Terraformer-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Terraformer.cs` | The `Terraformer` class and all high-level map generation helpers. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/CellLayerUtils.cs` | Conversions between `CellLayer`, `Matrix`, `CPos`, and `WPos`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MatrixUtils.cs` | Boolean morphology, contour/path extraction, and distance transforms. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/NoiseUtils.cs` | Fractal noise generation consumed by `Terraformer` noise helpers. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Symmetry.cs` | Rotational and mirror-symmetry operations. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MultiBrush.cs` | Tile/actor super-brush engine used by `PaintArea`, `PaintTiling`, `PaintLoopsAndFill`, and `RepaintTiles`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/TilingPath.cs` | Path-aware tiling used by `PartitionPath` and `PaintLoopsAndFill`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/ActorPlan.cs` | Mutable actor placement plan used by `ActorPlans`, `ProjectPlaceDezoneActor`, and `ReorderPlayerSpawns`. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo parameters that drive the `Terraformer` phases. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml` | Red Alert temperate tileset with `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml` | Red Alert snow tileset with `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml` | Red Alert desert tileset with `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` | Arrakis tileset with `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |

## Architecture

`Terraformer` is a single-instance-per-map workspace. The constructor captures everything needed to produce the map, and public methods mutate the workspace or return derived layers.

```
MapGenerationArgs
       |
       v
new Terraformer(map, modData, actorPlans, mirror, rotations)
       |
       +-- Map  ........................... mutable map tile/height/actor data
       +-- ActorPlans  .................... mutable list of planned actors
       +-- WMirror / Rotations  ........... symmetry settings
       +-- terrainInfo / templatedTerrainInfo  (cached tileset rules)
       +-- lazyProjectionSpacing  ........... Chebyshev distance to nearest symmetry projection
       |
       v
   InitMap()  --> set Map bounds, title, author, mod
       |
       v
   (generate terrain / paths / actors / resources)
       |
       v
   BakeMap()  --> create PlayerDefinitions, ActorDefinitions
```

### Core types defined in `Terraformer`

- **`Terraformer`** — main orchestration class.
- **`ResourceBias`** — describes how to bias or exclude resource placement near a point or actor.
- **`Region`** — metadata for connected regions returned by `FindRegions`.
- **`PathPartitionZone`** — describes a zone segment when partitioning a path (water, land, road, etc.).
- **`Side` enum** — `Out = -1`, `None = 0`, `In = 1`; used by `InsideOutside` and `PaintLoopsAndFill`.
- **`ResourceDensityMode` enum** — controls how resource density is interpreted.
- **`FractionMax = 1000`** — common denominator for fractional arguments.

### Key fields and construction
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_04_Terraformer-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


The constructor caches `terrainInfo`, extracts `templatedTerrainInfo` if the current tileset supports templates, and lazily builds a `projectionSpacing` layer. `ProjectionSpacing` computes, for each cell, half the distance to its nearest symmetry-projection copy, preventing placements from colliding with their own mirror images.

```csharp
public Terraformer(
    MapGenerationArgs mapGenerationArgs,
    Map map,
    ModData modData,
    List<ActorPlan> actorPlans,
    Symmetry.Mirror mirror,
    int rotations)
{
    MapGenerationArgs = mapGenerationArgs;
    Map = map;
    ModData = modData;
    ActorPlans = actorPlans;
    WMirror = new Symmetry.WMirror(mirror, map.Grid.Type);
    Rotations = rotations;
    terrainInfo = modData.DefaultTerrainInfo[map.Tileset];
    templatedTerrainInfo = terrainInfo as ITemplatedTerrainInfo;
    lazyProjectionSpacing = new(ProjectionSpacing);
}
```

## Data Flow / Code Path

A typical procedural map generator using `Terraformer` follows this sequence, which is exactly how `ClassicMapGenerator` and `D2kMapGenerator` work in Cameo:

1. **Create the workspace.**
   ```csharp
   var terraformer = new Terraformer(args, map, modData, actorPlans, mirror, rotations);
   terraformer.InitMap();
   ```

2. **Generate terrain.**
   - Use `ElevationNoiseMatrix` to get a height field.
   - Use `SliceElevation` to threshold the field into land/water masks.
   - Use `BooleanNoise` for additional masks (clumps, roughness, etc.).
   - Paint base terrain via `PaintArea` / `PaintActors` / `RepaintTiles`.
   - Carve passageways with `PlanPassages` and fill them in.

3. **Generate roads / rivers / cliffs.**
   - Use `PlanRoads` or external contour extraction to get point paths.
   - Use `PartitionPath` / `PartitionPaths` to assign segment types to sub-paths.
   - Use `PaintLoopsAndFill` or `PaintTiling` to stamp the path tiles using `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` from the tileset.

4. **Place actors and resources.**
   - Build masks with `CheckSpace` / `GetZoneable`.
   - Place spawns with `ChooseSpawnInZoneable` and `ProjectPlaceDezoneActor`.
   - Place other actors with `AddActor`, `AddDistributedActors`, or `AddActorCluster`.
   - Place resources with `PlanResources` and `GrowResources`.
   - Optionally run `ReorderPlayerSpawns` before baking.

5. **Commit everything.**
   ```csharp
   terraformer.BakeMap();
   ```

### `InitMap`

`InitMap` sets the play area bounds, title, author, and required mod. It accounts for the maximum terrain height when computing the bottom-right bound, because the topmost row of an elevated map is reserved for height projection.

```csharp
public void InitMap()
{
    var maxTerrainHeight = Map.Grid.MaximumTerrainHeight;
    var tl = new PPos(1, 1 + maxTerrainHeight);
    var br = new PPos(Map.MapSize.Width - 2, Map.MapSize.Height - maxTerrainHeight - 2);
    Map.SetBounds(tl, br);
    Map.Title = MapGenerationArgs.Title;
    Map.Author = MapGenerationArgs.Author;
    Map.RequiresMod = ModData.Manifest.Id;
}
```

### `BakeMap`

`BakeMap` turns the mutable workspace into a serializable map. Player definitions are generated based on the count of `mpspawn` actors. Actor definitions are filtered by whether their projected footprint is inside the map, then serialized into a numbered list.

## Configuration (YAML)

Cameo's `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` supplies the parameter values that control the `Terraformer` phases. The following table maps `Terraformer` concepts to Cameo YAML fields.

| `Terraformer` phase | Cameo YAML keys (Classic) | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Noise/elevation | `TerrainFeatureSize`, `RoughnessRadius`, `Roughness`, `WaterRoughness` | Height-field generation and roughness. |
| Land/water threshold | `Water`, `LandTile`, `WaterTile`, `MinimumLandSeaThickness`, `MinimumCoastStraight` | Convert elevation noise into land/water masks. |
| Mountains/forests | `Mountains`, `Forests`, `ForestFeatureSize`, `ForestCutout`, `MaximumCutoutSpacing` | Boolean noise masks for obstacles and forests. |
| Symmetry | `Mirror`, `Rotations`, `EnforceSymmetry` | Symmetry group passed to the `Terraformer` constructor. |
| Roads/paths | `Roads`, `RoadSpacing`, `RoadShrink`, `RoadSegmentTypes`, `ClearSegmentTypes` | Path generation and segment-type assignment. |
| Beaches/cliffs | `BeachSegmentTypes`, `CliffSegmentTypes`, `WaterCliffSegmentTypes`, `MinimumBeachLength`, `MinimumCliffLength` | `MultiBrush` collections used by `PaintLoopsAndFill`. |
| Actor placement | `CivilianBuildings`, `MinimumBuildings`, `MaximumBuildings`, `BuildingWeights`, `CentralSpawnReservationFraction`, `SpawnReservation` | Actor density and reservation radii. |
| Resources | `DefaultResource`, `ResourceSpawnSeeds`, `ResourcesPerPlayer`, `SpawnResourceSpawns`, `MaximumExpansionResourceSpawns` | Resource field planning and growth. |

The `D2kMapGenerator@d2k` entry uses a different set of keys (`Rock`, `SandCliffs`, `Dunes`, `SandDetail`, etc.) but still drives the same `Terraformer` methods with Arrakis-specific `MultiBrushCollections`.

## Cameo-specific notes

- Cameo does **not** override `Terraformer.cs`, `TilingPath.cs`, `RampTiler.cs`, or `LatTiler.cs`. All terrain sculpting logic is inherited from upstream `OpenRA.Mods.Common`.
- The multi-franchise terrain in Cameo is handled by **parameter and brush data**, not by code. For example, the classic generator's `ClearSegmentTypes`, `BeachSegmentTypes`, `CliffSegmentTypes`, and `RoadSegmentTypes` map to `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` entries in the RA tilesets, while the D2k generator maps to the Arrakis `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` entries.
- The `CivilianBuildings` and `BuildingWeights` options in Cameo's classic generator reference neutral actors such as `hosp`, `miss`, and `oilb` defined in `mods/cameo/rules/civilian.yaml` and `mods/cameo/rules/tech.yaml`.

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_04_Terraformer-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:** `MatrixUtils`, `NoiseUtils`, `Symmetry`, `CellLayerUtils`, `MultiBrush`, `TilingPath`, `ActorPlan`.
- **Used by:** `ClassicMapGenerator`, `D2kMapGenerator`, `ClearMapGenerator`, and any custom generator added to a mod.

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo's `Terraformer` usage is identical to upstream. Divergence is limited to:

- Different YAML parameter values in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`.
- Different `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` content in Cameo's tilesets.
- Different actor and resource template names in the classic generator's `ResourceSpawnSeeds` and `BuildingWeights`.

# Chapter 7.5 — MultiBrush and Tile Placement (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_05_MultiBrush}

## Purpose

`[MultiBrush](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)` is OpenRA's template-based tile and actor placement system. It takes a YAML-defined “super-template” — one or more terrain templates, individual terrain tiles, and/or actor placements — and applies it to a map as a single unit. The system is used by the map generator and editor tooling to paint large, coherent terrain features (beaches, cliffs, roads, water-to-land transitions) while respecting which cells are allowed to be overwritten.

Cameo does not change the `MultiBrush` runtime; it provides tileset-specific brush collections that let the upstream generator paint RA, TD, and Dune 2000 terrain styles.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain how `MultiBrush` provides template-based tile and actor placement.
- Describe the YAML data layer (`MultiBrushInfo`), segments, and runtime layer (`MultiBrush`).
- Load brush collections from tileset YAML and paint them onto a `Map`.
- Understand `Replaceability` contracts and how they control overwrite behavior.
- Identify the Cameo tilesets that define `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_05_MultiBrush-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MultiBrush.cs` | `MultiBrushInfo`, `MultiBrushSegment`, and `MultiBrush` runtime implementation. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Direction.cs` | `Direction`/`DirectionMask` values used by segment directions. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Terrain/DefaultTerrain.cs` | Loads `MultiBrushCollections` from tileset YAML and exposes them through `ITemplatedTerrainInfo`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/TilingPathTool.cs` | Downstream consumer that loads segmented brushes and chains them into editor-placeable paths. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Lint/CheckMultiBrushes.cs` | Lint pass that instantiates every `MultiBrushInfo` at load time. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml` | RA temperate `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` (Beach, Cliff, Road, etc.). |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml` | RA snow `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml` | RA desert `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` | Arrakis `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` (RockSmooth, Sand cliff segments, etc.). |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Generator settings that name the segment types used from these collections. |

## Architecture

The subsystem is split into three layers:

1. **YAML Data Layer — `MultiBrushInfo`** — A `FieldLoader`-driven definition loaded from MiniYaml before a map is available.
2. **Segment Layer — `MultiBrushSegment`** — Describes how some brushes link head-to-tail (a cliff that continues straight or turns a corner).
3. **Runtime Layer — `MultiBrush`** — The actual paintable object that knows how to paint itself onto a `Map`.

```
Tileset YAML
   |
   v
MultiBrushInfo.ParseCollection
   |
   v
MultiBrushInfo (per-brush definition)
   |
   +--> MultiBrushSegment (optional)
   |
   v
new MultiBrush(map, info)
   |
   v
MultiBrush.Paint / MultiBrush.PaintArea
   |
   v
map.Tiles / map.Height / actorPlans
```

### Key classes
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_05_MultiBrush-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


- **`MultiBrushInfo`** — YAML-bound definition. Contains:
  - `Weight` (int, default 1000)
  - `Actors` (`ImmutableArray<ActorInfo>`)
  - `BackingTile` (`TerrainTile?`)
  - `Templates` (`ImmutableArray<TemplateInfo>`)
  - `Tiles` (`ImmutableArray<TileInfo>`)
  - `Segment` (`MultiBrushSegment`)

- **`MultiBrushInfo.ActorInfo`** — actor type plus a `WVec` offset.
- **`MultiBrushInfo.TemplateInfo`** — terrain template ID plus a `CVec` offset.
- **`MultiBrushInfo.TileInfo`** — explicit `TerrainTile` plus a `CVec` offset.

- **`MultiBrushSegment`** — describes chaining:
  - `Start` — required, includes a direction suffix (e.g., `Beach.L`, `RockSmooth.R`).
  - `Inner` — optional, no direction suffix.
  - `End` — required, includes a direction suffix.
  - `Points` — cardinal-step path of `-X-Y` corners of template tiles.

- **`MultiBrush`** — runtime brush. Notable members:
  - `Weight`, `tiles`, `actorPlans`, `Segment`, `Shape`, `Area`, `FirstCell`.

- **`MultiBrush.Replaceability`** — a mask describing how a cell may be modified:
  - `None` (0) — cannot be touched.
  - `Tile` (1) — the tile may be replaced; an actor may also be placed.
  - `Actor` (2) — the tile must stay, but an actor may be placed.
  - `Any` (3) — both tile and actor may be placed.

- **`MultiBrush.TileRange`** — a tile type plus an optional index range, height offset, and ramp.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### 1. Loading from YAML

`DefaultTerrainInfo` parses the top-level `MultiBrushCollections` node in the tileset YAML. Each collection is stored as a frozen dictionary mapping collection names to arrays of `MultiBrushInfo`.

When code needs a named collection, it calls:

```csharp
var brushes = MultiBrush.LoadCollection(map, name);  // MultiBrush.cs
```

`LoadCollection` fetches the `MultiBrushInfo` array and constructs a `MultiBrush` for each one.

### 2. Composing a brush

A brush can be built incrementally:

- `WithTemplate` — expands a `TerrainTemplateInfo` into tile entries.
- `WithTile` — adds a single explicit tile.
- `WithActor` — adds an `ActorPlan`.
- `WithBackingTile` — adds the same tile to every cell currently in the shape.
- `ReplaceSegment` — attaches a `MultiBrushSegment`.
- `WithWeight` — sets the selection weight; must be > 0.
- `MergeFrom` — copies tiles and actor plans from another brush at an offset.

### 3. Computing the footprint

The shape is the union of all tile offsets and all actor footprint cells. This is lazily cached and invalidated whenever tiles or actors are added.

### 4. Painting a single brush

`Paint` is the direct stamping method:

```csharp
public void Paint(Map map, List<ActorPlan> actorPlans, CPos paintAt,
    short? heightOffset, Replaceability contract, MersenneTwister random)
```

`PaintArea` paints the brush at every cell in a region, optionally randomized. Both methods consult the `Replaceability` contract to decide whether each affected cell may be overwritten.

## Configuration (YAML)

The relevant Cameo YAML is in two layers:

1. **Tileset brush libraries** define the available brushes and segments.
2. **Generator settings** select which brush collections to use for each segment type.

For example, in `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml`:

```yaml
MultiBrushCollections:
    Segmented:
        MultiBrush@3:
            Template: 3
            Segment:
                Start: Beach.L
                End: Beach.L
                Points: 4,1, 4,2, 3,2, 2,2, 1,2, 1,3, 0,3
```

And in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`:

```yaml
ClassicMapGenerator@classic:
    Settings:
        ...
        ClearSegmentTypes: Clear
        BeachSegmentTypes: Beach
        CliffSegmentTypes: Cliff
        WaterCliffSegmentTypes: WaterCliff
        RoadSegmentTypes: Road
```

The segment-type strings (`Beach`, `Cliff`, `Road`, etc.) must match collection names or prefixed brush names inside the tileset's `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`.

## Cameo-specific notes

- Cameo provides `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` in the tilesets used by the RMG:
  - `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml`
  - `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml`
  - `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml`
  - `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml`
- The `ClearMapGenerator` does not use segmented brushes; it only needs a single tile index.
- Cameo tilesets that are **not** registered for random map generation (e.g., `CAMEO`, `TIBFIELDS`, `WC2SUMMER`, `WC2SUNSET`, `WC2SWAMP`, `OUTPOST2`, `BARREN`, `CARIBIC`, `JUNGLE`, `WINTER`, `RA2_TEMPERAT`) may still define their own `MultiBrushCollections` for the editor, but the upstream generators will not use them.

## Interconnectivity

- **Used by:** `Terraformer.PaintArea`, `Terraformer.PaintTiling`, `Terraformer.PaintLoopsAndFill`, `Terraformer.RepaintTiles`, and `TilingPathTool`.
- **Depends on:** `DefaultTerrainInfo` for parsing, `ActorPlan` for embedded actors, `Direction` for segment directions.

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo reuses the upstream `MultiBrush` runtime and syntax. The divergence is in the brush data:

- Cameo ships its own RA/TD/Arrakis tilesets, so the brush template IDs and segment shapes differ from the base mods.
- The D2k generator in Cameo uses the Arrakis tileset's `RockSmooth.*` and sand-cliff segments rather than the base `mods/d2k/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` brushes.

# Chapter 7.6 — Mod-Specific Generators (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_06_Mod_Generators}

## Purpose

The OpenRA map generator is not a single monolithic program. It is a small ecosystem of **mod-specific generators** that each decide *what* a procedurally generated map should look like for a particular game, while a shared layer of `OpenRA.Mods.Common` code decides *how* to sculpt terrain, tile paths, grow resources, and place actors. This chapter studies the generators that Cameo actually uses:

- `ClassicMapGenerator` — generates Red Alert / Tiberian Dawn style maps.
- `D2kMapGenerator` — generates Arrakis-style Dune 2000 maps.
- `ClearMapGenerator` — a minimal utility generator that fills a map with one tile.

Cameo does not add a new mod-specific generator class; it configures the upstream ones through YAML.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the two-level architecture of mod-specific map generators (`Info` class + tool class).
- Compare the `ClassicMapGenerator` and `D2kMapGenerator` parameter sets in Cameo.
- Describe how `Parameters` classes bridge YAML settings to typed generator fields.
- Trace the common generator phases from base terrain to `BakeMap`.
- Add a new generator to Cameo by implementing `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` in a custom mod assembly.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_06_Mod_Generators-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClassicMapGenerator.cs` | Red Alert / Tiberian Dawn generator with full `Parameters` and phases. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.D2k/Traits/World/D2kMapGenerator.cs` | Dune 2000 Arrakis generator (sand, rock platforms, spice, dunes). |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClearMapGenerator.cs` | Minimal flat-map generator reference. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | `IMapGeneratorInfo` base interface. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo`, `IMapGeneratorSettings`. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo's registration and settings for `classic`, `d2k`, and `clear`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml` | RA temperate tileset and brushes used by `ClassicMapGenerator`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml` | RA snow tileset and brushes. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml` | RA desert tileset and brushes. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` | Arrakis tileset and brushes used by `D2kMapGenerator`. |

## Architecture

### Two-level architecture

Each generator is a `[TraitInfo](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)` located on `SystemActors.EditorWorld`. The actual class is split into two parts:

1. **The `Info` class** (`ClassicMapGeneratorInfo`, `D2kMapGeneratorInfo`, `ClearMapGeneratorInfo`) — implements `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` and owns:
   - `Type`, `Name`, `Tilesets`, `MapTitle`, `PanelWidget` metadata.
   - A `Settings` MiniYaml subtree describing the editor UI options.
   - A `Generate` method that is the real map generation routine.
   - `TryGenerateMetadata` for player count and rule definitions.

2. **The generator tool class** (`ClassicMapGenerator`, `D2kMapGenerator`, `ClearMapGenerator`) — implements `IEditorTool` and is what the editor UI instantiates when the tool is selected.

### Common interface

All generators implement `IMapGeneratorInfo`:

```csharp
public interface IMapGeneratorInfo : ITraitInfoInterface
{
    string Type { get; }
    string Name { get; }
    string MapTitle { get; }
    Map Generate(ModData modData, MapGenerationArgs args);
    bool TryGenerateMetadata(...);
}
```

Editor-visible generators also implement `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo`:

```csharp
public interface IEditorMapGeneratorInfo : IMapGeneratorInfo
{
    ImmutableArray<string> Tilesets { get; }
    IMapGeneratorSettings GetSettings();
}
```

`GetSettings` returns a `MapGeneratorSettings` object that parses the `Settings` MiniYaml and exposes the options the editor UI renders.

### Shared algorithm layer
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_06_Mod_Generators-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


Every generator follows the same broad pattern:

1. Create a new `Map` from `modData.DefaultTerrainInfo[args.Tileset]` and the requested size.
2. Create an `[ActorPlan](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)` list.
3. Build a `Parameters` object by loading generator-specific YAML settings via `FieldLoader.Load`.
4. Instantiate `Terraformer` with the chosen symmetry.
5. Seed a master `MersenneTwister` from `param.Seed`, then derive independent sub-generators for each phase.
6. Initialize the map to a default tile.
7. Run terrain phases (water, rock, cliffs, forests, dunes, ramps, etc.).
8. Place actors, resources, and decorations.
9. Call `ReorderPlayerSpawns()` and `BakeMap()`.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Entry point

When a user clicks the random-map button, the engine:

1. Looks up the generator by `Type` under `^MapGenerators:`.
2. Calls `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo.GetSettings()` to build the option panel.
3. Collects user choices into a `MapGenerationArgs`.
4. Calls `IMapGeneratorInfo.Generate(modData, args)`.
5. Calls `TryGenerateMetadata` to produce player definitions.

Inside `Generate`, the first thing each generator does is:

```csharp
var terrainInfo = modData.DefaultTerrainInfo[args.Tileset];
var size = args.Size;
var map = new Map(modData, terrainInfo, size);
var actorPlans = new List<ActorPlan>();
var param = new Parameters(map, args.Settings);
var terraformer = new Terraformer(args, map, modData, actorPlans, param.Mirror, param.Rotations);
```

### Per-phase random generators

Every generator derives many independent `MersenneTwister` instances from a single seed. This keeps the phases reproducible: changing the forest algorithm should not change the coastline.

### Finalization

At the end of every generator:

```csharp
terraformer.ReorderPlayerSpawns();
terraformer.BakeMap();
return map;
```

`ReorderPlayerSpawns` sorts `mpspawn` actors clockwise around the map center. `BakeMap` commits the `ActorPlans` and creates player definitions.

## Configuration (YAML)

Cameo's `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` registers three generators:

```yaml
^MapGenerators:
    ClassicMapGenerator@classic:
        Type: classic
        Name: map-generator-classic
        Tilesets: RA_TEMPERAT, RA_SNOW, RA_DESERT
        Settings:
            ...
    D2kMapGenerator@d2k:
        Type: d2k
        Name: map-generator-d2k
        Tilesets: ARRAKIS
        Settings:
            ...
    ClearMapGenerator@clear:
        Type: clear
        Name: map-generator-clear
        Tilesets: RA_TEMPERAT, RA_SNOW, RA_DESERT, RA_INTERIOR, ARRAKIS, TEMPERAT, DESERT
        Settings:
            ...
```

### Classic generator parameters

The `ClassicMapGenerator` `Parameters` class loads settings such as:

| Setting group | Examples |
| :---- | :---- |
| Terrain shaping | `TerrainFeatureSize`, `Water`, `Mountains`, `Forests`, `TerrainSmoothing` |
| Symmetry | `Mirror`, `Rotations`, `EnforceSymmetry` |
| Roads | `Roads`, `RoadSpacing`, `RoadShrink`, `RoadSegmentTypes` |
| Resources | `DefaultResource`, `ResourceSpawnSeeds`, `ResourcesPerPlayer`, `SpawnResourceSpawns` |
| Civilian buildings | `CivilianBuildings`, `BuildingWeights`, `MinimumBuildings`, `MaximumBuildings` |
| Spawn fairness | `CentralSpawnReservationFraction`, `SpawnRegionSize`, `SpawnBuildSize`, `MinimumSpawnRadius` |

### D2k generator parameters

The `D2kMapGenerator` uses a different parameter set tuned for Arrakis:

| Setting group | Examples |
| :---- | :---- |
| Terrain shaping | `Rock`, `SandCliffs`, `Dunes`, `TerrainFeatureSize`, `SandDetail` |
| Rock/sand/cliff thickness | `MinimumRockSandThickness`, `MinimumSandCliffThickness`, `MinimumDuneThickness` |
| Spice | `ResourceFeatureSize`, `Spice`, spice-spawn and expansion weights |
| Symmetry | `Mirror`, `Rotations` |

### Clear generator parameters

The `ClearMapGenerator` only needs a tile type per tileset. Cameo's YAML provides a `MultiChoiceOption@Tile` with tile indices for each supported tileset.

## Interconnectivity

- **Depends on:** `Terraformer`, `MultiBrush`, `TilingPath`, `NoiseUtils`, `MatrixUtils`, `CellLayerUtils`, `ActorPlan`, `MapGeneratorSettings`.
- **Used by:** The map chooser (`MapGeneratorLogic`) and the editor generator tool (`MapGeneratorToolLogic`).

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo has no custom generator class in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` or `OpenRA.Mods.CA`. Divergence is in YAML configuration:

- Cameo registers `ClassicMapGenerator` for `RA_TEMPERAT`, `RA_SNOW`, and `RA_DESERT`.
- Cameo registers `D2kMapGenerator` for the `ARRAKIS` tileset.
- Cameo registers `ClearMapGenerator` for a broader set of tilesets than the base mods.
- Resource and building presets are tuned for Cameo's multi-franchise economy (Tiberium variants, Ore, Gems, etc.).
- The base `TSMapGenerator` (Tiberian Sun) is **not** registered in Cameo because Cameo does not expose the TS tileset to the RMG.

## Practical notes

- To add a brand-new generator to Cameo, create a class implementing `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` or `OpenRA.Mods.CA`, add a YAML entry under `^MapGenerators:`, and add Fluent labels.
- To add a new tileset to an existing generator, extend the `Tilesets` field and ensure the tileset contains compatible `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` entries.

- Part 7.5 — MultiBrush (Cameo)
- Part 7.7 — Resources and Actor Placement (Cameo)

# Chapter 7.7 — Resource and Actor Placement (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_07_Resources_Actors}

## Purpose

This chapter documents the subsystem that decides **where resources and [actors](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) go on procedurally generated maps**. After terrain, elevation, water, and forests have been carved out, the map generator must place player spawns, resource fields, neutral structures, expansion points, and decorative actors without breaking fairness, symmetry, or playability.

Cameo uses the upstream placement code in `[Terraformer](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary).cs` and `Symmetry.cs` with custom YAML mappings for Cameo's multi-franchise resources and neutral actors.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain how resources and actors are placed on procedurally generated maps while respecting fairness and symmetry.
- Describe the roles of `Terraformer`, `ActorPlan`, and `Symmetry` in placement.
- Build zoneable masks that exclude invalid terrain, ramps, actors, and resources.
- Use `ResourceBias` and `PlanResources`/`GrowResources` to create resource fields.
- Identify Cameo's `ResourceSpawnSeeds` and `BuildingWeights` mappings.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_07_Resources_Actors-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Terraformer.cs` | High-level placement utilities: `PlanResources`, `GrowResources`, spawn placement, actor placement, zone management, `BakeMap`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/ActorPlan.cs` | Lightweight draft description of an actor to be placed on a map. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/Symmetry.cs` | Mirror and rotational helpers for duplicating points, cell layers, and `ActorPlan`s. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClassicMapGenerator.cs` | Primary consumer; orchestrates terrain generation then calls `Terraformer` to place spawns, resources, expansions, and buildings. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MultiBrush.cs` | Paints tiles and embedded `ActorPlan`s. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/CellLayerUtils.cs` | Grid conversion helpers and `PickWeighted` / `FindRandomBest` primitives. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ResourceLayer.cs` | `ResourceLayerInfo` / `ResourceTypeInfo` and the `ResourceTypes` table. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo resource and actor placement parameters. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` | Cameo `ResourceLayer`/`ResourceRenderer` definitions and resource types. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/misc.yaml` | Resource-actor templates (`split*`, `mine`, `gmine`) referenced by `ResourceSpawnSeeds`. |

## Architecture

### Core objects

```
[Terraformer] --owns--> [Map, ModData, ActorPlans]
[Terraformer] --uses--> [Symmetry.WMirror]
[Terraformer] --creates--> [ActorPlan]
[ActorPlan] --references--> [ActorReference, ActorInfo, Map]
[ClassicMapGenerator] --orchestrates--> [Terraformer]
[MultiBrush] --embeds--> [ActorPlan]
```

### `Terraformer`

`Terraformer` is the central utility class for a single map generation pass. It is constructed with `MapGenerationArgs`, the mutable `Map`, `ModData`, the shared `List<ActorPlan>`, and the symmetry group (`WMirror` + `Rotations`). It lazily computes `ProjectionSpacing`, a `CellLayer<int>` that records, for each cell, half the minimum distance to any of its symmetry-projected positions. This layer prevents placements from colliding with their own mirror images.

### `ActorPlan`

`ActorPlan` is a draft actor. It stores:

- `Map` and `ActorInfo`.
- `ActorReference` with `LocationInit` and `OwnerInit`.
- `Location` (CPos) and `WPosLocation` / `WPosCenterLocation`.
- `Footprint()` — occupied cells derived from `IOccupySpaceInfo.OccupiedCells`.
- `Clone()` — clones the underlying `ActorReference` for symmetry projection.

### `Symmetry`

`Symmetry` defines the symmetry group:

- `Mirror` enum: `None`, `LeftMatchesRight`, `TopLeftMatchesBottomRight`, `TopMatchesBottom`, `TopRightMatchesBottomLeft`.
- `WMirror` adapts a mirror from `WPos` to `CPos`. For `RectangularIsometric` grids, the mirror index is rotated by 2.
- `RotateAndMirrorActorPlan` clones an `ActorPlan` at each projected position.
- `RotateAndMirrorOverCPos` iterates every cell and applies a callback to each symmetry orbit.

### `ResourceBias`
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_07_Resources_Actors-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


`ResourceBias` tells `PlanResources` how to treat a specific location:

- `WPos` — anchor point.
- `ExclusionRadius` — no resources within this distance.
- `BiasRadius` — bias function applied within this distance.
- `Bias` — transforms per-resource strength based on squared world distance.
- `ResourceType` — restricts the bias to one resource type.

## Data Flow / Code Path

The canonical caller is `ClassicMapGenerator.Generate`. After terrain and water are resolved, the flow is:

### 1. Build the zoneable mask

```csharp
zoneable = terraformer.GetZoneable(param.ZoneableTerrain, playable)
```

`GetZoneable` intersects playable terrain with bounds, ramps, actors, and resources, then runs `ImproveSymmetry` so a cell is only zoneable if all of its symmetry projections are also zoneable.

### 2. Place player spawns

For each symmetry group:

```csharp
chosenCPos = terraformer.ChooseSpawnInZoneable(...)
spawn = new ActorPlan(map, "mpspawn") { Location = chosenCPos }
resourceSpawnPreferences = terraformer.TargetWalkingDistance(...)
terraformer.AddDistributedActors(
    zoneable, resourceSpawnPreferences,
    param.ResourceSpawnWeights,
    param.SpawnResourceSpawns,
    weighted: false,
    actorDezoneRadius: ResourceSpawnReservation)
terraformer.ProjectPlaceDezoneActor(spawn, zoneable, SpawnReservation)
```

### 3. Place expansion resources

`AddDistributedActors` is called again with `ExpansionResourceSpawnWeights` and `MaximumExpansionResourceSpawns` to place resource fields away from player spawns.

### 4. Place neutral buildings and props

`AddActorCluster` and `AddDistributedActors` place civilian buildings and props using `BuildingWeights` and `CivilianBuildingDensity` parameters.

### 5. Bake

`ReorderPlayerSpawns` numbers spawns clockwise, then `BakeMap` commits actor definitions and player slots.

## Configuration (YAML)

### Cameo `ResourceSpawnSeeds`

`mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` maps resource-actor template names to resource types:

```yaml
ResourceSpawnSeeds:
    mine: Ore
    gmine: Gems
    split2: Tiberium
    splitblue: BlueTiberium
    splitred: RedTiberium
    splitgold: GoldTiberium
```

These actors are defined in `mods/cameo/rules/misc.yaml`. `mine` is a standard ore mine, `gmine` is a gem mine, and the `split*` actors are Tiberium trees that seed the corresponding resource type via `SeedsResource`.

### Resource presets

The `Resources` choice in the classic generator sets:

| Preset | `SpawnResourceSpawns` | `ResourcesPerPlayer` | Main resource | Expansion resources |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| None | 0 | 0 | — | — |
| Low | 2 | 18,750 | mine / split2 | splitblue / splitred / splitgold / gmine |
| Medium | 3 | 37,500 | mine / split2 | splitblue / splitred / splitgold / gmine |
| High | 3 | 56,250 | mine / split2 | splitblue / splitred / splitgold / gmine |
| Very High | 4 | 75,000 | mine / split2 | splitblue / splitred / splitgold / gmine |
| Full | 0 | 1,000,000,000 | — | — |

### Building weights

The `Buildings` choice controls which neutral buildings appear:

```yaml
BuildingWeights:
    oilb: 9
    hosp: 2
    miss: 1
    fcom: 3
```

These reference actors in `mods/cameo/rules/civilian.yaml`, `mods/cameo/rules/tech.yaml`, etc.

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_07_Resources_Actors-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:** `Terraformer`, `ActorPlan`, `Symmetry`, `ResourceLayer`, `CellLayerUtils`.
- **Used by:** `ClassicMapGenerator` and `D2kMapGenerator`.

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo does not modify the placement algorithms. Divergence is in the content:

- `ResourceSpawnSeeds` includes Tiberium variants (`split2`, `splitblue`, `splitred`, `splitgold`) not present in the base Red Alert mod.
- `ExpansionResourceSpawnWeights` and `ResourceSpawnWeights` are tuned for Cameo's combined economy.
- `BuildingWeights` reference Cameo's neutral/tech actors (`oilb`, `hosp`, `miss`, `fcom`).
- The `World` rules in `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` define many resource types, but only those listed in the generator's `ResourceSpawnSeeds` are actually placed by the RMG.

## Practical notes

- The `DefaultResource` field determines which resource type is placed around player spawns by default.
- `SpawnResourceSpawns` and `ResourcesPerPlayer` are the main knobs for starting economy.
- `MaximumExpansionResourceSpawns` controls how many extra resource fields are placed on the map for expansion.
- If a resource actor template is missing from `ResourceSpawnSeeds`, the generator will not place it, even if the resource type is defined in `ResourceLayer`.

# Chapter 7.8 — Random Map Generator Extension Points (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_08_Extension_Points}

## Purpose

The OpenRA [Random Map Generator (RMG)](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) is deliberately split into reusable pieces. The shared engine code in `OpenRA.Mods.Common` provides the toolbox (`[Terraformer](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)`, `TilingPath`, `[MultiBrush](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)`, `MatrixUtils`, `CellLayerUtils`, and `NoiseUtils`), while each mod provides its own generator class and YAML configuration that decides how to use that toolbox. This chapter describes the formal extension points and how to use them within Cameo.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the formal extension points for OpenRA's random map generator.
- Implement a new generator by creating `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` and `IEditorTool` classes.
- Configure generator options using `MapGeneratorSettings` and the four option types.
- Add new tileset brush collections under `MultiBrushCollections`.
- Extend an existing generator with new YAML options without recompiling the engine.

## Files
![Architecture diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_08_Extension_Points-architecture-diagram-showing-the-main-classes-interfaces-and-9161e6.svg)


| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | Core `IMapGeneratorInfo` interface. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo`, `IMapGeneratorSettings`, `MapGenerationException`. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MapGeneratorSettings.cs` | `MapGeneratorSettings` and the four option types. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClearMapGenerator.cs` | Minimal example of a generator and editor tool. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClassicMapGenerator.cs` | Complex generator with a full `Parameters` class and YAML settings. |
| `OpenRA.Mods.D2k/Traits/World/D2kMapGenerator.cs` | Mod-specific generator example. |
| `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` | Cameo YAML registration of `classic`, `d2k`, and `clear`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_temperat.yaml` | RA temperate `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_snow.yaml` | RA snow `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/ra_desert.yaml` | RA desert `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |
| `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` | Arrakis `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented`. |

## Architecture

### Two interfaces every generator must implement

The generator contract is defined in two layers:

```
[IMapGeneratorInfo] <--extends-- [IEditorMapGeneratorInfo]
```

`IMapGeneratorInfo` (engine) is the runtime contract:

```csharp
public interface IMapGeneratorInfo : ITraitInfoInterface
{
    string Type { get; }
    string Name { get; }
    string MapTitle { get; }
    Map Generate(ModData modData, MapGenerationArgs args);
    bool TryGenerateMetadata(ModData modData, MapGenerationArgs args, out MapPlayers players, out Dictionary<string, MiniYaml> rules);
}
```

`IEditorMapGeneratorInfo` (Common) adds editor integration:

```csharp
public interface IEditorMapGeneratorInfo : IMapGeneratorInfo
{
    ImmutableArray<string> Tilesets { get; }
    IMapGeneratorSettings GetSettings();
}
```

A generator is a `[TraitInfo]` placed on `SystemActors.EditorWorld`. The concrete generator class only implements `IEditorTool` and is what the editor UI instantiates; the heavy work is done by the `Info` class. This mirrors the normal OpenRA trait pattern.

### Settings and option objects

The editor option panel is produced by `IMapGeneratorSettings.GetSettings()`. The canonical implementation is `MapGeneratorSettings` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/MapGenerator/MapGeneratorSettings.cs`. It parses a `Settings` MiniYaml subtree and creates a typed option object for each:

- `BooleanOption@`
- `IntegerOption@`
- `MultiChoiceOption@`
- `MultiIntegerChoiceOption@`

Choices in a `MultiChoiceOption` can be gated by `Tileset` and `Players`.

### The `Parameters` bridge

Every non-trivial generator defines an inner `Parameters` class. The constructor receives the map and the `MapGenerationArgs` produced by the settings object, then uses `[FieldLoader](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary).Load` to turn the emitted MiniYaml into typed fields. `Parameters` is where a mod author declares every tunable knob without changing the engine code.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Adding a new generator from scratch

1. Create a class `MyMapGeneratorInfo` that inherits `TraitInfo` and implements `IEditorMapGeneratorInfo`.
2. Declare required metadata fields: `Type`, `Name`, `Tilesets`, `MapTitle`, and `PanelWidget`.
3. Add a `Settings` MiniYaml field and a `GetSettings()` method returning `new MapGeneratorSettings(this, Settings)`.
4. Implement `Generate(ModData, MapGenerationArgs)` to create a `Map`, build a `Parameters`, instantiate `Terraformer`, run phases, and call `BakeMap()`.
5. Implement `TryGenerateMetadata(...)` to return a `MapPlayers` block and any rule overrides.
6. Implement `Create(...)` to return the `IEditorTool` instance (usually just a wrapper).
7. Add the generator to `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml` under `^MapGenerators:`.
8. Add Fluent labels for `Name`, option labels, and choice labels in `mods/cameo/fluent/en.ftl`.

### Minimal generator example: ClearMapGenerator

`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ClearMapGenerator.cs` is the smallest possible generator. It declares metadata, returns a single `MapGeneratorSettings` that expects a `Tile` parameter, and produces a flat map of that tile. This is useful as a template because it shows every required step.

### Extending an existing generator without C# changes

Because the `Parameters` class is loaded via `FieldLoader`, adding a new scalar or boolean key to a generator's YAML settings is usually enough to change behavior, provided the generator's code reads that key. In Cameo, many customizations are done this way:

- Add a new `Choice@` under an existing `MultiChoiceOption@` in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`.
- Override numeric fields such as `TerrainFeatureSize`, `Water`, `Mountains`, `ResourcesPerPlayer`, etc.
- Add new `MultiBrush` entries to `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` in a tileset YAML.

### Adding new tileset brush collections

To add a new segmented brush collection to a Cameo tileset:

1. Add `MultiBrush@<id>` entries under `MultiBrushCollections/Segmented` in the tileset YAML.
2. Ensure the segment `Start`/`End` names match the generator's `*SegmentTypes` settings.
3. Run `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Lint/CheckMultiBrushes.cs` will catch malformed entries at load time.

For example, the Arrakis `RockSmooth.R` segments in `mods/cameo/tilesets/arrakis.yaml` are consumed by `D2kMapGenerator` settings.

## Cameo-specific notes

- Cameo currently has no custom generator in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` or `OpenRA.Mods.CA`. All generation is performed by upstream `ClassicMapGenerator`, `D2kMapGenerator`, and `ClearMapGenerator`.
- The most common extension in Cameo is **YAML-level**: adding new presets, adjusting resource/building weights, or extending `Tilesets` lists.
- To register a custom generator in Cameo, place the trait in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` (or `OpenRA.Mods.CA`), ensure the assembly is referenced in `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`, and add a YAML entry under `^MapGenerators:`.
- Cameo's `CAMEO`, `WC2*`, `OUTPOST2`, `BARREN`, and other non-RMG tilesets can be used for manual maps but are not yet wired into the RMG.

## Interconnectivity
![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_07_Chapter_08_Extension_Points-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:** `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs`, `OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs`, `MapGeneratorSettings`, `Terraformer`.
- **Used by:** The editor (`MapGeneratorToolLogic`) and map chooser (`MapGeneratorLogic`).

## Divergence from upstream OpenRA

Cameo has no code-level divergence in the RMG extension points. It uses the standard OpenRA interfaces and option types. The divergence is in the content registered through those extension points:

- Different generator `Tilesets` lists.
- Different `MultiBrushCollections` data.
- Different `Parameters` values in `mods/cameo/rules/map-generators.yaml`.

# Chapter 7.9 — Random Map Generator File Index (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_09_File_Index}

## Purpose

This chapter is a curated reference of the files involved in random/procedural map generation for the Cameo mod, grouped by role so a developer can locate the right source when extending or debugging a generator.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Navigate the RMG file structure across engine, common, mod, and YAML configuration.
- Locate the interface contracts, shared infrastructure, and mod-specific generators used by Cameo.
- Identify Cameo YAML files for generator registration and tileset brushes.
- Find the editor and UI files that host generator panels.

## Core Engine Contracts

| File | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs` | Defines `IMapGeneratorInfo`, the base interface implemented by every generator. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/Map.cs` | The `Map` object being generated; holds `Tiles`, `Resources`, `ActorDefinitions`, `MapPlayers`, and `AllCells`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Map/MapGrid.cs` | Grid coordinate geometry; determines how cell indices map to world positions. |
| `OpenRA.Game/MiniYaml.cs` | MiniYaml parsing and merging; `MapGenerationArgs.Settings` is a `MiniYaml` object. |
| `OpenRA.Game/FieldLoader.cs` | Loads YAML values into C# fields via attributes such as `[FieldLoader.Require]`, `[FieldLoader.LoadUsing]`, and `[FieldLoader.Ignore]`. |
| `OpenRA.Game/FieldSaver.cs` | Formats C# values back into YAML strings used by option emission. |
| `OpenRA.Game/Support/MersenneTwister.cs` | Deterministic random source used by all generators. |
| `OpenRA.Support/Exts.cs` | Utility helpers such as `TryParseUshortInvariant`. |

# Chapter 8.1 — Bot Architecture and IBot (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_08_Chapter_01_IBot}

## Purpose

OpenRA's [bot](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) framework is built around the idea that **bot logic is not allowed to mutate the [world](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) directly**. Instead, a bot is a player-level trait that observes the world, decides what [orders](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) to issue, and queues those orders through the normal order system. Because orders go through the same lockstep pipeline as human orders, bot actions are recorded in replays and stay synchronized across clients.

Cameo reuses this upstream architecture unchanged but replaces the default bot modules with its own. The engine's `ModularBot` still coordinates everything, yet the modules that make decisions are the Cameo/Combined Arms variants (`BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`, `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`, `HarvesterBotModuleCA`, `SquadManagerBotModuleCA`) plus Cameo-specific helpers (`DeployBotModule`, `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA`, `BotGlobalUnitBudget`, `BotLimits`). This chapter introduces the core interfaces (`IBot`, `IBotInfo`, `IBotTick`) and the modular pipeline that runs them, then explains how Cameo modules plug into that pipeline.

## Learning Objectives
![Practical example: a bot builds a power plant diagram](images/Part_08_Chapter_01_IBot-end-to-end-worked-example-diagram-showing-the-inputs-interme-5fc6a2.svg)


After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

1. Explain why bot logic is forbidden from mutating world state directly and must issue orders instead.
2. Describe the responsibilities of `IBot`, `IBotInfo`, and `ModularBot`.
3. List the common bot module callback interfaces (`IBotTick`, `IBotEnabled`, `IBotRespondToAttack`, etc.) and when each is invoked.
4. Trace bot activation, the per-tick decision loop, and attack-response dispatch.
5. Explain how `ModularBot` throttles orders and why `RunUnsynced` is used around bot code.
6. Register a bot type and configure modules in a mod's AI YAML, including Cameo's difficulty-scaled `BotLimits`.
7. Diagnose common bot issues such as stalled construction, unresponsive defense, order flooding, and units hitting a global budget cap.
8. Explain how Cameo's `*CA` modules differ from the upstream modules they replace and how `BotGlobalUnitBudget` limits production.

## Practical Example: A Bot Builds a Power Plant

When a rush-style AI decides it needs more power:

1. **Bot activation.** At game start, the engine creates the bot's `PlayerActor` and calls `IBot.Activate`. `ModularBot` caches references to all modules on the actor that implement `IBotTick` and `IBotRespondToAttack`.
2. **Tick entry.** Every simulation tick, `ModularBot.Tick` runs inside a `PerfSample` and wraps module logic in `Sync.RunUnsynced(...)` so that bot-private calculations do not affect the sync hash.
3. **Base builder decision.** `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` (an `IBotTick` module) checks the current power surplus, `BuildingFractions`, `BuildingLimits`, and any `BotLimits` refineries/construction caps. It decides that a power plant is required.
4. **Order queuing.** The module calls `bot.QueueOrder(Order.StartProduction(...))` with `Subject` set to the construction yard and `TargetString` set to the power plant actor name.
5. **Order throttling.** `ModularBot.Tick` dequeues only a fraction of the pending orders each tick based on `MinOrderQuotientPerTick`. This prevents the bot from dumping a large burst of orders onto the network in a single frame.
6. **Order issue.** The selected order is passed to `world.IssueOrder`, which routes it through `OrderManager` exactly like a human order.
7. **Production resolve.** The construction yard's `ProductionQueue` trait receives the order via `ResolveOrder`, starts production, and eventually places the building when the player has enough funds.
8. **Placement confirmation.** A second queued order (e.g., `PlaceBuilding`) is issued when the power plant is ready, and the building appears on the map on the same simulation frame for every client.

This example shows how a bot decision becomes a sequence of normal orders that stay synchronized, replayable, and fair in multiplayer, whether the module is the upstream `BaseBuilderBotModule` or Cameo's `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`.

## Architecture

### Core interfaces

The engine defines two minimal interfaces in `OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IBotInfo : ITraitInfoInterface
{
    string Type { get; }
    string Name { get; }
}

public interface IBot
{
    void Activate(Player p);
    void QueueOrder(Order order);
    IBotInfo Info { get; }
    Player Player { get; }
}
```

Every bot is a player-level [trait](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) whose `Info` class implements `IBotInfo` and whose instance class implements `IBot`. The engine activates the bot when the player is created, and the bot then queues orders through `QueueOrder`.

### ModularBot

The current bot system is `ModularBot` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ModularBot.cs`. It is a `TraitInfo` located on `SystemActors.Player` and implements `ITick` and `INotifyDamage`. The class itself is a thin coordinator:

```csharp
public sealed class ModularBot : ITick, IBot, INotifyDamage
{
    readonly Queue<Order> orders = [];
    IBotTick[] tickModules;
    IBotRespondToAttack[] attackResponseModules;
    ...
}
```

`ModularBot` does not contain any AI strategy itself. It discovers modules on the same `PlayerActor` that implement `IBotTick`, `IBotRespondToAttack`, or other bot callback interfaces, and invokes them at the right times.

### Bot module callback interfaces
![Data flow  code path diagram](images/Part_08_Chapter_01_IBot-sequence-flow-diagram-tracing-the-execution-path-from-trigge-035864.svg)


`OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs` defines the callbacks that modules can subscribe to:

| Interface | Callback | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `IBotEnabled` | `BotEnabled(IBot bot)` | One-time setup when the bot is activated. |
| `IBotTick` | `BotTick(IBot bot)` | Called every tick for ongoing decision-making. |
| `IBotRespondToAttack` | `RespondToAttack(IBot bot, Actor self, AttackInfo e)` | Called when the bot's actor is damaged. |
| `IBotPositionsUpdated` | `UpdatedBaseCenter(CPos)` / `UpdatedDefenseCenter(CPos)` | Receives base/defense center updates from `BaseBuilderBotModule`. |
| `IBotNotifyIdleBaseUnits` | `UpdatedIdleBaseUnits(List<UnitWposWrapper>)` | Receives idle unit counts from `SquadManagerBotModule`. |
| `IBotRequestUnitProduction` | `RequestUnitProduction(...)` / `RequestedProductionCount(...)` | Allows one module to request units from another. |
| `IBotRequestPauseUnitProduction` | `PauseUnitProduction { get; }` | Tells `UnitBuilderBotModule` to pause production. |
| `IBotBaseExpansion` | `UpdateExpansionParams(...)` | Receives base expansion decisions from `McvManagerBotModule`. |
| `IBotSuggestRefineryProduction` | `RequestLocation(...)` | Suggests refinery placement locations. |

A module is a normal `ConditionalTrait<TInfo>` that implements one or more of these interfaces. Modules are placed on the `PlayerActor` in the mod's AI YAML.

### Cameo-specific bot architecture

Cameo uses the same `ModularBot`/`IBot` pipeline but ships its own modules and support traits. The high-level rule is: **the engine's coordinator is unchanged; only the decision-making modules are Cameo-specific.**

#### CA bot modules replacing the upstream defaults

The four core CA modules live in `OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/BotModules/` and implement the same callback interfaces as their upstream counterparts, so `ModularBot` discovers and runs them without any special logic:

* `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` implements `IBotTick`, `IBotPositionsUpdated`, and `IBotRespondToAttack`. It is the Cameo equivalent of `BaseBuilderBotModule` and delegates per-queue work to `BaseBuilderQueueManagerCA` instances. On `RespondToAttack`, it can decide to sell a damaged non-essential building or broadcast the attack location as a new defense center.
* `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA` implements `IBotTick`, `IBotNotifyIdleBaseUnits`, `IBotRequestUnitProduction`, and `IBotAircraftBuilder`. It is the Cameo equivalent of `UnitBuilderBotModule`, with support for parallel production queues (e.g., Zerg-style larva slots) and air-superiority logic (`MaintainAirSuperiority`, `AirToAirUnits`, `AirThreatUnits`).
* `HarvesterBotModuleCA` implements `IBotTick` and `IWorldLoaded`. It is the Cameo equivalent of `HarvesterBotModule`, periodically ordering idle harvesters to new resource patches and requesting replacement harvesters when the count is too low.
* `SquadManagerBotModuleCA` implements `IBotEnabled`, `IBotTick`, `IBotRespondToAttack`, and `IBotPositionsUpdated`. It is the Cameo equivalent of `SquadManagerBotModule`, but adds Cameo-specific concepts such as `GuerrillaTypes`/`MaxGuerrillaSize`, `SquadValue`/`SquadValueRandomBonus`, `HighValueTargetPriority`, `AirToAirPriority`, `AirSquadTargetTypes`, and `IndirectRouteChance`.

Because each module is a `ConditionalTrait<TInfo>` and implements the same engine interfaces, `ModularBot` treats them exactly like upstream modules: it iterates `tickModules` each tick and `attackResponseModules` on damage, skipping any module whose `IsTraitEnabled()` returns false.

#### Cameo-specific helpers

Cameo adds three additional modules that have no upstream equivalent:

* `DeployBotModule` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/BotModules/DeployBotModule.cs`) implements `IBotTick`. It is notified by `AutoDeployer` traits during the tick and, when the configured `DeployChance` succeeds, queues the deploy/undeploy orders for those units. The module itself does not mutate actor state; it only adds `Order` objects to `bot.QueueOrder`.
* `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/BotModules/PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA.cs`) implements `IBotTick` and `IResolveOrder`. It periodically scans the bot's buildings for a `Pluggable` that accepts the configured `Plug`, then issues a `PlacePlugAI` order. The order is resolved on the same player actor by adding the plug at the end of the frame, taking cash if `IgnoreCost` is false. This is a normal order just like any other bot order; it flows through the lockstep pipeline.
* `BotGlobalUnitBudget` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/BotGlobalUnitBudget.cs`) implements `IBotRequestPauseUnitProduction`. It does **not** tick directly; instead, `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA` queries all `IBotRequestPauseUnitProduction` implementations before producing units. If the bot's current mobile combat-unit count has reached its share of a global budget (`GlobalUnitBudget / living bots`, clamped by `MaxUnitsPerBot` and `MinUnitsPerBot`), the property returns `true` and `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA` stops queuing combat units for that tick. `IgnoreHarvesters` and `IgnoredActorTypes` keep the economy from being starved by the cap. The share is recomputed only every `RecalculationInterval` ticks for performance.

#### `BotLimits` integration

`BotLimits` (`OpenRA.Mods.CA/Traits/BotModules/BotLimits.cs`) is not a bot module in the `IBotTick` sense. It is a `ConditionalTrait<BotLimitsInfo>` that is enabled per-difficulty through `GrantConditionOnBotOwner` in `mods/cameo/ai/ai.yaml`. The other CA modules look it up in `Created` or `TraitEnabled` and use its fields to scale behavior:

* `RefineryLimit` is read by `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` and `HarvesterBotModuleCA` to cap refineries and harvesters.
* `HarvesterLimit` is read by `HarvesterBotModuleCA`.
* `BuildingDelayModifier` and `BuildingIntervalModifier` are used by `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` to scale `BuildingDelays` and `BuildingIntervals`.
* `UnitDelayModifier` and `UnitIntervalModifier` are used by `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA` to scale `UnitDelays` and `UnitIntervals`.
* `InitialAttackDelay` is used by `SquadManagerBotModuleCA` to delay the first attack force on lower difficulties.
* `ConstructionYardLimit` and `ProductionTypeLimit` are available for the same kind of difficulty-driven scaling.

This is why `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` cannot be understood in isolation: its effective delay windows and refinery caps are set at runtime by the `BotLimits` instance active for the chosen difficulty.

## Data Flow / Code Path

### Bot activation

When a player is created with a bot type, the engine calls `IBot.Activate`:

```csharp
public void Activate(Player p)
{
    if (p.World.IsReplay)
        return;

    IsEnabled = true;
    player = p;
    tickModules = p.PlayerActor.TraitsImplementing<IBotTick>().ToArray();
    attackResponseModules = p.PlayerActor.TraitsImplementing<IBotRespondToAttack>().ToArray();
    foreach (var ibe in p.PlayerActor.TraitsImplementing<IBotEnabled>())
        ibe.BotEnabled(this);
}
```

Bots are disabled during replays because replays only replay orders, not bot decision-making. In Cameo, this means `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`, `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`, `HarvesterBotModuleCA`, `SquadManagerBotModuleCA`, `DeployBotModule`, and `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA` are all discovered by the same `TraitsImplementing<IBotTick>()` call, while `SquadManagerBotModuleCA` and `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` are also discovered as `IBotRespondToAttack` modules.

### Per-tick decision loop

`ModularBot.Tick` runs each `IBotTick` module in `Sync.RunUnsynced`, which allows bot code to use world-local state without affecting the sync hash:

```csharp
void ITick.Tick(Actor self)
{
    if (!IsEnabled || self.World.IsLoadingGameSave)
        return;

    using (new PerfSample("bot_tick"))
    {
        Sync.RunUnsynced(Game.Settings.Debug.SyncCheckBotModuleCode, world, () =>
        {
            foreach (var t in tickModules)
                if (t.IsTraitEnabled())
                    t.BotTick(this);
        });
    }

    var ordersToIssueThisTick = Math.Min((orders.Count + info.MinOrderQuotientPerTick - 1) / info.MinOrderQuotientPerTick, orders.Count);
    for (var i = 0; i < ordersToIssueThisTick; i++)
        world.IssueOrder(orders.Dequeue());
}
```

Modules call `bot.QueueOrder(order)` to add orders. The bot issues a configurable fraction of the queue each tick to avoid network spikes and to keep the bot from looking too robotic. In Cameo, this single loop drives `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`, `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`, `HarvesterBotModuleCA`, `SquadManagerBotModuleCA`, `DeployBotModule`, and `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA` simultaneously.

### Attack response

When the bot player actor is damaged, `INotifyDamage.Damaged` dispatches to `IBotRespondToAttack` modules:

```csharp
void INotifyDamage.Damaged(Actor self, AttackInfo e)
{
    ...
    Sync.RunUnsynced(..., () =>
    {
        foreach (var t in attackResponseModules)
            if (t.IsTraitEnabled())
                t.RespondToAttack(this, self, e);
    });
}
```

This is how the harvester, base defense, and squad modules react to raids without waiting for the next tick. In Cameo, both `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` (which may sell damaged buildings or move the defense center) and `SquadManagerBotModuleCA` (which creates a protection squad) are triggered by this path.

### Order issuing
![Configuration (yaml) diagram](images/Part_08_Chapter_01_IBot-annotated-yaml-snippet-diagram-showing-the-key-fields-and-ho-6a1b98.svg)


`world.IssueOrder` places the order into the local order manager. From there, the order follows the same path as human orders: it is serialized to the local command queue, sent to the server if multiplayer, and executed on the next simulation tick. Cameo-specific orders such as `PlacePlugAI` are no different in this respect; they are still processed through the same `OrderManager` and `ResolveOrder` pipeline.

## Configuration (YAML)

### Bot registration

Cameo bots are defined in `mods/cameo/ai/ai.yaml`. A minimal Cameo-style bot entry looks like this:

```yaml
^AIDifficulties:
    BotLimits@medium:
        ProductionTypeLimit: 3
        ConstructionYardLimit: 2
        RefineryLimit: 4
        HarvesterLimit: 12
        BuildingDelayModifier: 175
        BuildingIntervalModifier: 175
        UnitDelayModifier: 175
        UnitIntervalModifier: 175
        InitialAttackDelay: 1500
        RequiresCondition: mediumbot

Player:
    Inherits@aidifficulties: ^AIDifficulties
    ModularBot@MediumAI:
        Name: bot-ai.medium
        Type: medium
    ...
    BaseBuilderBotModuleCA@generic:
        RequiresCondition: genericbot
        ConstructionYardTypes: fact.td_gdi, rafact.ra1_allies, ...
        RefineryTypes: proc.td_gdi, raproc.ra1_allies, ...
        PowerTypes: powr, apwr, ...
        BuildingFractions:
            powr: 20
            tent: 10
            weap: 20
            proc: 20
        BuildingLimits:
            weap: 2
    UnitBuilderBotModuleCA@generic:
        RequiresCondition: genericbot
        UnitQueues: Infantry, Vehicle, Aircraft, ...
        UnitsToBuild:
            e1: 80
            jeep: 10
    SquadManagerBotModuleCA@generic:
        RequiresCondition: genericbot
        SquadSize: 5
        ...
    HarvesterBotModuleCA:
        RequiresCondition: genericbot
        HarvestersPerRefinery: 3
    DeployBotModule:
        RequiresCondition: genericbot
    BotGlobalUnitBudget:
        GlobalUnitBudget: 600
        MaxUnitsPerBot: 300
        IgnoreHarvesters: true
```

The `Type` string is the key used by the lobby dropdown. The `Name` is a Fluent reference. `RequiresCondition: genericbot` (and the per-difficulty bot conditions) is what enables the modules for a given bot player. `BotLimits` entries are selected by difficulty via `GrantConditionOnBotOwner`, and the active `BotLimits` instance is read by the CA modules at runtime.

### Conditional traits

Bot modules are `ConditionalTrait<TInfo>` subclasses. They can be enabled or disabled by external conditions, which Cameo uses heavily to pick a difficulty-specific `BotLimits` and to turn entire modules on or off for a bot player. Most AI modules are enabled by `genericbot`, while `BotLimits` uses the per-difficulty conditions such as `mediumbot`.

![Algorithms diagram](images/Part_08_Chapter_01_IBot-algorithm-diagram-or-pseudocode-flowchart-for-the-non-trivia-5983ed.svg)


- **Depends on:** [Part 1.1 — ECS, Actors, and Traits](#file-chapters-Part_01_Chapter_01_ECS) (Actor/Trait system), [Part 1.3 — World, OrderManager, and Orders](#file-chapters-Part_01_Chapter_03_World_Orders) (World/Orders), [Part 2.4 — Rulesets, Actors, and Weapons](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_04_Rules_Weapons) (Rulesets and production queues), [Part 3.1 — Mod SDK and Project Structure](#file-chapters-Part_03_Chapter_01_Mod_SDK) (PlayerActor setup), [Part 9.1 — OrderManager and Lockstep Foundation](#file-chapters-Part_09_Chapter_01_OrderManager) (OrderManager and lockstep).
- **Used by:** [Part 8.2 — Bot Modules](#file-chapters-Part_08_Chapter_02_Bot_Modules) (Bot Modules), [Part 8.3 — Bot Squads and Combat Heuristics](#file-chapters-Part_08_Chapter_03_Squads) (Squads), [Part 8.4 — Bot Order Flow](#file-chapters-Part_08_Chapter_04_Order_Flow) (Order Flow), [Part 9.1 — OrderManager and Lockstep Foundation](#file-chapters-Part_09_Chapter_01_OrderManager) (network orders originate from bot `QueueOrder`).

## Algorithms

### Order throttling

`MinOrderQuotientPerTick` controls the maximum fraction of the queue issued per tick:

```csharp
var ordersToIssueThisTick = Math.Min((orders.Count + info.MinOrderQuotientPerTick - 1) / info.MinOrderQuotientPerTick, orders.Count);
```

With `MinOrderQuotientPerTick = 5`, at least one fifth of the pending queue is issued each tick. This smooths bot output and prevents a single tick from being flooded with orders.

### Module discovery

`ModularBot` discovers modules at activation time using `TraitsImplementing<T>()`. This means modules are plain traits; no central registry is needed. A mod can add new AI behavior by adding new trait modules. Cameo takes advantage of this: `ModularBot` does not know whether a module is `BaseBuilderBotModule` or `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`; it only requires the interface.

### Sync isolation
![Extension points diagram](images/Part_08_Chapter_01_IBot-extension-hook-diagram-showing-the-interface-s-to-implement-b4a27b.svg)


```csharp
Sync.RunUnsynced(Game.Settings.Debug.SyncCheckBotModuleCode, world, () =>
{
    foreach (var t in tickModules)
        ...
});
```

Bot code runs unsynced, so it can use random numbers, local state, and pathfinding without affecting the deterministic simulation. The only thing that crosses the sync boundary is the `Order` issued afterward. This is just as true for `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA` and `DeployBotModule` as for the upstream modules.

### Difficulty scaling via `BotLimits`

Several CA modules multiply base YAML delays by a `BotLimits` modifier (e.g., `UnitDelays[name] * unitDelayModifier / 100`). This means the same `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` YAML can produce a slower, smaller AI on easy difficulties and a faster, larger AI on hard difficulties without duplicating the module configuration. The limits are also read directly to cap `RefineryLimit` and `HarvesterLimit`.

### Global unit budget

`BotGlobalUnitBudget` computes `cap = GlobalUnitBudget / livingBots`, clamps it with `MaxUnitsPerBot` and `MinUnitsPerBot`, and then counts the bot's mobile `IPositionable` actors (excluding harvesters and any `IgnoredActorTypes`). When the count reaches the cap, `PauseUnitProduction` returns `true` and `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA` stops producing combat units for that tick. The recomputation is throttled to `RecalculationInterval` ticks.

## Common Pitfalls / Guardrails

- **No direct world mutation:** bot modules must not call `actor.QueueActivity`, set actor state, or mutate the world directly. All changes must flow through orders. `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA` follows this by resolving the `PlacePlugAI` order through `IResolveOrder` rather than directly mutating the building.
- **Replays:** bot logic is disabled during replays. If a bot mutates state without an order, the replay will desync.
- **Order latency:** bot modules should account for order latency. A module that checks "is this building being built?" must consider that the order it issued earlier has not yet executed.
- **Sync isolation:** bot code runs unsynced, so it must not call simulation-only APIs that assume sync context. Random choices should use `world.LocalRandom`, not `world.SharedRandom`.
- **Trait enabled checks:** `ModularBot` only invokes modules whose `IsTraitEnabled()` is true. If a module is conditional, it should handle being skipped gracefully. `BotGlobalUnitBudget` returns `false` from `PauseUnitProduction` when disabled.
- **Performance:** bot ticks are wrapped in `PerfSample("bot_tick")`. Expensive pathfinding or scanning should be rate-limited with tick counters, as seen in `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`, `HarvesterBotModuleCA`, and `SquadManagerBotModuleCA`.
- **Global budget interaction:** `BotGlobalUnitBudget` only pauses `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`; it does not stop base building or defense construction. If a bot seems to stop making units mid-game, check whether the global cap has been reached and whether the bot is still producing harvesters (which are excluded from the count).
- **Air superiority mismatch:** `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`'s `MaintainAirSuperiority` logic dynamically raises the air-to-air unit limit based on enemy `AirThreatUnits`. If the `AirThreatUnits` list is incomplete, the bot may under-produce or over-produce anti-aircraft units.
- **Missing `RequiresCondition`:** In `mods/cameo/ai/ai.yaml`, every module must have a `RequiresCondition` that matches the bot conditions set up by `GrantConditionOnBotOwner`. A module without a condition will run for every player, including humans, or never run, depending on the trait setup.

## Summary

This chapter explains how OpenRA's [bot](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) framework issues [orders](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) through the lockstep pipeline instead of mutating the [world](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) directly, and how Cameo reuses that pipeline with its own modules.

After reading this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain why bot logic is forbidden from mutating world state directly and must issue orders instead.
- Describe the responsibilities of `IBot`, `IBotInfo`, and `ModularBot`.
- List the common bot module callback interfaces (`IBotTick`, `IBotEnabled`, `IBotRespondToAttack`, etc.) and when each is invoked.
- Trace bot activation, the per-tick decision loop, and attack-response dispatch.
- Explain how `ModularBot` throttles orders and why `RunUnsynced` is used around bot code.
- Register a bot type and configure modules in a mod's AI YAML, including Cameo's difficulty-scaled `BotLimits`.
- Diagnose common bot issues such as stalled construction, unresponsive defense, order flooding, and units hitting a global budget cap.
- Explain how Cameo's `*CA` modules differ from the upstream modules they replace and how `BotGlobalUnitBudget` limits production.

If any of the concepts above feel unclear, review the relevant section before continuing. For source files and further reading, see the References section.

# Chapter 8.2 — Bot Modules (Cameo) {#file-chapters-Part_08_Chapter_02_Bot_Modules}

## Purpose

`[ModularBot](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)` is only a coordinator; the actual AI behavior in Cameo lives in specialized **[bot modules](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary)**. Most of these modules are Cameo-specific variants located in `OpenRA.Mods.CA` (and a few in `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo`), often subclassing or replacing upstream OpenRA modules with new heuristics tuned for the mod's huge multi-faction roster. Each module is a player-level trait that observes one slice of the world (base construction, unit production, harvesters, squads, support powers, garrisons, MCVs, plugs) and issues [orders](#file-appendices-Appendix_A_Glossary) through the bot's `QueueOrder`. This chapter surveys the major Cameo modules, their responsibilities, and the heuristics that guide them.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this chapter, you should be able to:

- Explain the modular bot architecture and how Cameo modules are discovered as player traits.
- Describe the responsibilities of the major Cameo bot modules (base builder, unit builder, harvester, squads, capture, MCV, repair, power-down, garrison, plugs, deploy, budgets).
- Understand how modules coordinate through shared callback interfaces and the `BotLimits` helper.
- Trace the data flow and heuristics in `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA` and `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`.
- Configure bot modules in `mods/cameo/ai/ai.yaml` and `mods/cameo/ai/ai_airforce.yaml` to tune AI behavior.
- Identify where to add a new bot module or state that integrates with Cameo's `ModularBot`.
