# Appendix H — Asset Visual Reference {#file-appendices-Appendix_H_Asset_Visual_Reference}


## Purpose

This appendix provides a categorical reference to every asset type that Cameo loads, renders, plays, or simulates, with descriptions and source-file pointers.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Identify the file format, YAML wiring, and loader class for each asset type.
- Understand how Cameo-specific assets such as R8 sprites and BAG audio differ from upstream assets.

This appendix is a categorical field guide to every asset type that Cameo loads, renders, plays, or simulates. For each category it shows the raw file format, the YAML file that wires the asset into the engine, the C# class or loader that owns it, a plain-text visual placeholder, and any special notes. Use it when you need to answer "what kind of asset is this and where is it defined?".

> **Visual note:** All previews in this appendix are placeholder descriptions or diagrams. No copyrighted game art is embedded.

## How to read the tables

Each table uses the same columns:

| Column | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Asset** | The name of the asset type in modding terms. |
| **File Format(s)** | The raw file extension(s) the engine reads. |
| **Definition YAML** | The YAML file(s) and manifest key that tell the engine how to use the asset. |
| **Engine Loader / Class** | The C# class, interface, or loader responsible for the asset. |
| **Visual Preview** | A description of what the asset looks like in-game. |
| **Notes** | Anything special: palette usage, tileset rules, spatial audio, etc. |

---

## Sprites / Sprite Sequences

Sprites are the 2D bitmaps that actors, projectiles, effects, and overlays draw on screen. A *sequence* is a named animation that maps frames from a sprite file to an actor state.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Unit / vehicle sprite | `.shp`, `.shp(TS)`, `.png` | `sequences/*.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `Sequences` | `DefaultSpriteSequence`, `ClassicSpriteSequence`, `ISpriteSequence` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SequenceSet.cs`), `SpriteCache` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteCache.cs`), `SheetBuilder` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SheetBuilder.cs`) | A rectangular sprite sheet; each cell is one frame of the unit viewed from a fixed angle. | `Facings` duplicates frames for 8 or 32 orientations. `DepthSprite` can give per-pixel depth. |
| Infantry sprite | `.shp`, `.png` | `sequences/infantry.yaml` | same as above | A strip of walking frames, repeated for 8 facing directions. | Uses `Tick` for gait timing and `Transpose` or `Facings` for orientation. `WithInfantryBody` selects the sequence. |
| Structure sprite | `.shp`, `.png` | `sequences/structures.yaml` | same as above | A large base frame plus optional build, idle, and damaged frames. | `Make:` is the construction animation; `WithIdleOverlay` adds independent overlays. |
| Projectile / effect sprite | `.shp`, `.png` | `sequences/misc.yaml`, `weapons.yaml` `Image` / `Palette` | same as above | A small 16×16 to 48×48 burst, bullet, or explosion frame. | Usually short `Length` and no facings; referenced by `Projectile` or `CreateEffect` warhead. |
| Raw sprite sheet | `.shp`, `.png`, `.tmp` | `mod.yaml` → `SpriteFormats` / `Loaders` → `Sprite` | `ISpriteLoader` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteLoader.cs`), `SpriteCache`, `SheetBuilder`, `Sprite` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/Sprite.cs`) | A large GPU texture packed with many individual frames. | `SpriteCache` packs frames into `Sheet` objects to reduce draw calls. |

---

## Terrain / Tilesets

Tilesets define the visual and gameplay properties of every cell on a map. A tileset YAML file contains the tile size, terrain types, and a library of templates that the map editor and renderer use.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Tile template | `.shp`, `.tmp`, `.png` | `tilesets/*.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `TileSets` | `ITerrainInfo` / `DefaultTerrainInfo` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Terrain/DefaultTerrain.cs`), `TerrainTemplateInfo` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Terrain/TerrainInfo.cs`), `TerrainRenderer` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/TerrainRenderer.cs`) | A square tile grid showing a single terrain template (e.g., a 2×2 cliff or road piece). | `PickAny` lets the engine pick a random variation; `Riser` defines height transitions between cells. |
| Terrain type | `.yaml` (inside tileset) | `tilesets/*.yaml` | `TerrainTypeInfo` (`OpenRA.Game/Map/TerrainInfo.cs`), `ITerrainInfo` | A colored cell representing a movement/terrain class. | Defines speed, minimap color, and restricted player color rules. |
| Rendered terrain layer | `.bin` (inside map) | `map.yaml`, `tilesets/*.yaml` | `TerrainRenderer`, `Map` (`OpenRA.Game/Map/Map.cs`) | A top-down isometric battlefield of connected tiles. | Each map cell stores a template index + frame; the renderer draws only the visible tiles. |

---

## Palettes

Palettes are 256-color lookup tables used by 8-bit indexed sprites. The engine can load a palette from disk, derive one from another palette, or extract one from a sprite file.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Palette from file | `.pal` | `rules/palettes.yaml` | `PaletteFromFile` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Palettes/PaletteFromFile.cs`), `IPalette` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/Palette.cs`) | A horizontal strip of 256 indexed colors numbered 0–255. | 8-bit sprites reference a named palette at render time; a `.pal` can be 6-bit Westwood or 8-bit. |
| Derived palette | `.yaml` only | `rules/palettes.yaml` | `PaletteFromPaletteWithAlpha` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Palettes/PaletteFromPaletteWithAlpha.cs`), `PaletteFromPlayerPalette*` (common palettes), `IPalette` | Same color strip but with a translucent or player-tint overlay. | Used for remap colors, shadows, and faction tints. |
| Embedded palette | inside `.shp` | `rules/palettes.yaml` | `PaletteFromEmbeddedSpritePalette` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Palettes/PaletteFromEmbeddedSpritePalette.cs`) | A tiny palette extracted from a sprite file. | Some SHP files carry their own palette; OpenRA can expose it via a palette trait. |

---

## Cursors

Cursors are small animated sprites that follow the mouse pointer. OpenRA prefers hardware cursors but falls back to software rendering when necessary.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Mouse cursor | `.shp`, `.png` | `cursors.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `Cursors` | `CursorManager` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/CursorManager.cs`), `IHardwareCursor` / `ISoftwareCursor` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/PlatformInterfaces.cs`) | A small pointer (e.g., 32×32) with an active hot spot. | Hardware cursors are preferred; software fallback is used when disabled. |
| Animated cursor | `.shp`, `.png` | `cursors.yaml` | `CursorManager` | A 4–8 frame animation loop (e.g., a loading spinner). | `Start` / `Length` selects frames from the source sprite; packed onto a cursor sheet. |

---

## Chrome / UI

Chrome is OpenRA's UI system. It combines skin images (chrome collections) with widget layout YAML and C# logic classes to build menus, HUDs, and in-game interfaces.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| UI panel / button skin | `.png` (1×, 2×, 3×) | `chrome.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `Chrome` | `ChromeProvider` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/ChromeProvider.cs`) | A 9-slice panel: corners, edges, and a stretchable center. | `PanelRegion` and `PanelSides` define the slices; `Collection` maps names to regions. |
| Widget layout | `.yaml` | `chrome/*.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `ChromeLayout` | `WidgetLoader`, `Widget` (`OpenRA.Game/Widgets/Widget.cs`), `ChromeLogic` | A tree diagram of nested UI containers, labels, and buttons. | The `Logic` key names the C# class that drives the widget. |
| UI icon | `.png` | `chrome.yaml` | `ChromeProvider` | A small 24×24 icon inside a named collection region. | Referenced by chrome widgets via `Image` / `ImageCollection`. |

---

## Audio / Sounds

Sound effects are short positional or global samples triggered by weapons, traits, and UI events. The engine tries each registered `ISoundLoader` until one parses the file.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Sound effect | `.aud`, `.wav`, `.ogg`, `.mp3` | `weapons.yaml` `Report`, trait `Sound:` fields, `mod.yaml` → `SoundFormats` | `ISoundLoader` (`OpenRA.Game/Sound/Sound.cs`), `Sound` (Game.Sound) | A short waveform or a single "pop" in a sound-field. | Spatial attenuation; random pitch via `Pitch` modifiers; can be positional. |
| Ambient sound | `.wav`, `.ogg` | `AmbientSound` trait in map / rules | `Sound`, `AmbientSound` trait | A looping waveform that fills an area. | Optional `Interval` and `RequiredCondition` control when it plays. |

---

## Voices

Voices are phrases spoken by units when selected, ordered, or killed. They are grouped into sets and referenced by the `Voiced` trait.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Voice set | `.aud`, `.wav`, `.ogg` | `voices.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `Voices` | `SoundInfo` (`OpenRA.Game/GameRules/Ruleset.cs`), `Sound` | A speaker icon with a unit silhouette and phrases like "Select", "Move", "Attack". | `Voiced` trait selects the set; the engine picks a phrase matching the action. |

---

## Notifications

Notifications are global speech events such as "Construction complete" or "Unit ready". They are not positional and are played per-player through the central sound system.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Game notification | `.aud`, `.wav`, `.ogg` | `notifications.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `Notifications` | `SoundInfo` (`OpenRA.Game/GameRules/Ruleset.cs`), `Sound` | A warning triangle with a speech bubble (e.g., "Construction complete"). | Played via `Game.Sound.PlayNotification`; global per-player, not positional. |

---

## Music

Music tracks are background songs played by the `MusicPlaylist` trait. The mod manifest lists the available tracks and the ruleset loads them as `MusicInfo` objects.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Music track | `.ogg`, `.mp3`, `.wav` | `music.yaml`, `mod.yaml` → `Music` | `MusicInfo` (`OpenRA.Game/GameRules/Ruleset.cs`), `MusicPlaylist` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/MusicPlaylist.cs`) | A musical note with a track title and progress bar. | `MusicPlaylist` selects tracks, honors `Hidden`, and pauses for in-game speech. |

---

## Maps

Maps are self-contained packages that include terrain, actor placement, rules overrides, and a preview image. They can be packaged as `.oramap` (a ZIP file) or as a directory.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Map package | `.oramap` (zip), directory | `map.yaml`, `map.bin`, `map.png` | `Map` (`OpenRA.Game/Map/Map.cs`), `MapPreview` (`OpenRA.Game/Map/MapPreview.cs`) | A minimap thumbnail with colored terrain and numbered spawn points. | `map.bin` is the binary tile layer; `map.yaml` holds rules, actors, and metadata. |
| Map preview image | `.png` | `map.png` | `MapPreview` | A 256×256 top-down overview of the map. | Auto-generated by the editor; used by the map browser. |

---

## Fonts

Fonts are TrueType files declared in `mod.yaml`. The engine rasterizes glyphs into a sprite sheet via `SpriteFont` so text can be drawn efficiently with the rest of the UI.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| UI font | `.ttf` | `mod.yaml` → `Fonts` | `SpriteFont` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/SpriteFont.cs`), `IFont` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/PlatformInterfaces.cs`) | The text "ABC" rendered as a crisp bitmap glyph strip. | Rasterized into a sprite sheet at load time; multiple named sizes can use the same `.ttf`. |

---

## Translations

Translations use Project Fluent `.ftl` files. The engine loads a mod-level bundle and an optional map-level bundle, then resolves strings by key at runtime.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fluent string | `.ftl` | `mod.yaml` → `Translations`, map `FluentMessageDefinitions` | `FluentProvider` (`OpenRA.Game/FluentProvider.cs`), `FluentBundle` | A label shown in two languages side by side. | Supports variables, pluralization, and map-level overrides. |

---

## Videos

Full-motion videos are loaded through the `IVideoLoader` interface. The Tiberian Dawn mod provides a Westwood VQA loader.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FMV / cutscene | `.vqa`, `.ogv` | `mod.yaml` → `Movies` | `IVideoLoader` (`OpenRA.Game/Graphics/VideoLoader.cs`), `VqaLoader` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/VideoLoaders/VqaLoader.cs`), `IVideo` | A filmstrip frame with a play button and subtitle area. | The sound engine plays the audio track; optional subtitle support. |

---

## Voxels (TS/RA2)

Voxels are 3D models used by Tiberian Sun and Red Alert 2 style mods. They are stored as a `.vxl` volume plus an `.hva` animation/position file.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Voxel model | `.vxl` + `.hva` | `mod.yaml` → `ModelSequences` | `VoxelLoader` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Graphics/VoxelLoader.cs`), `Voxel` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Graphics/Voxel.cs`), `IModel` | A blocky 3D object (e.g., a turret) viewed from a rotating angle. | `.hva` holds the limb transforms; TS/RA2-style mods use these for units and projectiles. |

---

## MIX / Package archives

OpenRA mounts archives and directories through a layered virtual file system. MIX files are the classic Westwood archive format; ZIP files and loose folders are also supported.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| MIX archive | `.mix` | `mod.yaml` → `PackageFormats` / `Packages` / `FileSystem` | `MixFile` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/FileSystem/MixFile.cs`), `IPackage` (`OpenRA.Game/FileSystem/IPackage.cs`), `FileSystem` | A closed box labeled `.mix` containing many small asset icons. | Westwood archive format; mounted by the VFS so files are addressed by name. |
| ZIP / loose package | `.zip`, folder | `mod.yaml` → `Packages` | `ZipFile` (`OpenRA.Game/FileSystem/ZipFile.cs`), `IPackage` | A folder or zip icon at the bottom of a layered stack. | The VFS layers packages in mount order; later mounts override earlier ones. |

---

## Cameo-specific assets

Cameo extends the upstream OpenRA asset pipeline with new sequence loaders, package formats, content-pack layering, faction-specific UI skinning, and custom widget asset references.

### Cameo sprite sequences

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Cameo sprite sequence | `.shp`, `.png`, `.r8`, `.r16` | `mod.yaml` → `SpriteSequenceFormat: CameoSpriteSequence` | `CameoSpriteSequenceLoader`, `CameoSpriteSequence` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Graphics/CameoSpriteSequence.cs`) | A sprite sequence whose source file can change per tileset. | Set `SpriteSequenceFormat` in `mod.yaml` to replace the default loader. Adds `Remap`, `UseShadow`, `ConvertShroudToFog`, and tileset filename overrides. |
| Tileset filename override | `.yaml` field | `sequences/*.yaml` | `CameoSpriteSequence.ParseFilenames` / `ParseCombineFilenames` | The same sequence resolving to a different source file when the active tileset changes. | `TilesetFilenames` maps `<tileset>: filename`; `TilesetFilenamesPattern` maps `<tileset>: filename pattern` with `Start`/`Count`. Used for tileset-specific sprites such as terrain objects or faction variants. |

### Cameo audio packages

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AudioBag / `.bag` archive | `.bag` + `.idx` | `mod.yaml` → `PackageFormats: AudioBag` | `AudioBagLoader` / `BagFile` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/FileSystem/BagFile.cs`) | A locked audio box with an `.idx` index card. | `.bag` holds raw audio data; a paired `.idx` file (`IdxReader`) lists offsets, lengths, sample rate, and flags. The loader synthesizes a WAV header (PCM or IMA ADPCM) so files are exposed as standard `.wav` streams. |
| Dune 2000 sound resources | `.rs` | `mod.yaml` → `PackageFormats: D2kSoundResources` | `D2kSoundResourcesLoader` / `D2kSoundResources` (`OpenRA.Mods.D2k/PackageLoaders/D2kSoundResources.cs`) | A flat archive of named sound samples. | Header lists ASCIIZ names with offset/length pairs; files are exposed as raw streams. |

### Content packs

Cameo organizes some external factions as content packs: a small manifest under `mods/cameo/ContentPacks/` that is mounted by the main `mod.yaml` and then referenced as an additional yaml/Fluent source.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Content pack manifest | `.yaml` | `mods/cameo/ContentPacks/<Game>/<Faction>/content.yaml` | `MiniYaml` / `FileSystem` mount, loaded via `mod.yaml` `ContentPacks` | A folder labeled `ContentPacks/<Game>/<Faction>` containing yaml/, sprites/, and translations/. | `content.yaml` declares a `Rules:` list and a `FluentMessages:` list, all referenced through the `ContentPacks\|` VFS prefix. The main `mod.yaml` mounts `cameo\|ContentPacks: ContentPacks` and then loads `ContentPacks\|<Game>/<Faction>/content.yaml` so the pack's rules and translations merge into the ruleset. |
| Content pack sprite | `.shp` | Inside the pack's `sprites/` directory | `SpriteCache` / `ISpriteLoader` | A unit or icon image bundled with the pack. | Packs are mounted as VFS folders, so their `sprites/` contents are addressable by the same sequence definitions as the main mod. |
| Content pack translation | `.ftl` | `content.yaml` → `FluentMessages` | `FluentProvider` | Strings for the pack's faction-specific names or descriptions. | Loaded through the same `FluentProvider` pipeline as mod-level translations. |

### Faction-specific assets

Cameo supports many source-game factions on a single shared sidebar. The chrome skin and some background collections can be switched per faction at runtime.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Faction suffix mapping | `metrics.yaml` → `FactionSuffix-<faction>` | `mods/cameo/metrics.yaml` | `AddFactionSuffixLogicCA` (`OpenRA.Mods.CA/Widgets/Logic/AddFactionSuffixLogicCA.cs`) | A faction name remapped to a chrome collection suffix such as `sidebar-allies` or `sidebar-ra2soviet`. | Each faction's internal name is looked up as `FactionSuffix-<internalName>`. The resolved suffix is appended to widget backgrounds, image collections, and tab/decoration names so the sidebar, command bar, and production tabs render the source-appropriate skin. |
| Faction definition | `.yaml` | `rules/world.yaml` or content pack `rules/faction.yaml` | `FactionCAInfo` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/Player/FactionCA.cs`) | A faction entry with a `Game` field describing which source game it belongs to. | `FactionCAInfo` extends `FactionInfo` with an extra `Game` string; used by lobby logic and content-pack matching. |
| Faction insignia | `.png` | `chrome.yaml` → `sidebar-<faction>` collection | `ChromeProvider`, `ImageWidget` with `Logic: AddFactionSuffixLogic` | A faction badge shown in the commander-tree window. | The commander-tree window's `FACTION_INSIGNIA` image uses `ImageCollection: sidebar` and `ImageName: insignia`; `CommanderTreeWindowLogic.HasFactionInsignia()` checks that the suffix-remapped collection actually defines an `insignia` region before showing the frame. |

### Custom UI widget asset references

Cameo adds several custom widgets whose visuals are defined partly in YAML and partly in dedicated sequence files.

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Custom formation marker sequences | `.shp` | `rules/player.yaml` → `CustomFormationsModOptions` | `CustomFormationsModOptions` / `CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Traits/Player/CustomFormationsModOptions.cs`, `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Orders/CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase.cs`) | Small tile and line markers drawn along a command-line move/attack order. | The player trait defines per-order-type palette and sequence pairs (e.g., `MoveOrderTileMarkerImage`, `MoveOrderTileMarkerSequence`, `AttackMoveOrderMarkerImage`, `AssaultMoveOrderMarkerSequence`). Defaults use `cftilemarkers.shp` / `mouse4.shp` sequences such as `MoveOrder`, `AttackMoveOrder`, `AssaultMoveOrder`, and `ForceFireOrder`. |
| Commander tree node icons | `.shp`, `.png` | `chrome/commander-tree-window.yaml` + `sequences/*.yaml` | `CommanderTreeWidget` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/CommanderTreeWidget.cs`) | Production-style icons arranged as a promotion tree. | `CommanderTreeWidget` draws production icons from the actor's `icon` sequence. Borders, group backgrounds, and ancestor highlight colors are widget properties; the window's header insignia is resolved via `AddFactionSuffixLogic`. |
| Promotion counter | `.yaml` only | `chrome/ingame-player.yaml` → `IngamePromotionCounter@PROMOTIONS` | `IngamePromotionCounterWidget` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/IngamePromotionCounterWidget.cs`) | Three text lines (rank, available points, progress) drawn over the sidebar. | No dedicated image; uses the `Bold` font and player/white color. Text keys are `promotion-counter.rank`, `promotion-counter.points`, and `promotion-counter.progress`. |
| Quota production palette | `.shp`, `.png` | `chrome/ingame-player.yaml` → `QuotaProductionPalette@PRODUCTION_PALETTE` | `QuotaProductionPaletteWidget` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/Widgets/QuotaProductionPaletteWidget.cs`) | A production palette that shows an `alive/quota` counter in cyan on each icon. | Inherits from `ProductionPaletteCAWidget`; the icon images are normal production sequences. The overlay is rendered with the `OverlayFont` from the base widget. |

### Cameo-specific loaders and formats

| Asset | File Format(s) | Definition YAML | Engine Loader / Class | Visual Preview | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R8 / R16 sprite | `.r8`, `.r16` | `mod.yaml` → `SpriteFormats: R8` | `R8Loader` (`OpenRA.Mods.D2k/SpriteLoaders/R8Loader.cs`) | An indexed 8-bit or 16-bit Dune 2000 sprite frame. | Cameo lists `R8` in `SpriteFormats`. `CameoSpriteSequence` knows how to handle `R8Loader.RemappableFrame` when the `Remap` field is set. |
| Loading screen images | `.png` | `mod.yaml` → `LoadScreen: FitImageLoadScreen` | `FitImageLoadScreen` (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/LoadScreens/FitImageLoadScreen.cs`) | A full-screen splash image that fades in, then randomized loading screens. | `SplashImage` is shown once at cold start; `Image` is a comma-separated list of screens the loader picks randomly between sessions. The screen fits the image to the window and displays a Fluent message. |
| Asset browser extensions | various | `mod.yaml` → `AssetBrowser` | `AssetBrowserLogic` | Filtered lists of `.shp`, `.tem`, `.des`, `.sno`, `.jun`, `.png`, `.r8`, `.r16`, `.car`, `.bar` for sprites and `.aud`, `.wav`, `.mp3` for audio. | Cameo extends the browser sprite extensions to include Dune 2000 and custom formats. |

---

## Summary

This appendix catalogued Cameo's asset types: the upstream sprites, terrain, palettes, cursors, chrome, audio, voices, notifications, music, maps, fonts, translations, videos, voxels, and MIX archives, plus Cameo-specific additions such as the `CameoSpriteSequence` loader, `AudioBag` / `.bag`+`.idx` archives, `D2kSoundResources` `.rs` packages, `ContentPacks` layering, faction-suffix UI skinning, and custom widget references for formations, commander tree, promotion counters, and quota production. Each entry showed the raw file format, the YAML definition, the engine loader or class, and any special rendering or playback notes. It is intended as a quick reference while reading the rest of the manual or while working in a mod's asset tree.

# Appendix I — Actor Reference (Cameo) {#file-appendices-Appendix_I_Actor_Reference}


## Purpose

This appendix lists the actors defined or customized by Cameo, summarizing their roles, traits, and where they are defined.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Look up a Cameo actor by name or faction.
- Understand the key traits and inheritance chain of each actor.

This appendix catalogs the **Cameo-specific actors** that modders are most likely to encounter when reading or editing the `mods/cameo/` ruleset. It is not an exhaustive inventory of every imported unit from every franchise represented in Cameo; instead, it focuses on:

* The abstract templates and world/player definitions that underpin the whole mod.
* The `Camea` boss faction, an original Cameo faction that combines GDI, Nod, Allied, and Soviet technology.
* Shared utility, resource, and tech actors that are unique to the Cameo rules layer.

All values are read from the `Cameo-mod` source tree (2026-07-24). Where an actor inherits from another definition, the source file noted is the one that contains the concrete actor key; parent templates are listed in the **Primary traits** column.

> **Generated reference, not balance commentary.** This appendix is hand-maintained for readability, so always verify the current YAML before relying on a value for implementation work.

## How to read these tables

Each table lists a representative set of actors in a category. Columns:

* **Actor key** — the internal name used in `rules/*.yaml`, map actor definitions, and Lua (`Actor.Create("mcv.camea", ...)`).
* **Primary traits** — the most important inherited templates and direct traits that define the actor's behavior. Abstract keys (`^...`) are templates; concrete keys are buildable/spawnable actors.
* **Source file** — the relative path under `mods/cameo/rules/` where the actor key is defined.
* **Description** — what the actor does in the game and any notable Cameo-specific quirks.

## Cameo actor reference

### Abstract / template actors

These `^` keys live in `defaults.yaml` and are inherited by almost every concrete actor in the mod. They are not spawned directly.

| Actor key | Primary traits | Source file | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `^ExistsInWorld` | `AppearsOnRadar`, `UpdatesPlayerStatistics`, `CombatDebugOverlay`, `GivesExperience`, `GivesExperienceToMasterOrTransport`, `ScriptTriggers`, `RenderDebugState` | `defaults.yaml` | Base presence template: makes an actor count for radar, statistics, experience, and script triggers. |
| `^SpriteActor` | `BodyOrientation`, `QuantizeFacingsFromSequence`, `RenderSprites` | `defaults.yaml` | Minimum template for any sprite-based actor. |

## Scope and caveats

* This appendix covers the **Camea** boss faction and the Cameo-wide templates/utility actors. It does not enumerate the dozens of imported factions (Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn, Tiberian Sun, Red Alert 2, Dune 2000, Generals, StarCraft, Warcraft, etc.) that also appear in `mods/cameo/rules/`.
* **Naval units:** The `Camea` faction has no dedicated naval buildable units. Naval production is gated globally by the `Naval` lobby prerequisite (`globalnaval`) in `player.yaml` and the naval units are defined in `ships.yaml` for other factions.
* **Art references:** All concrete actors use existing art from their parent definitions (e.g., `Image: fact`, `Image: MCV`). No image previews are included in this reference.
* **Verified source:** All entries were checked against the `Cameo-mod` rules YAML (2026-07-24). If you are working against a newer Cameo tree, re-verify keys and prerequisites before using them in maps or scripts.

# Appendix J — Terrain Tile Reference {#file-appendices-Appendix_J_Terrain_Tiles}


## Purpose

This appendix catalogs the terrain tiles and templates used by Cameo, organized by tileset.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Identify the tile index and terrain type for common tiles.
- Understand how tilesets are wired into the random map generator and editor.

This appendix catalogs every terrain template in every official OpenRA mod tileset.
Each row shows a rendered preview, the template ID, the source image file(s), the grid size,
the primary terrain type, and notes about the template.

## Cameo terrain tiles

The Cameo mod reuses and extends many of the tilesets listed above. Tilesets are declared in the
`mods/cameo/tilesets/` directory and registered in the `TileSets:` block of `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`.

### Tilesets shipped with Cameo

### Tileset YAML structure

Each `mods/cameo/tilesets/<name>.yaml` file contains three top-level sections:

1. **`General`** — tileset metadata such as `Name`, `Id`, `TileSize`, `SheetSize`, and `EditorTemplateOrder`.
2. **`Terrain`** — one `TerrainType@<id>` entry for every logical terrain type. Each entry declares the
   `Type` name used in templates and locomotors, `TargetTypes`, `Color`, and optional `AcceptsSmudgeType`.
3. **`Templates`** — one `Template@<id>` entry for every placeable tile. Each template declares `Id`,
   `Images`, `Size`, `Categories`, and a `Tiles` map that assigns a terrain type to every cell in the template.

### CameoSpriteSequence tileset filename overrides

`mods/cameo/mod.yaml` sets `SpriteSequenceFormat: CameoSpriteSequence`. The `CameoSpriteSequence` class
adds two tileset-specific sequence fields:

- `TilesetFilenames` — a dictionary of `<tileset name>: filename` that overrides the normal `Filename` for
  that tileset.
- `TilesetFilenamesPattern` — a dictionary of `<tileset name>: filename pattern` that overrides the normal
  `FilenamePattern` for that tileset.

These overrides are resolved when the sequence system loads actor/animation sprites. **They do not apply to
terrain template rendering**, which is driven by the tileset YAML's `Images` entries and the engine's
`DefaultTerrain` loader. If you add a new tileset-specific variant, it affects units, structures, and effects
that reference the sequence, not the terrain tiles themselves.

### `^BaseWorld` and terrain logic

`mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` begins with `^BaseWorld`, the base world actor definition. It includes the
`TerrainRenderer` and `TerrainLighting` traits that actually draw the tileset, plus the global `Locomotor`
entries that define movement costs for every terrain type. Because Cameo merges many different games, the
locomotors list a large set of terrain types, including game-specific variants such as:

- `ClearTemperat`, `ClearWinter`, `ClearJungle`, `ClearSnow`, `ClearDesert`, `ClearInterior`
- `Dune`, `RoughDune`, `Spice`, `SpiceSand`, `Sand`, `Transition`
- `Tiberium`, `BlueTiberium`, `RedTiberium`, `GoldTiberium`, `Veins`
- `Ore`, `Gems`, `RA2Copper`, `RA2Silver`, `RA2Ore`, `RA2Gems`, `SCMinerals`
- `Ford`, `Beach`, `Road`, `Rails`, `Bridge`, `Tunnel`, `Water`, `Concrete`, `ZergSoil`

If a new `TerrainType` is added to a tileset but not added to every relevant `Locomotor@` in `^BaseWorld`,
actors that use that locomotor will receive a default speed (often zero) on the new terrain.

### `TintedCellsLayer` interaction

`^BaseWorld` also defines several `TintedCellsLayer` traits:

- `TintedCellsLayer@ra2rad` — Red Alert 2 radiation
- `TintedCellsLayer@tibrad` — Tiberium radiation
- `TintedCellsLayer@generalsrad` — Generals-style radiation
- `TintedCellsLayer@anthraxgreen`, `@anthraxblue`, `@anthraxpurple` — chemical contamination
- `TintedCellsLayer@cryo` — cryo effect

These render a colored overlay on top of the terrain and can damage actors via `DamagedByTintedCells`. They are
not part of any tileset; they are world-layer effects that are applied at run time. When designing new terrain,
keep in mind that a `TintedCellsLayer` overlay may make the underlying tile colors look different on the
battlefield than in the editor.

### How to add a new terrain tile

1. **Choose the tileset** — open the appropriate `mods/cameo/tilesets/<tileset>.yaml` file.
2. **Add the terrain type** — if the tile introduces a new logical terrain, add a `TerrainType@<id>` entry
   under the `Terrain:` section.
3. **Update `^BaseWorld` locomotors** — add the new type to the `TerrainSpeeds` of every `Locomotor@` in
   `mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` that should be able to move on it.
4. **Add the source artwork** — place the image file (`.shp`, `.tem`, `.des`, `.png`, etc.) in the correct
   package so the tileset loader can resolve it.
5. **Create a template** — add a `Template@<id>` entry with a unique `Id`, `Images`, `Size`, `Categories`, and
   a `Tiles` map that assigns a terrain type to each cell.
6. **Register the tileset** — if you created a brand-new tileset, add it to the `TileSets:` block in
   `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`.
7. **Test in the map editor** — set the map's `Tileset` to the correct tileset ID and confirm the tile
   appears in the palette and renders correctly.

### How to modify an existing tileset

- Change the `Terrain` definitions to rename, recolor, or change the target/smudge behavior of a terrain type.
- Edit the `Tiles` sub-node of a `Template` to change the terrain type of individual cells.
- Change `Images` to point to a new source file, or adjust `Size` if the template dimensions change.
- Update `EditorTemplateOrder` if you add new categories.
- Verify that the `TileSize` in `General` still matches the artwork grid.

### Common pitfalls

- **Duplicate template IDs** — every `Template@<id>` node must have a unique `Id` value within the tileset.
  Duplicate IDs silently override each other.
- **Missing locomotor entry** — new terrain types must be added to the `Locomotor` definitions in `^BaseWorld`.
  Otherwise units may be unable to move.
- **Wrong image extension or path** — tileset `Images` must resolve to a file that exists in the mod package.
  The asset browser extensions are declared in `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`.
- **Tile/grid size mismatch** — the `Size` of a template must match the number of cells in the `Tiles` map, and
  the artwork must match the `TileSize` declared in `General`.
- **Forgetting to enable a tileset** — a tileset file is only available if it is listed in the `TileSets:` block
  of `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`.
- **Expecting `CameoSpriteSequence` overrides to change terrain** — `TilesetFilenames` and
  `TilesetFilenamesPattern` are sequence-level features for actors, not for terrain templates.
- **`TintedCellsLayer` overlays** — layers such as radiation or tiberium tint cells at run time. If a tile looks
  fine in the editor but wrong in-game, check whether an overlay layer is active.
- **Modifying tiles after maps are created** — changing a tile's `Size` or `Tiles` map can break existing
  maps that reference the same template ID.

# Appendix K — Environmental Actor Reference {#file-appendices-Appendix_K_Environmental_Actors}


## Purpose

This appendix catalogs the environmental actors (trees, rocks, civilian buildings, resource spawns, etc.) used by Cameo and the upstream bundled mods.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Look up environmental actors by category and tileset.
- Understand which actors can be placed by the random map generator and which are editor-only.

This appendix catalogs the **environmental actors** in the four official OpenRA mods: *Red Alert (RA)*, *Tiberian Dawn (C&C)*, *Dune 2000 (D2K)*, and *Tiberian Sun (TS)*. Environmental actors are map-placed objects that are not produced by a player's factory or construction yard in the normal tech tree—things like trees, rocks, civilian buildings, bridges, walls, gates, crates, resource spawns, and decorative props. Some of them (sandbags, concrete walls, gates) can also be built by players once the right prerequisites are met, but they still behave as world objects rather than as units.

They differ from buildable combat actors in a few key ways:

* Most inherit from templates such as `^Tree`, `^Rock`, `^CivBuilding`, `^Bridge`, `^Wall`, or `^Crate` rather than from `^Building` or `^Vehicle`.
* They are usually owned by `Neutral` (or `Creeps` for hostile wildlife) and placed in the map editor.
* They typically use `Building` for footprint, `Interactable` for selection bounds, `Tooltip` for display names, and `MapEditorData` for editor categorization.
* Many are invulnerable or have very high health, and some have special death behavior such as `SpawnActorOnDeath`, `FireWarheadsOnDeath`, `SeedsResource`, or `CashTrickler`.

The tables use the YAML data as it appears in the rules files. "Name/Tooltip" shows the in-game display name resolved from the mod's Fluent translation files. "Size" combines the `Dimensions` and `Footprint` values from the `Building` trait. "Key Traits" highlights the most important behavior traits. A "—" means the field is not explicitly set on that actor or its inherited template.

> **Generated, not hand-written.** This appendix is produced by `build files/generate_environmental_actor_reference.py`, which parses each mod's `rules/*.yaml` (resolving `Inherits:` chains) and `fluent/rules.ftl` (for display names). The preview column shows labelled placeholders by default; run `build files/extract_environmental_images.py` after installing the game content to render real sprites with the OpenRA Utility's `--export-sequence-frame` command.

> **A note on art.** OpenRA's own assets are openly licensed; the classic Westwood/EA unit art is distributed as freeware and remains its owners' property. Showing previews in a free, non-commercial, educational reference is a fair-use use, not an open-license grant. Attribute the art to its owners and include a "not endorsed by or affiliated with EA" notice when publishing.

> Cross-references: [Part 1.1 — ECS](#file-chapters-Part_01_Chapter_01_ECS), [Part 2.4 — Rulesets, Actors, and Weapons](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_04_Rules_Weapons), [Part 7.7 — RMG Resources and Actors](#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_07_Resources_Actors), [Part 10.1 — Official Mods](#file-chapters-Part_10_Chapter_01_Official_Mods), [Appendix J — Terrain Tile Reference](#file-appendices-Appendix_J_Terrain_Tiles)

## Cameo environmental actors

Cameo reuses the core four Westwood mods and adds dozens of franchises, so its environmental actors are spread across many rule files under `mods/cameo/rules/`. The most important ones are the neutral templates in `defaults.yaml`, the vegetation in `trees.yaml`, the civilian/tech buildings in `civilian.yaml`, `civilian-desert.yaml` and `tech.yaml`, the resource spawners in `misc.yaml`, and the wildlife/critters in `monsters.yaml`.

They follow the same OpenRA conventions as the baseline mods: they usually inherit from a template such as `^Tree`, `^Rock`, `^CivBuilding`, `^TechBuilding`, `^Crate` or `^TibTree`, use `Building` for their footprint, `Tooltip` for their display name, `MapEditorData` for editor placement, and are owned by `Neutral` (or `Creeps` for hostile creatures). Cameo-specific mechanics are described below, followed by a table of notable actors.

### Environmental/neutral actor templates

| Template | Purpose | Defined in | Key inherited traits |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `^Tree` | Vegetation (trees, ice floes, utility poles) | `defaults.yaml` | `SpawnActorOnDeath` (to a husk or fire), `MapEditorData`, tileset filters |
| `^TreeHusk` | Burnt/destroyed tree props | `defaults.yaml` | Visual-only replacement, no selection |
| `^Rock` | Rocks and cliff props | `defaults.yaml` | Static footprint, passable decoration |

| `^CivBuilding` | Civilian houses, churches, etc. | `defaults.yaml` | `FireWarheadsOnDeath`, `Demolishable`, `SpawnActorOnDeath` to a husk |
| `^CivBuildingHusk` | Repairable ruins of civ buildings | `defaults.yaml` | `TransformOnCapture` back into the original building |
| `^TechBuilding` | Capturable neutral tech structures | `defaults.yaml` | `Capturable`, `InstantlyRepairable`, `GpsDot`, `ProvidesPrerequisite` |

| `^Crate` | Pickups and bonuses | `defaults.yaml` | `Crate` trait, random actions, editor-only render |
| `^Mine` | Explosive mines | `defaults.yaml` | Buried weapon trigger |

### Cameo-specific environmental mechanics

`mods/cameo/rules/world.yaml` registers several world traits that add environmental overlays and resources:

* `TintedCellsLayer` — cell-based colored overlays. Each layer has a unique `Name` and is created by `CreateTintedCells` warheads or `ConeTintLayer` logic:
  * `ra2rad` → `Name: ra2radiation` (RA2 nuclear radiation, green tint)
  * `tibrad` → `Name: tibradiation` (color `00B300`, Tiberium/radiation)
  * `generalsrad` → `Name: genradiation` (color `FF7C00`, Generals-style radiation)
  * `anthraxgreen` → `Name: anthraxgreen` (color `8FFF00`)
  * `anthraxblue` → `Name: anthraxblue` (color `0068FF`)
  * `anthraxpurple` → `Name: anthraxpurple` (color `7400FF`)
  * `cryo` → `Name: cryo` (color `88BBFF`, fast fade-out)

  Warheads reference these by `LayerName:` (e.g., `CreateTintedCells` with `LayerName: ra2radiation`). The `cryo` layer is also used by cone weapons (`ConeTintLayer: cryo`).

* `WeaponTriggerCells@Inferno` — a fire field layer that can trigger repeated weapons on cells.

* `ResourceLayer` / `ResourceRenderer` — Cameo supports many resource types in parallel: `Tiberium`, `BlueTiberium`, `RedTiberium`, `GoldTiberium`, `Ore`, `Gems`, `RA2Ore`, `RA2Gems`, `RA2Silver`, `RA2Copper`, `SCMinerals`, `SCGas`, `SCGas2`, `SCGas3`, `OP2Ore`, `OP2Ore2`, `Spice`, `Veins`, etc.

* `D2kResourceRenderer` and `ResourceSparkleEffect` add Dune 2000 spice bloom and resource sparkle effects.

* `CashTrickler` and `UpdatesDerrickCount` are used by oil derricks to provide passive income and enforce the `derricklimit` cap.

### How to add or modify an environmental actor in Cameo

1. Choose the closest template in `defaults.yaml` (`^Tree`, `^Rock`, `^CivBuilding`, `^TechBuilding`, `^Crate`, `^TibTree`, etc.).
2. Create a new actor entry in an appropriate `mods/cameo/rules/*.yaml` file (e.g., `trees.yaml`, `civilian.yaml`, `tech.yaml`, `misc.yaml`).
3. Add the required traits:
   * `Building` with `Footprint` and `Dimensions` for footprint and pathability.
   * `Tooltip` for the in-game name.
   * `MapEditorData` with a `Categories` value so the actor appears in the editor.
   * `RenderSprites` / `WithSpriteBody` for the art.
   * For capturable tech buildings, inherit `^TechBuilding` and set `CaptureManager`, `Capturable`, and `InstantlyRepairable`.
   * For resource spawners, inherit `^TibTree` and add `SeedsResource` with `ResourceType`, `Interval`, and `MaxRange`.
   * For environmental overlays, add a `CreateTintedCells` warhead to a weapon and reference the `TintedCellsLayer` `Name` with `LayerName:`.
4. Make sure the file is included in the mod's `Rules` section of `mods/cameo/mod.yaml`.
5. Add a `SpawnActorOnDeath` target if the actor is meant to leave a husk or wreck.
6. Use `MapEditorData` `RequireTilesets` / `ExcludeTilesets` to restrict the actor to the correct tilesets.

### Common pitfalls

* `MapEditorData` without a valid `Categories` entry makes the actor invisible in the map editor.
* `TintedCellsLayer` `Name` values must match exactly the `LayerName` used by warheads; mismatches silently produce no overlay.
* Oil derricks need both `CashTrickler` and `UpdatesDerrickCount` to respect the `derricklimit` actor.
* A missing `Building` trait or footprint means the actor cannot be placed or selected properly.
* `SpawnActorOnDeath` references must point to actors that actually exist, or the game will crash when the actor dies.
* `^Crate` and `^TechBuilding` have many inherited traits; check whether you need to remove traits (`-TraitName:`) rather than just add them.
* Tileset restrictions in `MapEditorData` can hide an actor from a map author; verify `RequireTilesets` and `ExcludeTilesets` against the tileset list in `world.yaml`.

> Cross-reference: [Appendix L — Cameo Divergence](#file-appendices-Appendix_L_Cameo_Divergence)

It pairs each object's internal codename with its editor category, footprint, key traits, and a preview slot, all drawn from the engine's own rules so the reference stays in sync with the pinned source.

# Appendix L — Cameo Divergence {#file-appendices-Appendix_L_Cameo_Divergence}


## Purpose

This appendix summarizes the ways the Cameo mod diverges from upstream OpenRA, serving as the canonical divergence reference for this manual.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Identify the major custom C# assemblies and data layers in Cameo.
- Understand where Cameo overrides upstream behavior and where it reuses it unchanged.

This appendix summarizes the ways the Cameo mod diverges from upstream OpenRA. For per-file and per-trait details, consult the Cameo source tree directly.

> **Scope:** This summary reflects the `Cameo-mod` source tree as of 2026-07-24. The manual is pinned to that source; newer Cameo or OpenRA versions may differ.

## 1. Engine baseline

Cameo is a third-party OpenRA total-conversion mod. It does not modify the OpenRA engine directly; instead, it layers two custom C# assemblies and a large `mods/cameo/` data directory on top of the engine:

- `OpenRA.Mods.Cameo` — 190+ class declarations covering custom traits, activities, effects, bot modules, order generators, sprite-sequence loading, file-system loaders, and UI/rendering helpers.
- `OpenRA.Mods.CA` — 370+ class declarations covering additional traits, projectiles, warheads, activities, bot modules, squad AI state machines, and Lua globals.
- `mods/cameo/` — custom rules, weapons, sequences, audio, chrome, tilesets, translations, maps, AI definitions, and a `ContentPacks/` layer for per-game asset packs.

The engine version pinned by the Cameo SDK is `ENGINE_VERSION="2949af8"`, sourced from a Cameo-maintained OpenRA fork (`https://github.com/cameo-mod/OpenRA`). The mod is therefore intentionally anchored to a specific OpenRA commit rather than tracking `bleed` continuously.

## 2. Custom C# code

### 2.1 OpenRA.Mods.Cameo

Major additions and overrides in this assembly include:

| Area | Notable classes / traits | What they do |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Factions / player** | `FactionCA`, `PlayerPromotions`, `PromotionUpgrade`, `PromotionPalette`, `PlayerDisplayUpgrade` | Custom faction handling, player-level promotion/upgrade systems, and palette effects tied to progression. |
| **Infection / mind control** | `AttackInfectCA`, `InfectCA`, `InfectableCA`, `InfectorOld`, `MindControlWarhead` | Unit infection mechanics and mind-control warheads not present in upstream OpenRA. |
| **Deployment** | `DeployOnCondition`, `HeliGrantConditionOnDeploy`, `HeliDeployForGrantedCondition`, `AutoDeployer` | Extended deployment logic for ground and helicopter actors. |
| **Resources / economy** | `CashBack`, `CashTransferToAllies`, `GrantConditionOnPlayerTotalCash`, `BotGlobalUnitBudget`, `BotInsurance` | Custom cash-sharing, refund, and AI economy guardrails. |
| **Spawning / production** | `DroneSpawnerMasterCA`, `LarvaProductionQueue`, `LarvaConsumingProduction`, `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA`, `FreeActorWithCondition` | Custom spawn, plug, and alternate production mechanics. |
| **Combat / damage** | `ExplodesCA` (`FireWarheadsOnDeathCA`), `AnnounceOnDamageState`, `Integrity` | Extended death/damage-state behavior. |
| **Bot modules** | `DeployBotModule`, `PlugSpawnerBotModuleCA` | AI modules that drive the custom deployment and plug mechanics. |
| **Orders / UI** | `CustomFormationsUnitOrderGenerator`, `CustomFormationsAttackMoveOrderGenerator`, `CustomFormationsOrderGeneratorBase`, `CustomFormationsModOptions` | Custom formation and attack-move order generators with mod-option integration. |
| **Rendering / palettes** | `ColorPickerColorShift`, `PlayerColorShift`, `OverlayPlayerColorPalette`, `RenderRangeCircleCA`, `WithPhysicalStateColoredOverlay`, `TAStealthTankCloakPaletteEffect` | Custom palette shifting, color overlays, and range-circle rendering. |
| **Sprite sequences** | `CameoSpriteSequence`, `CameoSpriteSequenceLoader` | Tileset-specific sprite-sequence variants. |
| **File system** | `BagFile`, `AudioBagLoader` | Loader for BAG audio archives used by some legacy assets. |
| **Effects** | `DeterministicSmokeParticle`, `TintedSpriteEffect`, `DeterministicOffsetSmokeParticleEmitter`, `DeterministicCellOffset` | Deterministic particle effects with cell-level offsets. |
| **Load screens** | `FitImageLoadScreen` | Custom load-screen image fitting. |
| **Renderables** | `UILineAnnotationRenderable`, `UIRectangleAnnotationRenderable`, `TurretSearchlightRenderable` | Custom UI-line and search-light annotations. |

### 2.2 OpenRA.Mods.CA

Major additions and overrides in this assembly include:

| Area | Notable classes / traits | What they do |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Aircraft / missiles** | `AttackAircraftCA`, `DiveOnAttack`, `Dive`, `BallisticMissileCA`, `BallisticMissileCAFly`, `CruiseMissile`, `CruiseMissileFly`, `GuidedMissile`, `GuidedMissileFly`, `AirstrikeMasterCA`, `AirstrikeSlaveCA`, `AttachedAircraft` | Custom aircraft attack logic, dive behavior, ballistic/cruise/guided missile flight, and airstrike master/slave handling. |
| **Attach system** | `Attachable`, `AttachableTo`, `AttachOnCreation`, `AttachOnTransform` | Mechanic for attaching one actor to another (e.g., carried aircraft or turrets). |
| **Attack variants** | `AttackBomberCA`, `AttackFrontalCharged`, `AttackTurretedCharged`, `AttackPrismSupported` | Charged and prism-supported attack variants. |
| **Projectiles** | `LaserZapCA`, `LinearPulse`, `PlasmaBeam`, `SpriteAthenaLaser`, `WarheadTrailProjectileCA`, `NukeLaunchInfo` | Custom beam, pulse, and trail projectiles. |
| **Warheads** | `CreateTintedCells`, `TintedCell`, `SpawnActorWarheadCA`, `FireProjectilesWarhead`, `MindControlWarhead`, `DetachAttachmentWarhead` | Custom warheads that create tinted cells, spawn actors, fire sub-projectiles, mind-control, or detach attachments. |
| **Teleport / chronoshift** | `TeleportCA`, `ChronoshiftableCA` | Custom teleport and chronoshift handling. |
| **Instant transform** | `InstantTransform` | One-shot actor transformation. |
| **Conditions** | `GrantConditionOnAttackCA`, `GrantConditionOnBotOwnerCA`, `GrantConditionOnPrerequisiteCA`, `GrantConditionOnDamage`, `GrantConditionOnFogEnabled`, `GrantConditionOnHealingReceived`, `GrantChargingCondition`, `GrantDelayedCondition`, `GrantStackingCondition`, `GrantThermalCondition`, `GrantTimedConditionOnCargoAction`, `GrantTimedConditionOnCrushWarning`, `UnloadOnCondition` | A large set of condition-granting triggers and CA variants of upstream conditions. |
| **Support powers** | `CashHackable`, `SupportPowerChargeManager`, `GrantConditionOnSupportPower` | Custom support-power scaffolding and cash-hack tagging. |
| **Bot modules** | `BaseBuilderBotModuleCA`, `SquadManagerBotModuleCA`, `MCVManagerBotModuleCA`, `CaptureManagerBotModuleCA`, `HarvesterBotModuleCA`, `BuildingRepairBotModuleCA`, `PowerDownBotModuleCA`, `LoadGarrisonerBotModuleCA`, `UnitBuilderBotModuleCA`, `UnitCompositionsBotModule`, `BotLimits` | Full CA-specific AI suite, plus squad state machines (`SquadCA`, `StateMachineCA`, `StateBaseCA`, air/ground/navy/protection states). |
| **Lua globals** | `MadTankCAGlobal`, `ReinforcementsCAGlobal` | Cameo-specific Lua mission helpers. |
| **Effects / graphics** | `WarheadTrailProjectileEffectCA`, `TintedCell`, `MindControlArc` | Custom trail and mind-control arc effects. |
| **Harvester / economy** | `HarvesterBalancerCA`, `HarvesterBotModuleCA` | Custom harvester balance and AI harvesting. |
| **Selection / rendering** | `CustomRadarColor`, `GuardsSelection`, `DoesNotBlock`, `GivesExperienceToMaster` | Radar color overrides, selection guarding, pass-through actors, and experience routing. |

## 3. Custom YAML / rules / content packs

The `mods/cameo/` directory is the primary divergence layer. As of the 2026-07-24 source snapshot it contains:

| Directory | Contents |
| :---- | :---- |
| `rules/` | 64 YAML files defining actors, buildings, factions, upgrades, and conditions. |
| `weapons/` | 51 YAML files defining weapons, projectiles, and warheads. |
| `sequences/` | 59 YAML files defining sprite sequences, cameos, and animations. |
| `audio/` | 32 YAML files defining voices, notifications, music playlists, and per-game audio packs. |
| `bits/` | 28,116 asset files in 58 sub-directories (per-game sprite, voxel, audio, and icon collections). |
| `tilesets/` | 20 tileset definition files. |
| `chrome/` | 16 UI/chrome layout files. |
| `ai/` | 1 AI definition file. |
| `maps/` | 359 maps. |
| `ContentPacks/` | Per-theme and per-faction content packs organized as `<Theme>/<Faction>/`, each with a `content.yaml` manifest and a `yaml/` subdirectory for rules, weapons, sequences, and translations. Current themes include Core, Shared, TiberianDawn, RedAlert, TiberianSun, RedAlert2, RedAlert2Mod, TKM, D2k, StarCraft, Warcraft2, and Outpost2. |

Cameo uses the same MiniYaml syntax and inheritance rules as upstream OpenRA, but the actor and weapon definitions are entirely mod-specific. The `ContentPacks/` directory is a notable structural addition: it lets the mod layer per-game or per-faction content packs on top of the base `mods/cameo/` rules.

## 4. Custom assets

Cameo bundles a large set of third-party and original assets:

- **Sprites / cameos:** `mods/cameo/bits/` and `mods/cameo/ContentPacks/*/sprites/` hold per-game unit, building, and cameo graphics.
- **Audio:** `mods/cameo/audio/` defines voices, notifications, and music playlists sourced from many different games. The `BagFile` loader supports legacy BAG archives.
- **Chrome / UI:** `mods/cameo/chrome/` provides custom layouts and widgets.
- **Translations:** `mods/cameo/fluent/` and `ContentPacks/*/translations/` hold Fluent localization files.
- **Tilesets:** `mods/cameo/tilesets/` defines the terrain tilesets used by Cameo maps.

All game assets remain the property of their respective owners and are used as fair-use educational reference material.

## 5. Upstream OpenRA features present but missing / not used in Cameo

The following OpenRA features documented in the OpenRA Knowledge Base Manual are either absent from the Cameo source or not inherited by the mod:

- **Official bundled mod source trees:** `mods/ra/`, `mods/cnc/`, `mods/d2k/`, and their campaign Lua infrastructure are not part of the Cameo mod (the engine still contains them, but Cameo does not use them).
- **Random map generator (RMG) layer:** Some newer `MapGenerator*` / `CellLayer*` / `RandomMapGenerator` classes in the upstream source are not obviously used by Cameo; the mod relies on the engine's existing RMG hooks.
- **Newer `OpenRA.Traits.Common` variants:** Cameo overrides several upstream traits with CA-specific copies (`*CA` classes), so the upstream behavior may be replaced rather than extended in those cases.

When the OpenRA manual and the Cameo manual conflict on a specific trait, the Cameo source is the authority for Cameo behavior; the OpenRA manual remains the authority for the engine baseline.

## 6. How to read the divergence inventory

- For a **high-level** summary, read this appendix.
- For the **full file-by-file and trait-by-trait inventory**, consult the Cameo source tree (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/` and `OpenRA.Mods.CA/`).
- For **engine fundamentals**, read the OpenRA Knowledge Base Manual v.5.
- For **Cameo-specific behavior**, read the corresponding chapter in this manual (e.g., Part 1 for traits/activities, Part 8 for bot modules, Part 4 for rendering/UI, Part 5 for audio).

## 7. References

- Cameo source tree (`OpenRA.Mods.Cameo/`, `OpenRA.Mods.CA/`) — complete custom code inventory.
- [OpenRA Knowledge Base Manual v.5](https://github.com/Renegade1993/OpenRA-Knowledge-Base-Manual) — upstream OpenRA engine and official mod documentation.
- Cameo source: `Cameo-mod` (main branch, 2026-07-24) — the authoritative source for all Cameo-specific behavior.

### See also

- `docs/DESIGN.md`
- `docs/design/FORMULA_V2.md` and `docs/design/ARMOR_SYSTEM.md`
- `docs/MIGRATION.md``mod.yaml` entries to self-contained ContentPacks, a major structural divergence from upstream OpenRA.
- `docs/audit/SUMMARY.md`

# Appendix M — Official Mod Actor Reference {#file-appendices-Appendix_M_Official_Actor_Reference}

## Purpose

This appendix consolidates, in one place, every **buildable actor** in the four mods that ship with OpenRA — *Red Alert*, *Tiberian Dawn*, *Dune 2000*, and *Tiberian Sun* — with its cameo, codename, faction, role, and core combat statistics. The goal is the thing that exists nowhere else: the sprite, the internal codename you write in YAML, and the numbers that define the unit, all next to each other, so a new modder can see at a glance what a unit *is* and what rules drive it.

This is engine-data reference, not balance commentary. Every value here is read directly from the mod's own rules YAML, so it always reflects the pinned engine rather than a hand-maintained copy that can drift.

> **Generated, not hand-written.** This appendix is produced by `build files/generate_actor_reference.py`, which parses each mod's `rules/*.yaml` (resolving `Inherits:` chains) and `fluent/rules.ftl` (for display names).

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Look up an official-mod actor by its internal codename or faction.
- Read the preview, cost, HP, armor, speed, sight, weapons, and notable traits columns for any actor.
- Use the actor tables when writing or debugging YAML rulesets, Lua scripts, or map actor definitions.

## How to read these tables

Each mod is split into **Infantry, Vehicles, Aircraft, Naval, and Buildings**. Columns:

- **Preview** — the build-palette cameo and the in-world battlefield sprite stacked in one cell. The cameo is the icon shown in the production sidebar; the unit is the idle/stand frame rendered with the same palette the engine uses in-game. (See the note on the images below.)
- **Code** — the actor's internal name; this is the key you use in `rules/*.yaml`, map actor definitions, and Lua (`Actor.Create("e1", ...)`).
- **Name** — the in-game display name, resolved from the mod's Fluent (`.ftl`) strings.
- **Faction** — derived from the build `Prerequisites`/`Queue` (e.g. `~vehicles.soviet`). A dash means shared or not faction-restricted.
- **Cost** — `Valued.Cost` (credits).
- **HP** — `Health.HP`, in raw engine health units (OpenRA's RA mod uses a ~100x scale, so `60000` is the classic "600").
- **Armor** — `Armor.Type` (matched against weapon `Versus` tables).
- **Speed** — `Mobile.Speed` (ground) or `Aircraft.Speed` (air), in engine units.
- **Sight** — `RevealsShroud.Range`, in cells (`WDist`, e.g. `6c0` = 6 cells).
- **Weapon(s)** — the weapon name(s) from each `Armament`; look these up in the mod's `weapons/*.yaml`.
- **Notable traits** — a curated set of standout abilities present on the actor (cloak, capture, deploy, support powers, self-heal, etc.).

> **About the images.** Each actor shows a **Preview** cell containing both the build-palette cameo (sidebar/construction-menu icon) and the in-world battlefield sprite. Both are rendered from the original game art, which lives only where you have installed the OpenRA game content — it is not in the engine source, so it cannot be bundled. Until the extraction script (below) is run on a machine with the content installed, the cell shows two labelled faction-tinted **placeholders** (the cameo box is grey; the unit box is blue-grey). A handful of actors have no art for one of the two slots (e.g. fake structures, or units with no separate sidebar icon) and keep its placeholder there. The manual is fully laid out and link-valid in the meantime.

> **A note on art.** OpenRA's own assets are openly licensed; the classic Westwood/EA unit art is distributed as freeware and remains its owners' property. Showing cameos in a free, non-commercial, educational reference is a fair-use use, not an open-license grant. Attribute the art to its owners and include a "not endorsed by or affiliated with EA" notice when publishing.

## Summary

This appendix is a single-source, auto-generated reference to every buildable actor in OpenRA's four bundled mods, pairing each unit's cameo and internal codename with its faction, role, and core statistics drawn straight from the engine's own rules. It lowers the barrier to entry for new modders by putting the sprite, the YAML codename, and the numbers in one place, and it stays accurate over time because it is regenerated from the pinned source rather than maintained by hand.

## What to read next

- [Part 2.4 — Rules and Weapons](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_04_Rules_Weapons) — how the actor and weapon YAML in these tables is defined.
- [Appendix H — Asset Visual Reference](#file-appendices-Appendix_H_Asset_Visual_Reference) — the file formats and engine classes behind cameos, sprites, and other assets.
- [Part 10.3 — Porting and Modding](#file-chapters-Part_10_Chapter_03_Port_And_Modding) — creating your own actor from scratch.

# Appendix N — Official Mod Terrain Tile Reference {#file-appendices-Appendix_N_Official_Terrain_Tile_Reference}

## Purpose

This appendix catalogs every terrain template in every official OpenRA mod tileset. Each row shows a rendered preview, the template ID, the source image file(s), the grid size, the primary terrain type, and notes about the template.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Identify the template ID, image source, and size for any official-mod terrain tile.
- Read the primary terrain type and mixed-terrain notes for a template.
- Use the tables when authoring maps, tilesets, or random-map generator configurations.

# Appendix O — Official Mod Environmental Actors {#file-appendices-Appendix_O_Official_Environmental_Actors}

## Purpose

This appendix catalogs the **environmental actors** in the four official OpenRA mods: *Red Alert (RA)*, *Tiberian Dawn (C&C)*, *Dune 2000 (D2K)*, and *Tiberian Sun (TS)*. Environmental actors are map-placed objects that are not produced by a player's factory or construction yard in the normal tech tree—things like trees, rocks, civilian buildings, bridges, walls, gates, crates, resource spawns, and decorative props. Some of them (sandbags, concrete walls, gates) can also be built by players once the right prerequisites are met, but they still behave as world objects rather than as units.

They differ from buildable combat actors in a few key ways:

* Most inherit from templates such as `^Tree`, `^Rock`, `^CivBuilding`, `^Bridge`, `^Wall`, or `^Crate` rather than from `^Building` or `^Vehicle`.
* They are usually owned by `Neutral` (or `Creeps` for hostile wildlife) and placed in the map editor.
* They typically use `Building` for footprint, `Interactable` for selection bounds, `Tooltip` for display names, and `MapEditorData` for editor categorization.
* Many are invulnerable or have very high health, and some have special death behavior such as `SpawnActorOnDeath`, `FireWarheadsOnDeath`, `SeedsResource`, or `CashTrickler`.

The tables use the YAML data as it appears in the rules files. "Name/Tooltip" shows the in-game display name resolved from the mod's Fluent translation files. "Size" combines the `Dimensions` and `Footprint` values from the `Building` trait. "Key Traits" highlights the most important behavior traits. A "—" means the field is not explicitly set on that actor or its inherited template.

> **Generated, not hand-written.** This appendix is produced by `build files/generate_environmental_actor_reference.py`, which parses each mod's `rules/*.yaml` (resolving `Inherits:` chains) and `fluent/rules.ftl` (for display names). The preview column shows labelled placeholders by default; run `build files/extract_environmental_images.py` after installing the game content to render real sprites with the OpenRA Utility's `--export-sequence-frame` command.

> **A note on art.** OpenRA's own assets are openly licensed; the classic Westwood/EA unit art is distributed as freeware and remains its owners' property. Showing previews in a free, non-commercial, educational reference is a fair-use use, not an open-license grant. Attribute the art to its owners and include a "not endorsed by or affiliated with EA" notice when publishing.

## Learning Objectives

After studying this appendix, you should be able to:

- Identify the official-mod environmental actors by mod, category, and internal codename.
- Read the size, key traits, and placement notes for each actor.
- Cross-reference environmental actors with the official terrain tile reference and the Cameo-specific environmental appendix.

> Cross-references: [Part 1.1 — ECS](#file-chapters-Part_01_Chapter_01_ECS), [Part 2.4 — Rulesets, Actors, and Weapons](#file-chapters-Part_02_Chapter_04_Rules_Weapons), [Part 7.7 — RMG Resources and Actors](#file-chapters-Part_07_Chapter_07_Resources_Actors), [Part 10.1 — Official Mods](#file-chapters-Part_10_Chapter_01_Official_Mods), [Appendix N — Official Mod Terrain Tile Reference](#file-appendices-Appendix_N_Official_Terrain_Tile_Reference)

## Summary

This appendix is a single-source, auto-generated reference to the environmental actors in OpenRA's four bundled mods. It pairs each object's internal codename with its editor category, footprint, key traits, and a preview slot, all drawn from the engine's own rules so the reference stays in sync with the pinned source.

# Appendix P — Cameo Faction Actor Visual Reference {#file-appendices-Appendix_P_Cameo_Faction_Actor_Visual_Reference}

## Purpose

This appendix provides a visual catalog of every buildable actor in the active Cameo factions. Each entry shows the build-palette cameo and, where available, the in-world battlefield sprite or voxel render produced directly from the Cameo mod assets.

> **Generated reference.** This appendix is produced by `build files/generate_cameo_actor_appendix.py` from `cameo_actor_manifest.json`, which in turn is built by the OpenRA utility `--dump-actor-manifest` command and the active Cameo rules/sequences.

## How to read these tables

* **Preview** — cameo icon and in-world render side by side.
* **Code** — internal actor key used in `rules/*.yaml`, map definitions, and Lua.
* **Name** — display name from the actor's tooltip definition.
* **Category** — infantry, vehicle, aircraft, building, or other.
* **Render** — whether the battlefield render is a sprite (`sprite`) or a voxel model (`voxel`).

## Learning Objectives

After reading this appendix you should be able to:

- Identify the internal actor key and display name for any buildable Cameo faction unit or structure.
- Recognize the build-palette cameo and the corresponding in-world sprite or voxel render.
- Group actors by faction and category when comparing units across the active source factions.

## Summary

This appendix covers only the active (non-random) factions defined in the Cameo mod `mod.yaml`. Shared actors may appear in multiple faction tables because they are buildable by every faction in that source file. The renders were generated from the live Cameo ruleset and sequence definitions, so the preview images stay in sync with the pinned source.
